conflictos/actium.batallas.batalla-de-ac.t: Agrippa destroys the fleet of Antony and Cleopatra.

conflictos/actium.batallas.toma-de-aleja.t: Suicide of Antony and Cleopatra; Egypt becomes a Roman province.

conflictos/actium.descripcion.t: Octavian defeats Mark Antony and Cleopatra; Egypt is annexed and the Empire is born under Augustus.

conflictos/actium.nombre.t: Final War of the Roman Republic

conflictos/alejandro.batallas.batalla-de.t: Decisive victory that opens the heart of Persia to Alexander.
First defeat of Darius III in person.
Alexander's first victory over the Persian satraps in Asia Minor.
Alexander defeats King Porus by the present-day Jhelum River.

conflictos/alejandro.descripcion.t: In eleven years Alexander conquers the Persian Empire and reaches the Indus.

conflictos/an-lushan.bajas.t: Highly disputed: the census falls from 52.9 to 16.9 million (755–764), but historians largely attribute this to the collapse of registration; death estimates range from ~13 million to much lower figures

conflictos/an-lushan.batallas.caida-de-c.t: Emperor Xuanzong flees; his guard executes the concubine Yang Guifei.

conflictos/an-lushan.batallas.sitio-de-s.t: Desperate resistance that saves southern China.

conflictos/an-lushan.descripcion.t: General An Lushan rises against the Tang and takes both capitals; the dynasty survives but is broken for ever.

conflictos/anglo-espanola-1625.batallas..t: Cecil's expedition re-embarks in defeat; the city holds out.

conflictos/anglo-espanola-1625.descripci.t: Charles I of England attacks Cádiz with a large expedition that fails resoundingly; the war ends in a stalemate with the Peace of Madrid.

conflictos/anglo-espanola-1655.batallas..t: Blake destroys the anchored Indies fleet, although the silver was already ashore.
Attack on Santa Cruz de Tenerife
Penn and Venables occupy the island, the base of future English power in the Caribbean.

conflictos/anglo-espanola-1655.descripci.t: Cromwell's «Western Design»: England attacks the Spanish Caribbean, fails in Hispaniola but takes Jamaica, and its fleet strikes the Indies convoys.

conflictos/anglo-espanola-1796.batallas..t: Jervis and Nelson defeat the Spanish fleet.
General Gutiérrez repels Nelson, who loses his right arm.
Battle of Santa Cruz de Tenerife

conflictos/anglo-espanola-1796.descripci.t: Spain, allied with Revolutionary France, faces the Royal Navy: defeat at Cape St. Vincent, victory at Tenerife (Nelson loses his arm) and blockade of Cádiz.

conflictos/anglo-espanola-1796.zonas.atl.t: Iberian Atlantic and the Canary Islands

conflictos/anglo-espanola.batallas.batal.t: Battle of the Gulf of Almería
Naval battle of the Gulf of Cádiz

conflictos/anglo-espanola.batallas.la-ar.t: ~15,000 Spanish dead, almost all from shipwrecks
Philip II's great fleet fails in its attempt to invade England.

conflictos/anglo-espanola.descripcion.t: Naval conflict between Philip II and Elizabeth I.

conflictos/anglo-zulu.batallas.batalla-d.t: The worst British defeat at the hands of an indigenous army.

conflictos/anglo-zulu.batallas.defensa-d.t: 150 soldiers hold out against 4,000 Zulus; eleven Victoria Crosses.

conflictos/anglo-zulu.descripcion.t: The Empire invades Zululand: the Zulu spear crushes the redcoats at Isandlwana, but Cetshwayo's kingdom falls within six months.

conflictos/ano-cuatro-emperadores.bajas.t: tens of thousands (two battles of Bedriacum and sackings)

conflictos/ano-cuatro-emperadores.batall.t: The Vitellians defeat Otho, who commits suicide.
Vespasian's Flavians defeat Vitellius near Cremona.

conflictos/ano-cuatro-emperadores.descri.t: Civil war after the fall of Nero: Galba, Otho, Vitellius and Vespasian contend for the throne in little more than a year. It is decided in the Po valley, where Vespasian defeats Vitellius and founds the Flavian dynasty.

conflictos/ano-cuatro-emperadores.zonas..t: Civil war in the Po Valley

conflictos/arabe-israeli-1948.descripcio.t: When the State of Israel is proclaimed on 14 May 1948, the armies of Egypt, Transjordan, Syria, Lebanon and Iraq invade the former British Mandate of Palestine. After successive truces, Israel extends the borders of the UN partition plan and signs armistices in Rhodes in 1949; the Palestinian exodus (the Nakba) displaces some 700,000 Arabs.

conflictos/arabe-israeli-1948.zonas.fren.t: Southern front: Egyptian advance and the Faluja Pocket

conflictos/asedio-constantinopla-717.baj.t: tens of thousands, above all among the besiegers

conflictos/asedio-constantinopla-717.des.t: Leo III and the Bulgar khan Tervel repel Maslama's great Umayyad assault by land and sea; it marks the end of the caliphal attempts to take Constantinople.

conflictos/asiento.batallas.sitio-de-car.t: ~9,500–11,500 British dead (mostly from disease) versus ~800 Spanish
Blas de Lezo, with ~3,500 men and 6 ships of the line, defeats Vernon's ~27,000 men and 124 ships: one of Spain's greatest naval victories.

conflictos/asiento.batallas.toma-de-port.t: Vernon destroys Panama's gold port; euphoria in London.

conflictos/asiento.descripcion.t: Great Britain launches against Spanish America the largest fleet seen until then; the disaster before Cartagena de Indias (1741) against Blas de Lezo keeps the Spanish empire intact for another half century.

conflictos/asiento.nombre.t: War of the Asiento (War of Jenkins' Ear)

conflictos/atila.batallas.batalla-de-los.t: Aetius and the Visigoths of Theodoric I halt Attila in Gaul. Exact location disputed (between Châlons-en-Champagne and Troyes).

conflictos/atila.batallas.saqueo-de-aqui.t: Attila destroys Aquileia; its refugees will found Venice.

conflictos/atila.batallas.saqueo-de-nais.t: The Huns raze the Balkan city with siege towers.

conflictos/atila.descripcion.t: Attila devastates the Balkans, Gaul and Italy; his empire crumbles on his death in 453.

conflictos/batalla-ankara-1402.descripci.t: Timur invades Anatolia and captures Sultan Bayezid I at Çubuk, near Ankara. The defeat opens the 'Ottoman Interregnum' (1402–1413), a civil war among Bayezid's sons that almost destroys the young empire.

conflictos/batalla-ankara-1402.nombre.t: Battle of Ankara and Ottoman collapse

conflictos/boer.bajas.t: ~75,000 dead, including ~28,000 Boer civilians in concentration camps

conflictos/boer.batallas.liberacion-de-m.t: End of the 217-day siege defended by Baden-Powell.

conflictos/boer.descripcion.t: The gold of the Transvaal pits the Empire against the Boer republics: guerrilla warfare, scorched earth and the first modern concentration camps.

conflictos/britania.descripcion.t: Claudius invades in 43; Boudica's revolt razes Londinium (60–61); Wales falls around 77 and Agricola wins at Mons Graupius (84).

conflictos/bulgaro-bizantinas.bajas.t: tens of thousands; end of the First Bulgarian Empire

conflictos/bulgaro-bizantinas.batallas.b.t: Basil II annihilates the Bulgarian army and blinds the prisoners.
Samuel defeats Basil II in his first campaign.
Battle of the Gates of Trajan

conflictos/bulgaro-bizantinas.descripcio.t: Basil II 'the Bulgar-Slayer' wages four decades of war against Samuel's empire. After the Bulgarian annihilation at Kleidion (1014), Bulgaria is fully annexed in 1018.

conflictos/caida-de-asiria.batallas.bata.t: Nebuchadnezzar defeats Pharaoh Necho II: end of Egyptian influence in the Levant.

conflictos/caida-de-asiria.batallas.caid.t: After a three-month siege, the Medes of Cyaxares and the Babylonians of Nabopolassar sack the Assyrian capital.

conflictos/caida-de-asiria.descripcion.t: Babylonians and Medes destroy Assyria: Nineveh falls (612) and at Carchemish (605) Nebuchadnezzar defeats the Egyptians and Assyrian remnants and takes Syria and the Levant.

conflictos/caida-occidente.bajas.t: unknown (hundreds of thousands over a century)

conflictos/caida-occidente.batallas.bata.t: The Goths annihilate the Eastern army.

conflictos/caida-occidente.batallas.depo.t: Odoacer deposes the last Western emperor in Ravenna.

conflictos/caida-occidente.batallas.saqu.t: First sack of Rome in 800 years; shock throughout the empire.
The Vandals sack the city for two weeks.

conflictos/caida-occidente.descripcion.t: From Adrianople (378) to the deposition of Romulus Augustulus (476): the Germanic peoples cross the frontiers, sack Rome twice and divide the West among themselves.

conflictos/caida-occidente.nombre.t: Germanic invasions and the fall of the West

conflictos/caida-occidente.zonas.cruce-d.t: Crossing of the Rhine (Vandals, Suebi and Alans)

conflictos/campanas-filipo-ii.batallas.b.t: Philip II and the young Alexander defeat the Athenians and Thebans.

conflictos/campanas-filipo-ii.descripcio.t: Philip II defeats the coalition of Athens and Thebes at Chaeronea; with the League of Corinth (337 BC) Macedon becomes the hegemonic power of Greece, the basis for Alexander's expedition.

conflictos/campanas-germania-augusto.baj.t: 16,000–20,000 Romans dead in the Teutoburg Forest alone

conflictos/campanas-germania-augusto.bat.t: Arminius annihilates Varus's three legions (probably at Kalkriese).

conflictos/campanas-germania-augusto.des.t: Drusus, Tiberius and Germanicus try to push the frontier from the Rhine to the Elbe. Arminius's ambush in the Teutoburg Forest (AD 9) destroys Varus's three legions and halts the expansion; after Germanicus's punitive campaigns (AD 16) the Rhine remains the frontier.

conflictos/campanas-germania-augusto.zon.t: Germania between the Rhine and the Elbe

conflictos/carlistas.batallas.abrazo-de-.t: Espartero and Maroto seal the peace of the first war.

conflictos/carlistas.batallas.batalla-de.t: Espartero breaks the Carlist siege of Bilbao on Christmas Eve.
Carlist victory in the third war.

conflictos/carlistas.descripcion.t: Three civil wars between Liberals and Carlists over the succession and the model of the country, with the foral north as the Carlist stronghold.

conflictos/chu-han.batallas.batalla-de-g.t: Liu Bang defeats Xiang Yu and founds the Han dynasty. Located in Guzhen County (Anhui); alternative locations in Lingbi and Luyi are debated.

conflictos/chu-han.descripcion.t: After the collapse of Qin, Xiang Yu, Hegemon of Chu, and Liu Bang, King of Han, fight for control of the empire. Liu Bang definitively defeats Xiang Yu in 202 BC and founds the Han dynasty as Emperor Gaozu.

conflictos/chu-han.zonas.frente-entre-ch.t: Front between Chu and Han in central China

conflictos/cienanos.batallas.batalla-de-.t: Henry V wins despite enormous numerical inferiority.
Last battle: the French artillery drives England off the Continent.
The English archers crush the French cavalry.

conflictos/cienanos.batallas.batalla-nav.t: Edward III's fleet destroys the French fleet off Sluys (24 June 1340).

conflictos/cienanos.batallas.liberacion-.t: Joan of Arc lifts the siege and changes the course of the war.

conflictos/cienanos.descripcion.t: Long dynastic struggle for the crown of France.

conflictos/cienanos.zonas.campanas-de-en.t: Campaigns of Henry V and Joan of Arc

conflictos/colonizacion-brasil.bajas.t: tens of thousands in combat; many more from epidemics and slavery

conflictos/colonizacion-brasil.batallas..t: Luso-Brazilian victories that decide the expulsion of the Dutch.
Mem de Sá puts an end to France Antarctique and founds São Sebastião do Rio de Janeiro.
Expulsion of the French from Rio

conflictos/colonizacion-brasil.descripci.t: From the brazilwood of the coastal trading posts (1500–1533) to the hereditary captaincies (1534), the general government at Salvador (1549), the expulsion of the French from Rio (1567), the bandeiras into the interior and the war against Dutch Brazil in Pernambuco (1630–1654).

conflictos/colonizacion-brasil.zonas.bah.t: Bahia and the general government of Salvador

conflictos/colonizacion-brasil.zonas.sao.t: São Paulo and bandeiras into the interior

conflictos/comunidades.batallas.batalla-.t: The comuneros are defeated; their leaders are beheaded the following day.

conflictos/comunidades.descripcion.t: The Castilian cities rise up against the young Charles I; the defeat at Villalar and the execution of Padilla, Bravo and Maldonado end the revolt.

conflictos/conflicto-israel-hezbola.baja.t: ~4,000–5,000 militiamen and ~130 Israelis dead; 1.4 million Lebanese displaced

conflictos/conflicto-israel-hezbola.bata.t: Thousands of Hezbollah pagers and walkie-talkies detonate simultaneously.
Israeli bombing of Hezbollah's headquarters in Beirut, 27 September.

conflictos/conflicto-israel-hezbola.desc.t: A year of cross-border fire escalates in September 2024: the pager attack, the killing of Nasrallah and the Israeli invasion of southern Lebanon; ceasefire on 27 November 2024.

conflictos/conquista-america.bajas.t: hundreds of thousands in combat; millions counting epidemics (smallpox, measles, typhus)

conflictos/conquista-america.batallas.ba.t: Cortés's first battle in Mexica lands; he receives La Malinche.
Cortés defeats the Mexica army in open field after the Noche Triste.

conflictos/conquista-america.batallas.ca.t: After months of siege the Mexica capital falls; Cuauhtémoc is captured.

conflictos/conquista-america.batallas.em.t: Capture of Atahualpa without Spanish casualties.

conflictos/conquista-america.batallas.la.t: The Spaniards flee Tenochtitlan with heavy losses.

conflictos/conquista-america.batallas.si.t: The great Inca rebellion comes close to retaking the city.

conflictos/conquista-america.descripcion.t: In less than a century, starting from the Antilles, Spain subdues the Mexica and Inca empires and founds the viceroyalties of New Spain and Peru. The advance came in waves: the Caribbean (1492–1519), Mexico (1519–1521), Central America and Yucatán (1524–1547), Peru (1532–1536), New Granada and Venezuela (1525–1546), Chile and the Río de la Plata (1536–1580).

conflictos/conquista-america.zonas.expan.t: Expansion across New Spain (west and north)

conflictos/conquista-america.zonas.rio-d.t: Río de la Plata and Paraguay

conflictos/conquista-danesa-inglaterra.b.t: Cnut defeats Edmund Ironside in Essex and is crowned King of England.

conflictos/conquista-danesa-inglaterra.d.t: Sweyn Forkbeard takes England in 1013; his son Cnut reconquers it in 1016 (Assandun) and integrates it into the North Sea Empire together with Denmark and Norway. Danish rule lasts until the death of Harthacnut (1042).

conflictos/conquista-grecia.batallas.bat.t: The legion proves its superiority over the phalanx.
End of the Kingdom of Macedon.

conflictos/conquista-grecia.descripcion.t: Four Macedonian Wars and the Achaean War put an end to Hellenistic Greece: in 146 BC Corinth is sacked and Greece comes under Roman rule.

conflictos/conquista-grecia.nombre.t: Macedonian Wars and the conquest of Greece

conflictos/conquista-hispania.batallas.b.t: Victory of Pelagius, the symbolic beginning of the Reconquista.
Defeat and death of the Visigothic king Roderic.

conflictos/conquista-hispania.descripcio.t: Tariq and Musa conquer the Visigothic Kingdom in a few years; al-Andalus is born.

conflictos/conquista-hispania.zonas.anda.t: Andalusia and the march on Toledo

conflictos/conquista-otomana-mamelucos.d.t: Selim I crushes the Mamluk Sultanate: he wins at Marj Dabiq (1516), taking Syria, and at Ridaniya (1517), conquering Cairo. Egypt, Syria and the Hejaz pass to the empire, which assumes custody of the Holy Places of Islam.

conflictos/conquista-otomana-mamelucos.n.t: Ottoman conquest of the Mamluk Sultanate

conflictos/conquista-zhou-de-shang.batal.t: End of the Shang dynasty. Marker at Xinxiang (Muye district), in northern Henan: the exact location of the battlefield is unknown.

conflictos/conquista-zhou-de-shang.descr.t: King Wu of Zhou and his allies defeat the last Shang king, Di Xin, at Muye, take the capital Yin and found the Zhou dynasty (approximate date: around 1046 BC).

conflictos/conquistas-arabes.bajas.t: tens of thousands; collapse of Persia and Byzantine loss of Syria and Egypt

conflictos/conquistas-arabes.batallas.ba.t: Last organized Persian resistance; the 'victory of victories'.
Decisive Byzantine defeat; Syria is lost.

conflictos/conquistas-arabes.descripcion.t: After the death of Muhammad, the Rashidun caliphs overwhelm the two great powers: they defeat Byzantium at Yarmouk (636) and take Syria and Egypt from it, and they annihilate the Sasanian Empire at al-Qadisiyyah (637) and Nahavand (642).

conflictos/conquistas-de-sargon.descripc.t: Sargon subdues the Sumerian cities and extends his rule as far as Syria and Elam: the first empire in history is born (dates according to the middle chronology).

conflictos/conquistas-timur.bajas.t: very high; the overall figures in circulation are highly disputed

conflictos/conquistas-timur.batallas.bat.t: Timur defeats Tokhtamysh, khan of the Golden Horde, in the North Caucasus.

conflictos/conquistas-timur.batallas.saq.t: After a forty-day siege, Timur takes and razes Baghdad.
Timur defeats the Sultan of Delhi and sacks the city (17–20 December 1398).

conflictos/conquistas-timur.descripcion.t: From Samarkand, Timur builds an empire stretching from the Caucasus to India: he defeats Tokhtamysh (1395), sacks Delhi (1398) and Baghdad (1401), and captures Sultan Bayezid at Ankara (1402).

conflictos/constantinopla.batallas.caida.t: Mehmed II takes the city after a 53-day siege; Constantine XI is killed.

conflictos/constantinopla.descripcion.t: End of the Byzantine Empire and, for many historians, of the medieval world.

conflictos/crimea-y-donbas.batallas.bata.t: Last major battle before the Minsk II ceasefire.
Encirclement and defeat of the Ukrainian army that consolidated the separatists.
Months of defence by the Ukrainian “cyborgs” until the terminal fell.

conflictos/crimea-y-donbas.descripcion.t: Russia annexes Crimea after the Euromaidan and backs the separatists of Donetsk and Luhansk; the Minsk agreements freeze a front that erupts in 2022.

conflictos/crimea-y-donbas.nombre.t: Annexation of Crimea and war in Donbas

conflictos/crimea.batallas.batalla-de-ba.t: The Charge of the Light Brigade, immortalized by Tennyson.

conflictos/crimea.batallas.sitio-de-seba.t: Eleven months of siege decide the war.

conflictos/crimea.descripcion.t: The Western powers halt Russian expansion at the expense of the Ottoman Empire; the war of the Charge of the Light Brigade and of Florence Nightingale.

conflictos/crisis-siglo-iii-inicio.batal.t: Maximinus Thrax dies before the walls of Aquileia at the hands of his own troops.

conflictos/crisis-siglo-iii-inicio.descr.t: The death of Severus Alexander and the proclamation of Maximinus Thrax open the military anarchy: the armies make and unmake emperors. It culminates in the Year of the Six Emperors (238), with the siege of Aquileia and the death of Maximinus.

conflictos/crisis-siglo-iii-inicio.nombr.t: Crisis of the Third Century (onset: military anarchy)

conflictos/crisis-siglo-iii-inicio.zonas.t: War between Maximinus and the Senate (northern Italy)

conflictos/crisis-siglo-iii.bajas.t: unknown (hundreds of thousands, including the Plague of Cyprian)

conflictos/crisis-siglo-iii.batallas.bat.t: Shapur I defeats and captures Emperor Valerian, the first Roman emperor taken prisoner. Coordinates of the city (Şanlıurfa): the battle was fought between Carrhae and Edessa.

conflictos/crisis-siglo-iii.descripcion.t: After 238 the Empire suffers continual usurpations, Germanic invasions and the Sasanian offensive: Shapur I captures Valerian at Edessa (260) and the Empire splits into three (the Gallic Empire, Palmyra and the Italian core) until Aurelian reunifies it (273–274). Diocletian brings the crisis to an end in 284.

conflictos/crisis-siglo-iii.nombre.t: Crisis of the Third Century (military anarchy and invasions)

conflictos/cruzada-albigense.batallas.ba.t: Simon de Montfort defeats Peter II of Aragon, who is killed in the fighting (12 September 1213).

conflictos/cruzada-albigense.batallas.sa.t: Massacre of the population on 22 July 1209 (coordinates of the city).

conflictos/cruzada-albigense.batallas.si.t: Siege of 1217–1218 in which Simon de Montfort is killed (coordinates of the city).

conflictos/cruzada-albigense.descripcion.t: Crusade against the Cathars of Languedoc; at Muret (1213) Peter II of Aragon is killed and southern France ends up integrated into the French crown, which halts Aragonese expansion north of the Pyrenees.

conflictos/cruzadas.batallas.batalla-de-.t: Saladin annihilates the crusader army and recovers Jerusalem.

conflictos/cruzadas.batallas.caida-de-ac.t: The Mamluks take the last major crusader stronghold in the Holy Land (18 May 1291).

conflictos/cruzadas.batallas.toma-de-jer.t: The First Crusade culminates in the assault on the city.

conflictos/cruzadas.descripcion.t: Christian military expeditions to the Holy Land; the Crusader States are founded and lost.

conflictos/cuadruple-alianza.batallas.ba.t: The British fleet destroys the Spanish fleet in a surprise attack without a declaration of war.

conflictos/cuadruple-alianza.descripcion.t: Philip V tries to recover Sicily and Sardinia after Utrecht; half of Europe forms a coalition against him.

conflictos/dacia.batallas.batalla-de-tap.t: Trajan opens the way to the Dacian capital.

conflictos/dacia.batallas.caida-de-sarmi.t: Decebalus commits suicide; Dacia becomes a Roman province.

conflictos/dacia.descripcion.t: Trajan conquers the Dacia of Decebalus; Dacian gold finances Trajan's Forum, and his column narrates the campaign. The empire reaches its greatest extent.

conflictos/dieciseis-reinos.batallas.bat.t: The Eastern Jin halt the invasion by Fu Jian's Former Qin and consolidate the division between north and south. The Fei River no longer exists; the marker is in Shou County (Anhui), where the battle was fought.

conflictos/dieciseis-reinos.descripcion.t: Northern China fragments into states ruled by Xiongnu, Xianbei, Di and Qiang dynasties while the Jin take refuge in the south. Fu Jian's Former Qin unifies the north, but its defeat at the Fei River (383) brings it down; the Northern Wei reunify the north in 439.

conflictos/dinastias-norte-sur.descripci.t: After the fall of the Jin, China is divided between the Northern dynasties (often of steppe origin) and the Southern dynasties (Han heirs with their capital at Jiankang/Nanjing). At the Battle of the Fei River (383) the Eastern Jin halt the invasion by the Former Qin, consolidating the division until the Sui reunification.

conflictos/dos-rosas.descripcion.t: Dynastic civil war between the houses of Lancaster (red rose) and York (white rose) for the English throne. It ends when Henry Tudor defeats and kills Richard III at Bosworth (1485), founds the Tudor dynasty and crushes the last Yorkist resistance at Stoke Field (1487).

conflictos/expansion-aquemenida.batallas.t: Cambyses II defeats Psamtik III and conquers Egypt.
Cyrus defeats Croesus and conquers Lydia and its legendary treasure.
The great city falls almost without a fight; Cyrus frees the Jews from exile.

conflictos/expansion-aquemenida.descripc.t: Cyrus the Great subdues Media (550 BC), Lydia (546) and Babylon (539); Cambyses conquers Egypt (525) and Darius reaches Thrace and the Indus: the largest empire of the ancient world.

conflictos/expansion-neoasiria.batallas..t: Shalmaneser III against a coalition of Syrian, Aramean and Israelite kings; the battle with the most combatants documented up to that time. Coordinates of Tell Qarqur.
Ashurbanipal sacks the capital of Elam (around 647 BC).

conflictos/expansion-neoasiria.descripci.t: Assyria becomes the largest empire known up to that time (~1.4 million km² around 670 BC): it subdues Syria, the Levant, Babylon and, in 671, Egypt.

conflictos/expansion-otomana-balcanes.de.t: From the Battle of Bapheus against Byzantium, the Ottomans cross into Europe and subdue the Balkans: they defeat the Serbs at Kosovo (1389, where Murad I is killed) and crush the crusades of Nicopolis (1396) and Varna (1444), consolidating Rumelia as the European core of the empire.

conflictos/franco-prusiana.batallas.bata.t: Napoleon III is captured along with his army.

conflictos/franco-prusiana.batallas.siti.t: Four months of siege; Paris capitulates on 28 January 1871, days after the German Empire is proclaimed at Versailles.

conflictos/franco-prusiana.descripcion.t: The Prussian victory brings about German unification and the fall of Napoleon III.

conflictos/franco-visigoda.batallas.bata.t: Clovis kills Alaric II; the Visigoths lose Gaul.

conflictos/franco-visigoda.descripcion.t: Clovis, already converted to Catholicism, attacks the Arian Visigoths of Alaric II. At Vouillé (507) he kills Alaric and drives the Visigoths out of almost all of Gaul, pushing them towards Hispania.

conflictos/galias.batallas.sitio-de-ales.t: Vercingetorix surrenders to Caesar after the double encirclement.

conflictos/galias.descripcion.t: Julius Caesar subdues Gaul; his chronicle is 'De bello Gallico'.

conflictos/genocidio-ruanda.bajas.t: ~800,000 Tutsis and moderate Hutus murdered in a hundred days

conflictos/genocidio-ruanda.batallas.tom.t: The RPF enters the capital on 4 July and puts an end to the genocide.

conflictos/genocidio-ruanda.descripcion.t: After the presidential plane is shot down, the Hutu authorities organize the extermination of the Tutsis; Kagame's Rwandan Patriotic Front takes the country and stops the killing.

conflictos/genpei.batallas.batalla-de-da.t: The Taira fleet is annihilated; the child emperor Antoku drowns.

conflictos/genpei.batallas.batalla-de-ku.t: Decisive Minamoto victory in the north.

conflictos/genpei.descripcion.t: The war between the Minamoto and Taira clans ends at Dan-no-ura and gives rise to the first shogunate: seven centuries of samurai rule.

conflictos/genpei.zonas.honshu-occidenta.t: Western Honshu and the Inland Sea

conflictos/gran-guerra-del-norte.batalla.t: First major Russian naval victory, in Riilahti Bay, north of the Hanko Peninsula (marker at Hanko; approximate position).
Charles XII defeats a far larger Russian army (30 November 1700).
Peter I annihilates the Swedish army; end of Swedish hegemony.

conflictos/gran-guerra-del-norte.descrip.t: A coalition led by Peter I's Russia defeats Charles XII's Sweden; with the Peace of Nystad (1721) Russia gains Estonia, Livonia and Ingria and proclaims itself an empire.

conflictos/gran-guerra-teutonica.bajas.t: tens of thousands; Grand Master Ulrich von Jungingen is killed

conflictos/gran-guerra-teutonica.batalla.t: Jogaila and Vytautas defeat the Teutonic Order (15 July 1410).
The victors of Grunwald fail to take the Order's capital (July–September 1410).

conflictos/gran-guerra-teutonica.descrip.t: Poland and Lithuania, united under the Jagiellonians, defeat the Teutonic Order at Grunwald (Tannenberg), one of the largest battles of medieval Europe.

conflictos/gran-guerra-turca.batallas.ba.t: Prince Eugene of Savoy destroys the Ottoman army as it crosses the Tisza.

conflictos/gran-guerra-turca.batallas.se.t: Decisive Ottoman defeat near Mount Harsány (12 August 1687; coordinates of Nagyharsány).

conflictos/gran-guerra-turca.batallas.si.t: John III Sobieski breaks the Ottoman siege from the Kahlenberg (12 September 1683).

conflictos/gran-guerra-turca.descripcion.t: After the Ottoman failure before Vienna, the Holy League reconquers Hungary; the Peace of Karlowitz marks the first major Ottoman territorial loss in Europe.

conflictos/gran-guerra-turca.nombre.t: Great Turkish War (War of the Holy League)

conflictos/granada-guerra.batallas.toma-.t: Boabdil hands over the keys of the city on 2 January 1492.

conflictos/granada-guerra.descripcion.t: The Catholic Monarchs conquer the last Muslim kingdom of the peninsula.

conflictos/guerra-1812.batallas.batalla-.t: Jackson crushes the British assault two weeks after the peace was signed.

conflictos/guerra-1812.batallas.batallas.t: Battles of Emuckfaw and Enotachopo Creek

conflictos/guerra-1812.batallas.quema-de.t: The British set fire to the Capitol and the White House.

conflictos/guerra-1812.descripcion.t: The US invades Canada without success; the British burn Washington (1814); the last battle, New Orleans, is fought after the peace has already been signed.

conflictos/guerra-1812.zonas.frontera-de.t: Canadian border and the Great Lakes

conflictos/guerra-afganistan.batallas.ba.t: Offensive against the al-Qaeda tunnels; Bin Laden escapes to Pakistan.

conflictos/guerra-afganistan.batallas.ca.t: The Taliban enter the capital on 15 August; chaotic evacuation from the airport.

conflictos/guerra-afganistan.batallas.op.t: The largest allied offensive of the war, in the Taliban stronghold of Helmand.

conflictos/guerra-afganistan.descripcion.t: After 9/11, the US overthrows the Taliban regime; twenty years of insurgency end with the Western withdrawal and the Taliban's return in 2021.

conflictos/guerra-afgano-sovietica.batal.t: Nine Soviet offensives against Ahmad Shah Massoud in the Panjshir Valley (1980–1985); coordinates of the valley.

conflictos/guerra-afgano-sovietica.descr.t: The USSR invades Afghanistan to prop up the communist regime; the mujahideen, backed by the US, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, force it to withdraw in 1989.

conflictos/guerra-africa.batallas.batall.t: Prim and the Catalan volunteers decide the capture of the city.

conflictos/guerra-africa.descripcion.t: The campaign of O'Donnell and Prim in Morocco, celebrated as a national feat; Spain takes Tetouan.

conflictos/guerra-argelia.bajas.t: between ~300,000 and more than 1,000,000 Algerian dead depending on the source (disputed); ~25,000 French soldiers

conflictos/guerra-argelia.descripcion.t: The FLN, which launches the insurrection with the «Toussaint Rouge» attacks (1 November 1954, mainly in the Aurès), fights against French Algeria; the 1958 crisis returns De Gaulle to power and the Évian Accords lead to independence (5 July 1962).

conflictos/guerra-austro-prusiana.descri.t: Prussia expels Austria from German affairs; the North German Confederation is born and Italy gains Venetia.

conflictos/guerra-barones.descripcion.t: Rebellion of the barons led by Simon de Montfort against Henry III in defence of the Provisions of Oxford. Montfort wins at Lewes (1264) and summons a representative parliament, but is defeated and killed at Evesham (1265).

conflictos/guerra-boshin.batallas.batall.t: Surrender of the Republic of Ezo, the last pro-Tokugawa stronghold.
Imperial victory south of Kyoto that marks the end of the bakufu.

conflictos/guerra-boshin.descripcion.t: Civil war that topples the Tokugawa shogunate and restores Emperor Meiji. From the Battle of Toba–Fushimi (1868) to the fall of the short-lived Republic of Ezo at Hakodate (1869).

conflictos/guerra-boshin.zonas.avance-im.t: Imperial advance through Honshu to the north

conflictos/guerra-chaco.batallas.batalla.t: First major battle of the war (9–29 September 1932), won by Paraguay.

conflictos/guerra-chaco.descripcion.t: Bolivia and Paraguay fight over the Chaco Boreal; Paraguay gains most of the territory (1938 treaty).

conflictos/guerra-chino-india.batallas.b.t: Fighting at Sela Pass during the Chinese offensive of November.

conflictos/guerra-chino-india.descripcio.t: Border war in the Himalayas (Aksai Chin and NEFA/Arunachal); Chinese victory and unilateral ceasefire.

conflictos/guerra-civil-castellana.batal.t: Defeat of Peter I, who dies days later at the hands of his half-brother (coordinates of the town).
The Black Prince and Peter I defeat Henry of Trastámara and Du Guesclin (3 April 1367).

conflictos/guerra-civil-castellana.descr.t: Peter I the Cruel, supported by the Black Prince, fights his half-brother Henry of Trastámara, supported by France and Du Guesclin; Peter dies at Montiel and the Trastámara dynasty begins.

conflictos/guerra-civil-cesar.bajas.t: tens of thousands (6,000–15,000 Pompeians killed at Pharsalus alone)

conflictos/guerra-civil-cesar.batallas.b.t: Caesar defeats Pompey, who flees to Egypt and is assassinated.
Caesar's last victory over the sons of Pompey; the exact site is disputed (probably near La Lantejuela).

conflictos/guerra-civil-cesar.descripcio.t: Caesar crosses the Rubicon and confronts Pompey and the Senate's optimates. He wins at Pharsalus (48 BC), in Africa and at Munda (45 BC) and remains as dictator; his assassination in 44 BC opens the final phase of the Republic.

conflictos/guerra-civil-china.bajas.t: ~6–8 million dead (not counting the war against Japan)

conflictos/guerra-civil-china.batallas.c.t: Half a million KMT soldiers annihilated or captured: the decisive battle.

conflictos/guerra-civil-china.batallas.t.t: Mao proclaims the People's Republic on 1 October 1949.

conflictos/guerra-civil-china.descripcio.t: Kuomintang Nationalists against Mao's Communists, with the truce forced by the Japanese invasion (1937–1945): it ends with the People's Republic in Beijing and the KMT taking refuge in Taiwan.

conflictos/guerra-civil-china.zonas.ofen.t: Final offensives (Manchuria and the Central Plain)

conflictos/guerra-civil-china.zonas.sovi.t: Southern soviets and the Long March

conflictos/guerra-civil-espanola.batalla.t: The only provincial capital taken by the Republic, retaken within weeks.
The longest and hardest battle of the war; it exhausts the Republic.
Bloody attempt to cut the Valencia road.
The Condor Legion razes the town; it inspires Picasso's painting.
«No pasarán» («They shall not pass»): the capital withstands the initial assault.

conflictos/guerra-civil-espanola.descrip.t: War between the Republic and Franco's rebels; prelude to the Second World War.

conflictos/guerra-civil-inglesa.bajas.t: hundreds of thousands (including famine and disease)

conflictos/guerra-civil-inglesa.descripc.t: Conflict between the supporters of King Charles I (Royalists) and Parliament. Cromwell's New Model Army wins at Marston Moor (1644) and Naseby (1645); Charles I is executed in 1649 and the Commonwealth is proclaimed. The final defeat of the Scottish Royalists at Worcester (1651) ends the war.

conflictos/guerra-civil-severa.batallas..t: Septimius Severus defeats Pescennius Niger in Cilicia.
Septimius Severus defeats Clodius Albinus near Lyon.

conflictos/guerra-civil-severa.descripci.t: After the year 193 Septimius Severus prevails over the other claimants: he defeats Pescennius Niger in the East (Issus, 194) and Clodius Albinus in Gaul (Lugdunum, 197), consolidating the Severan dynasty.

conflictos/guerra-civil-siria.batallas.b.t: Four years of siege; its recapture by the regime marked a turning point.

conflictos/guerra-civil-siria.batallas.c.t: HTS rebels enter the capital on 8 December; al-Assad flees to Moscow.

conflictos/guerra-civil-siria.batallas.o.t: The regime retakes the rebel belt around Damascus.

conflictos/guerra-civil-siria.batallas.t.t: The Islamic State destroys part of the heritage of the ancient city.
Capture of Palmyra by the Islamic State

conflictos/guerra-civil-siria.descripcio.t: The 2011 protests turn into a multi-sided war with foreign intervention; in December 2024 a lightning offensive topples Bashar al-Assad after 53 years of the regime.

conflictos/guerra-civil-siria.zonas.alza.t: Uprising and war in the west

conflictos/guerra-civil-sudan.batallas.b.t: The capital, an urban battlefield for two years; the army retakes it in March 2025.

conflictos/guerra-civil-sudan.batallas.c.t: tens of thousands killed in the siege
After an 18-month siege, the RSF take the army's last capital in Darfur; massacres documented by satellite.

conflictos/guerra-civil-sudan.batallas.m.t: Ethnic cleansing against the Masalit in West Darfur.

conflictos/guerra-civil-sudan.descripcio.t: The army (SAF) and the RSF paramilitaries have been fighting over the country since April 2023: Khartoum devastated and retaken by the army (2025), massacres in Darfur and the fall of El Fasher (2025). The world's largest displacement crisis.

conflictos/guerra-corea.bajas.t: ~3 million dead, half of them civilians

conflictos/guerra-corea.batallas.batalla.t: Epic retreat of the Marines encircled by the Chinese army at −30 °C.

conflictos/guerra-corea.batallas.desemba.t: MacArthur's masterstroke reverses the war in two weeks.

conflictos/guerra-corea.descripcion.t: The North invades the South; the UN (with the US) drives it back to the Yalu and China intervenes: three years of war to return almost to the 38th parallel, where the 1953 armistice has frozen the peninsula to this day.

conflictos/guerra-corea.zonas.contraofen.t: Counteroffensive to the Yalu and Chinese intervention

conflictos/guerra-corea.zonas.invasion-d.t: Invasion of the South and the Pusan Perimeter

conflictos/guerra-de-gaza.batallas.ataqu.t: Hamas storms the communities and the Nova festival next to the Strip.

conflictos/guerra-de-gaza.batallas.batal.t: Ground invasion of the northern Strip from 27 October.
The front shifts to the south of the Strip.

conflictos/guerra-de-gaza.batallas.ofens.t: Assault on the last refuge next to the Egyptian border.

conflictos/guerra-de-gaza.descripcion.t: Hamas's attack of 7 October 2023 (~1,200 dead) unleashes an Israeli invasion of the Strip that devastates it from north to south; a US-sponsored peace plan imposes a ceasefire in October 2025.

conflictos/guerra-de-tigray.batallas.tom.t: The federal army occupies the regional capital at the start of the war.

conflictos/guerra-de-tigray.descripcion.t: The Ethiopian government and Eritrea against the Tigray liberation front: one of the deadliest wars of the century, ended by the Pretoria agreement (November 2022).

conflictos/guerra-de-yemen.bajas.t: ~377,000 dead (up to 2021, UN), most from famine and disease

conflictos/guerra-de-yemen.batallas.bata.t: The recognized government holds out in the south with coalition support.
Fight for the port that feeds the country; Stockholm Agreement.

conflictos/guerra-de-yemen.batallas.toma.t: The Houthis occupy the capital and dissolve the government.

conflictos/guerra-de-yemen.descripcion.t: The Houthis take Sana'a in 2014 and a Saudi-led coalition intervenes from 2015; truce since 2022 and, since 2023, Houthi attacks on Red Sea shipping, answered by the US.

conflictos/guerra-del-pacifico.batallas..t: Surprise attack that drags the US into the war.
Surrender of the Filipino-American forces on Luzon (April 1942).
First major Allied offensive in the Pacific (August 1942 – February 1943).
Bloody American capture of the island.
Japanese naval defeat that marks the turning point in the Pacific.
Last major land battle before the surrender.
Conquest of the Marianas, the base for the bombing of Japan (June–July 1944).
The largest naval battle of the war; start of the reconquest of the Philippines (October 1944).
First naval battle fought solely between aircraft carriers (May 1942).
Surrender of the British garrison to the Japanese army (15 February 1942).

conflictos/guerra-del-pacifico.descripci.t: Japanese theatre of the Second World War: from the attack on Pearl Harbor (1941) to the American counteroffensive (Midway, Iwo Jima, Okinawa) and the atomic bombs of 1945. The zones are approximations of the theatres of operations (the central Pacific, Hawaii and Midway, are drawn separately so as not to cross the antimeridian). It is recorded as a conflict in its own right for its cartographic value centred on Japan, complementing 'wwii'.

conflictos/guerra-del-pacifico.zonas.asa.t: Assault on Japan (Iwo Jima, Okinawa, bombings)

conflictos/guerra-del-pacifico.zonas.con.t: Allied counteroffensive (Solomons, New Guinea, Marianas, Philippines)

conflictos/guerra-egipcio-otomana.descri.t: Muhammad Ali, governor of Egypt, rebels against the sultan. His troops, led by Ibrahim Pasha, defeat the Ottomans at Konya (1832) and Nezib (1839) and threaten Istanbul, forcing the intervention of the European powers.

conflictos/guerra-estado-islamico.batall.t: Last territorial stronghold of IS, March 2019.
Nine months of urban combat; the largest battle since 2003.
The Syrian «capital» of the caliphate falls.
Kurdish militias, with allied air support, halt IS for the first time.

conflictos/guerra-estado-islamico.descri.t: IS proclaims a «caliphate» over a third of Iraq and Syria; an international coalition and Kurdish and Iraqi forces reduce it to its last enclave at Baghuz (2019).

conflictos/guerra-golfo.batallas.liberac.t: The coalition enters the capital on 27 February; the oil wells burn.

conflictos/guerra-golfo.descripcion.t: Saddam invades Kuwait; a coalition of 35 countries expels him in Operation Desert Storm: a hundred hours of ground war after six weeks of bombing.

conflictos/guerra-gotica.bajas.t: hundreds of thousands; Italy is left devastated

conflictos/guerra-gotica.batallas.asedio.t: Belisarius withstands the Ostrogothic siege by Vitiges.

conflictos/guerra-gotica.batallas.batall.t: Narses defeats and kills King Totila; end of Ostrogothic power.

conflictos/guerra-gotica.descripcion.t: Justinian sends Belisarius and then Narses to recover Italy for the Empire. After almost twenty years of sieges and depopulation, the Ostrogothic kingdom is destroyed at Taginae (552), but Italy is left exhausted in the face of the imminent Lombard arrival.

conflictos/guerra-gotica.nombre.t: Gothic War: Byzantine reconquest of Italy

conflictos/guerra-independencia-cuba.baj.t: Ten Years' War: ~200,000; war of 1895: more than 200,000, counting the civilian victims of Weyler's reconcentration policy (disputed figures)

conflictos/guerra-independencia-cuba.bat.t: Victory of Máximo Gómez and Maceo a few kilometres from Cruces (coordinates of the town).
Céspedes frees his slaves at his La Demajagua sugar mill and rises up against Spain (10 October 1868).

conflictos/guerra-independencia-cuba.des.t: Ten Years' War (1868–1878, Pact of Zanjón), Little War (1879–1880) and the war of 1895–1898, launched by Martí and Maceo; Martí dies at Dos Ríos (1895). It leads to US intervention (see «Spanish–American War»).

conflictos/guerra-independencia-grecia.d.t: The Greeks rise up against Ottoman rule. After years of brutal war, the intervention of the European powers and the destruction of the Ottoman-Egyptian fleet at Navarino (1827) secure the birth of the independent Greek state.

conflictos/guerra-independencia-grecia.z.t: Greece and the Peloponnese in revolt

conflictos/guerra-indochina.descripcion.t: Ho Chi Minh's Viet Minh defeats France at Dien Bien Phu; the Geneva Accords divide Vietnam along the 17th parallel.

conflictos/guerra-irak.bajas.t: widely varying estimates, from ~150,000 to more than 400,000 Iraqi dead (disputed); ~4,500 US soldiers

conflictos/guerra-irak.descripcion.t: The US-led coalition invades Iraq and topples Saddam Hussein; an insurgency and a sectarian civil war follow. Spain withdraws its troops in 2004.

conflictos/guerra-iran-irak.batallas.bat.t: The «Iranian Stalingrad»: Iraq takes the city house by house; Iran retakes it in 1982.

conflictos/guerra-iran-irak.batallas.tom.t: Iran cuts off Iraqi access to the Gulf for two years.

conflictos/guerra-iran-irak.descripcion.t: Saddam Hussein invades revolutionary Iran expecting a quick victory: eight years of trench warfare, gas and «human waves» only to return to the original border.

conflictos/guerra-israel-iran.batallas.a.t: First Israeli strike against the main enrichment plant.

conflictos/guerra-israel-iran.batallas.b.t: US B-2 bombers strike the underground plant, 22 June.

conflictos/guerra-israel-iran.batallas.m.t: The Iranian retaliation hits Israeli urban areas.

conflictos/guerra-israel-iran.descripcio.t: From 13 to 24 June 2025: Israel bombs Iran's nuclear programme and military leadership; Iran responds with more than 550 ballistic missiles; the US strikes Fordow, Natanz and Isfahan before the ceasefire.

conflictos/guerra-italo-turca.descripcio.t: Italy invades Ottoman Tripolitania and Cyrenaica (present-day Libya). The defeat, together with the simultaneous Balkan Wars, accelerates the loss of the empire's last African possessions.

conflictos/guerra-judia.bajas.t: hundreds of thousands dead (Josephus speaks of more than a million)

conflictos/guerra-judia.batallas.sitio-d.t: Titus takes the city and destroys the Second Temple.
The last rebels commit suicide before the fortress falls.

conflictos/guerra-judia.descripcion.t: The great Jewish revolt: Vespasian and Titus subdue Galilee and Judea; Jerusalem and its Temple are destroyed in 70; Masada holds out until 73.

conflictos/guerra-kalinga.bajas.t: 100,000 dead and 150,000 deported according to Ashoka's Edict XIII

conflictos/guerra-kalinga.batallas.batal.t: Traditional site of the battle, 8 km south of Bhubaneswar, beside the Daya River (approximate coordinates).

conflictos/guerra-kalinga.descripcion.t: Ashoka conquers the kingdom of Kalinga (present-day Odisha). The horror of the slaughter, which he himself recounts in his edicts, leads him to embrace Buddhism and «conquest by dharma».

conflictos/guerra-kenmu.batallas.batalla.t: Ashikaga Takauji defeats Kusunoki Masashige, opening the Muromachi shogunate.

conflictos/guerra-kenmu.batallas.caida-d.t: Nitta Yoshisada takes Kamakura and ends the Hōjō regency.

conflictos/guerra-kenmu.descripcion.t: Go-Daigo overthrows the Kamakura bakufu (1333) and tries to restore imperial power; Ashikaga Takauji breaks with him and founds the Muromachi shogunate, opening the period of the Northern and Southern Courts (Nanboku-chō) until the reunification of 1392.

conflictos/guerra-lidio-meda.descripcion.t: According to Herodotus, the war lasts five years without a victor; in the sixth a solar eclipse (28 May 585 BC) interrupts the battle beside the Halys River, and the Lydians and Medes make peace and fix their border there.

conflictos/guerra-malvinas.batallas.bata.t: Battle of Goose Green (Pradera del Ganso)

conflictos/guerra-malvinas.descripcion.t: On 2 April 1982 the Argentine military dictatorship lands on the Falkland Islands (Malvinas), under British administration. The United Kingdom sends an expeditionary force to the South Atlantic; after the sinking of the cruiser General Belgrano and a ten-week land campaign, the Argentine troops surrender at Puerto Argentino (Stanley) on 14 June. The defeat hastens the fall of the military Junta.

conflictos/guerra-mexicano-estadounidens.t: ~25,000 Mexicans and ~13,000 Americans dead (mostly from disease)
Scott opens the road from Veracruz to the capital.
The Niños Héroes; the capital falls the following day.
US occupation of Monterey, capital of Alta California.
First major battle of the war (8 May 1846).
Battle of Resaca de la Palma
Skirmish in the disputed strip between the Nueces and the Rio Grande that the United States used as a casus belli.
After the annexation of Texas, the US invades Mexico; under the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo Mexico cedes Alta California and New Mexico, more than half of its territory.
Campaign from Veracruz to Mexico City

conflictos/guerra-onin.batallas.incendio.t: The fighting between East and West devastates the capital for a decade.

conflictos/guerra-onin.descripcion.t: A succession dispute in the Ashikaga shogunate sets Kyoto ablaze and triggers the disintegration of central power, the beginning of the Sengoku period of the 'warring states'.

conflictos/guerra-pacifico-1879.batallas.t: Assault and capture of the Morro de Arica
Battle of the Alto de la Alianza (Tacna)
Capture of the Huáscar; death of Miguel Grau.
Sinking of the Esmeralda and death of Arturo Prat.

conflictos/guerra-pacifico-1879.descripc.t: War of the Saltpetre: Chile occupies the Bolivian coast and Tarapacá, Tacna and Arica, and even takes Lima. Bolivia loses its access to the sea (Treaty of Ancón, 1883; truce pact, 1884).

conflictos/guerra-peloponeso.bajas.t: tens of thousands; demographic devastation of Athens by the plague (430–429 BC)

conflictos/guerra-peloponeso.descripcion.t: Hegemonic conflict between the Athenian-led Delian League and the Spartan-led Peloponnesian League. After the plague that carried off Pericles, the disaster of the Athenian expedition to Sicily (415–413) and Persian financial intervention, Lysander annihilated the Athenian fleet at Aegospotami (405), forcing Athens to surrender and ending its maritime empire.

conflictos/guerra-peloponeso.zonas.liga-.t: Delian League (Athenian dominion of the Aegean)

conflictos/guerra-ruso-japonesa.batallas.t: The largest land battle up to that time: more than 600,000 combatants.
~5,000 Russian sailors killed; the Baltic Fleet destroyed
Tōgō's fleet annihilates the Russian Baltic squadron and decides the war.
Five months of siege of the Russian naval base.

conflictos/guerra-ruso-japonesa.descripc.t: Japan crushes the Russian Empire over Manchuria and Korea: the first victory of an Asian power over a European one in the modern era, a prelude to the 1905 revolution.

conflictos/guerra-ruso-turca-1877.descri.t: Russia and its Balkan allies defeat the Ottoman Empire; the Treaty of San Stefano creates a Greater Bulgaria, which the Congress of Berlin reduces.

conflictos/guerra-secesion-eeuu.bajas.t: ~750,000 dead, the deadliest war in US history.

conflictos/guerra-secesion-eeuu.batallas.t: The bloodiest day in American military history.
The turning point: Lee would never again invade the North.
Battle of the Head of Passes
Ambush of the steamer J. R. Williams
Lee surrenders to Grant; end of the war.
Grant splits the Confederacy in two by gaining control of the Mississippi.

conflictos/guerra-secesion-eeuu.descripc.t: The Union against the slaveholding Confederacy: from Fort Sumter to Appomattox, with the Emancipation Proclamation (1863) abolishing slavery.

conflictos/guerra-seis-dias.descripcion.t: From 5 to 10 June 1967 Israel launches a pre-emptive strike that destroys the Egyptian air force on the ground and in six days captures the Sinai Peninsula and Gaza from Egypt, the West Bank and East Jerusalem from Jordan, and the Golan Heights from Syria, tripling its territory.

conflictos/guerra-shakushain.batallas.co.t: Initial focus of the Ainu uprising against the Matsumae posts.

conflictos/guerra-shakushain.descripcion.t: Ainu uprising led by Shakushain against the commercial abuses of the Matsumae clan in Ezo (Hokkaido); its defeat consolidates Japanese rule over the north.

conflictos/guerra-triple-alianza.bajas.t: between 150,000 and 300,000 dead; Paraguay loses a large part of its population (figures disputed)

conflictos/guerra-triple-alianza.batalla.t: Death of Francisco Solano López (1 March 1870).

conflictos/guerra-triple-alianza.descrip.t: The deadliest war in South American history: the alliance of Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay defeats the Paraguay of Solano López, who dies at Cerro Corá.

conflictos/guerra-triple-alianza.nombre.t: War of the Triple Alliance (Paraguayan War)

conflictos/guerra-vietnam.batallas.caida.t: North Vietnamese tanks enter the presidential palace; helicopter evacuation of the embassy.

conflictos/guerra-vietnam.batallas.incid.t: Pretext for the US escalation (congressional resolution).

conflictos/guerra-vietnam.batallas.ofens.t: The simultaneous assault on a hundred cities breaks American public opinion; Hue is devastated.

conflictos/guerra-vietnam.descripcion.t: The communist North and the Viet Cong against the South and the United States: the war the US could not win ends with the fall of Saigon and reunification (1976).

conflictos/guerra-yom-kippur.batallas.cr.t: Crossing of the Suez Canal (Operation Badr)

conflictos/guerra-yom-kippur.descripcion.t: On 6 October 1973, on the Jewish holy day of Yom Kippur, Egypt crosses the Suez Canal and Syria launches a surprise attack on the Golan. After initial losses, Israel counterattacks, crosses the canal and encircles the Egyptian Third Army; the ceasefire comes through superpower mediation. The war triggers the OPEC oil embargo.

conflictos/guerras-alto-karabaj.batallas.t: The capture of the fortress city decides the 2020 war.
The enclave's capital surrenders; dissolution of the Republic of Artsakh.

conflictos/guerras-alto-karabaj.descripc.t: In 44 days (2020) Azerbaijan retakes much of the Armenian enclave, and it seizes the whole of it in the lightning offensive of September 2023: almost the entire Armenian population flees.

conflictos/guerras-balcanes.descripcion.t: In the First Balkan War (1912–13) the Balkan League—Serbia, Bulgaria, Greece and Montenegro—drives the Ottoman Empire out of almost all of Europe. In the Second (1913), Bulgaria attacks its former allies over the partition of Macedonia and is defeated. The wars leave the region unstable, a prelude to the First World War.

conflictos/guerras-civiles-libia.batalla.t: Misrata forces drive IS out of its main Libyan enclave.
Battle of Sirte against the Islamic State
Last stronghold of the regime; Muammar Gaddafi is captured and killed on 20 October.
The rebels take the capital in August 2011.

conflictos/guerras-civiles-libia.descrip.t: The Arab Spring and NATO intervention topple Gaddafi (2011); the country then fractures between rival governments until the 2020 ceasefire.

conflictos/guerras-civiles-tetrarquia.ba.t: Constantine's final victory over Licinius, on the Asian shore of the Bosporus (present-day Üsküdar).
Constantine defeats Maxentius, who drowns in the Tiber (coordinates of the present-day Ponte Milvio).

conflictos/guerras-civiles-tetrarquia.de.t: Diocletian's Tetrarchy breaks down into wars between co-emperors. Constantine defeats Maxentius at the Milvian Bridge (312) and Licinius at Adrianople and Chrysopolis (324), and reunites the whole Empire under his rule.

conflictos/guerras-civiles-tetrarquia.zo.t: Thrace and the Bosporus (Constantine against Licinius)

conflictos/guerras-diadocos.descripcion.t: On the death of Alexander the Great his generals (the Diadochi) fought over the empire. After the partitions of Babylon (323) and Triparadisus (321) and the Greek revolts of the Lamian War, the Battle of Ipsus (301) sealed the fragmentation into the great Hellenistic kingdoms: the Ptolemaic in Egypt, the Seleucid in Asia and the Antigonid in Macedonia.

conflictos/guerras-emishi.batallas.campa.t: Sakanoue no Tamuramaro defeats Aterui and builds the fort of Isawa.

conflictos/guerras-emishi.descripcion.t: The Nara and Heian court subjugates the Emishi of northern Honshu; Sakanoue no Tamuramaro, the first sei-i taishōgun, completes the conquest of Tōhoku.

conflictos/guerras-husitas.bajas.t: tens of thousands; the population of Bohemia falls by about a third

conflictos/guerras-husitas.batallas.bata.t: The fifth crusade flees before the Hussites (coordinates of the town).
Žižka breaks the imperial encirclement (21 December 1421).
The moderate Hussites (Utraquists) defeat the radical Taborites.
Jan Žižka repels Sigismund's crusaders on Vítkov Hill, next to Prague.

conflictos/guerras-husitas.descripcion.t: After the death of Jan Hus, the Hussites of Bohemia repel five crusades with their fortified wagons and firearms; the Compacts of Basel (1436) recognize their form of worship.

conflictos/guerras-indias.bajas.t: ~50,000 killed in combat; displacement and epidemics cost many more Native lives

conflictos/guerras-indias.batallas.batal.t: Crazy Horse and Sitting Bull annihilate the 7th Cavalry.
Battle of the North Fork of the Red River

conflictos/guerras-indias.batallas.masac.t: ~200 Cheyenne and Arapaho killed, two-thirds of them women and children
The Colorado militia attacks a peaceful encampment.
~250–300 Lakota killed, mostly elderly people, women and children
The army crushes the Ghost Dance; end of the Indian Wars.

conflictos/guerras-indias.batallas.rendi.t: Apache resistance ends in Skeleton Canyon.

conflictos/guerras-indias.descripcion.t: A century of wars and broken treaties: from Tippecanoe (1811) and the Indian Removal Act (1830) with the Trail of Tears, to the Plains Wars, Little Bighorn (1876), the surrender of Geronimo (1886) and the Wounded Knee massacre (1890). The tribes lost almost all their territory, which was reduced to reservations.

conflictos/guerras-indias.nombre.t: American Indian Wars and the conquest of the West

conflictos/guerras-indo-pakistanies.baja.t: more than 30,000 dead across all the wars

conflictos/guerras-indo-pakistanies.desc.t: After the 1947 partition, India and Pakistan fight three wars: in 1947–48 and 1965 over Kashmir, with no decisive border changes, and in 1971, when Indian intervention in the Bangladesh Liberation War leads to the surrender of more than 90,000 Pakistani soldiers in Dhaka and the birth of Bangladesh.

conflictos/guerras-italia.batallas.batal.t: The Great Captain wins the first battle decided by infantry gunpowder.
Spanish arquebusiers capture King Francis I of France.
Philip II's victory commemorated by El Escorial.

conflictos/guerras-italia.descripcion.t: Sixty years of Franco-Spanish struggle for Italy: the Great Captain invents the tercios, Charles V captures Francis I at Pavia and the Peace of Cateau-Cambrésis enshrines Spanish hegemony.

conflictos/guerras-jin-song.batallas.bat.t: Yue Fei's victory over the Jin near present-day Luohe (coordinates of the city).

conflictos/guerras-jin-song.batallas.cai.t: The Jin sack the Song capital and carry off Emperors Huizong and Qinzong as captives.

conflictos/guerras-jin-song.descripcion.t: The Jurchen of the Jin dynasty take Kaifeng (Jingkang Incident, 1127) and capture Emperor Huizong; the Song take refuge in the south and the Treaty of Shaoxing (1142) fixes the border on the Huai River.

conflictos/guerras-magiares.batallas.bat.t: Otto I annihilates the Magyars near Augsburg.
The Magyars destroy the Bavarian army.
Henry I the Fowler defeats the Magyars.

conflictos/guerras-magiares.descripcion.t: For half a century Magyar horsemen raid central and western Europe, until Otto I crushes them on the banks of the Lech, near Augsburg (955), ending the raids and pushing Hungary towards a settled Christian way of life.

conflictos/guerras-marcomanas.batallas.b.t: Roman legions defeat the Sarmatian Iazyges on the frozen Danube.
Battle on the frozen Danube (against the Iazyges)

conflictos/guerras-marcomanas.descripcio.t: Marcus Aurelius fights for years against the Marcomanni, Quadi and Sarmatians, who cross the middle Danube and even besiege Aquileia. The Roman campaigns hold back Germanic pressure on Pannonia and Noricum until the emperor's death in 180.

conflictos/guerras-medicas.batallas.bata.t: Leonidas and his 300 Spartans hold out to the end.
Miltiades repels the first Persian invasion.
The Greek infantry annihilates the army of Mardonius.
Themistocles destroys the Persian fleet in the strait.

conflictos/guerras-medicas.descripcion.t: From the Ionian Revolt to Marathon (490 BC), Thermopylae and Salamis (480) and Plataea (479): the Greek poleis halt the greatest empire of their time.

conflictos/guerras-mesenia.descripcion.t: Series of wars through which Sparta conquered and subjugated neighboring Messenia, reducing its population to the status of helots. The third war (464 BC), a helot revolt after an earthquake, strained Sparta's relations with Athens. The dates are conventional: the chronology of the first two wars is uncertain (other sources give c. 735–715 and c. 660 BC).

conflictos/guerras-otomano-safavies.desc.t: Long rivalry with Safavid Persia over eastern Anatolia, the Caucasus and Iraq. Selim I defeats Shah Ismail at Çaldıran (1514) and Suleiman I conquers Tabriz and Baghdad (1534). The conflict, with a Sunni–Shia religious background, ends with the Peace of Zuhab (1639).

conflictos/guerras-otomano-safavies.zona.t: Contested eastern Anatolia, Caucasus and Iraq

conflictos/guerras-otomano-venecianas.de.t: Series of wars for control of the eastern Mediterranean. The Ottomans take Cyprus (Nicosia, 1570) and Crete (long siege of Candia, 1645–1669) from Venice, but suffer the great naval defeat of Lepanto (1571) at the hands of the Holy League.

conflictos/guerras-otomano-venecianas.zo.t: Aegean and eastern Mediterranean in dispute

conflictos/guerras-pergamo-galatas.descr.t: Campaigns of Attalus I of Pergamon against the Galatians, Celtic tribes settled in central Anatolia. His victory at the Caicus River legitimized the Attalids, who adopted the royal title and commemorated the triumph with the famous Dying Gaul.

conflictos/guerras-religion-francia.bata.t: Henry IV defeats the Catholic League (14 March 1590).
The Duke of Guise's troops attack a Calvinist service (1 March 1562); the war begins.
Massacre of Huguenots in Paris and the provinces (24 August 1572).

conflictos/guerras-religion-francia.desc.t: Catholics and Huguenots clash in eight wars; the conversion of Henry IV (1593) and the Edict of Nantes (1598) bring them to an end.

conflictos/guerras-romano-partas-alto-im.t: Trajan occupies the Parthian capital and reaches the Persian Gulf.

Series of campaigns for control of Armenia and Mesopotamia: Corbulo under Nero (54–63), Trajan's Parthian campaign (114–117), that of Lucius Verus (161–166) and the Second Parthian campaign of Septimius Severus (197–199). The conflict with the Arsacids lasts until the Sasanians replace them.

conflictos/guerras-romano-partas-republi.t: ~20,000 Romans killed and 10,000 taken prisoner at Carrhae alone
The Parthian Surena destroys the army of Crassus, who dies during the retreat.

First clash between Rome and the Parthians. Crassus invades Mesopotamia and is annihilated at Carrhae (53 BC); the Parthians counterattack in Syria and Mark Antony fails in his campaign of 36 BC. The Euphrates remains the border.

conflictos/guerras-ruso-turcas.batallas..t: Suvorov storms the Ottoman fortress on the Danube.
The Russian Baltic Fleet, arriving via the Mediterranean, destroys the Ottoman fleet off Çeşme.
Rumyantsev defeats the Grand Vizier by the Kagul River (today Cahul, Moldova).
Diebitsch defeats the Grand Vizier and opens the way across the Balkans towards Adrianople.
Suvorov and the Prince of Coburg defeat the Ottomans by the Râmnicu Sărat River.

conflictos/guerras-ruso-turcas.descripci.t: Cycle of wars with Russia over the Black Sea, the Danube, Crimea and the Caucasus. After the Ottoman victory on the Pruth (1711), the trend is reversed: the wars of 1768–1774 (Küçük Kaynarca), 1787–1792 (Jassy) and 1828–1829 mark the Ottoman retreat before Russian expansion.

conflictos/guerras-ruso-turcas.zonas.mar.t: Black Sea, Danube and Caucasus in dispute

conflictos/guerras-siriacas.descripcion.t: Series of wars between the Ptolemies and the Seleucids for control of Coele-Syria, Phoenicia and the eastern Aegean. The Ptolemaic victory at Raphia (217) and, above all, the Seleucid victory at Panium (200) shifted control of the region towards Antioch, until Rome halted Antiochus IV in 168.

conflictos/guerras-siriacas.zonas.egeo-o.t: Eastern Aegean and the Anatolian coast

conflictos/guerras-unificacion-italiana..t: Its carnage inspires Henry Dunant to create the Red Cross.
The First (1848–1849), Second (1859) and Third (1866) Wars of Independence, Garibaldi's Expedition of the Thousand (1860) and the capture of Rome (1870) create the Kingdom of Italy.

conflictos/guerras-yugoslavas.batallas.b.t: 87 days of siege; the first European city razed since 1945.

conflictos/guerras-yugoslavas.batallas.s.t: The longest siege of a capital city in modern history: 1,425 days.

conflictos/guerras-yugoslavas.descripcio.t: The disintegration of Yugoslavia in wars of ethnic cleansing: Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia (with the siege of Sarajevo) and Kosovo, until NATO intervention.

conflictos/han-xiongnu.batallas.cerco-de.t: The Xiongnu encircle Gaozu; truce and tribute.

conflictos/han-xiongnu.descripcion.t: Emperor Wu abandons the policy of appeasement (heqin) and launches major campaigns against the Xiongnu nomads of the steppe. Generals such as Wei Qing and Huo Qubing push the frontier north and into the Hexi Corridor, opening the route to Central Asia. Earlier, at Pingcheng (200 BC), the founder Gaozu had been surrounded by the Xiongnu.

conflictos/hastings.batallas.batalla-de-.t: King Harold II dies; the Normans conquer England.

conflictos/hastings.descripcion.t: William the Conqueror takes the English crown after Hastings.

conflictos/heraclio-sasanida.bajas.t: unknown; the last great war of Antiquity between Rome and Persia

conflictos/heraclio-sasanida.batallas.as.t: Avars and Persians fail before the city walls.

conflictos/heraclio-sasanida.batallas.ba.t: Heraclius defeats the Persian army by the Tigris.

conflictos/heraclio-sasanida.descripcion.t: The Sasanians of Khosrow II occupy Syria, Egypt and Anatolia and even besiege Constantinople together with the Avars (626). Heraclius counterattacks through the Caucasus, allied with the Khazars, and wins at Nineveh (627), forcing the return of everything that had been lost.

conflictos/hispania-romana.batallas.ases.t: Rome buys off his murderers: “Rome does not pay traitors”.

conflictos/hispania-romana.batallas.siti.t: Scipio Aemilianus starves the Celtiberian city, a symbol of resistance, into surrender.

conflictos/hispania-romana.descripcion.t: Two hundred years of conquest: from the landing at Emporion (218 BC) to the Lusitanian Wars of Viriathus, the siege of Numantia (133 BC) and the Cantabrian Wars of Augustus (29–19 BC).

conflictos/hispano-estadounidense.batall.t: Dewey destroys the Spanish squadron in the Philippines within hours.
Cervera's squadron is annihilated while trying to break the blockade.
The charge of Roosevelt's Rough Riders decides Santiago.

conflictos/hispano-estadounidense.descri.t: After the sinking of the Maine, the US takes Cuba, Puerto Rico, the Philippines and Guam from Spain: the end of the Spanish overseas empire.

conflictos/imjin.batallas.batalla-de-han.t: Yi Sun-sin destroys the Japanese fleet with the crane-wing formation.

conflictos/imjin.batallas.batalla-de-nor.t: Final battle: allied victory and death of Yi Sun-sin.

conflictos/imjin.descripcion.t: Hideyoshi invades Korea as a step towards China; Admiral Yi Sun-sin and his turtle ships cut the sea lanes, and Hideyoshi's death ends the war.

conflictos/imperio-nuevo-egipto.bajas.t: tens of thousands (ancient figures are propagandistic)

conflictos/imperio-nuevo-egipto.batallas.t: Ramesses II against Muwatalli II on the banks of the Orontes: the largest known chariot battle, which ended in a draw.
Thutmose III defeats the Canaanite coalition of the king of Kadesh: the first battle in history with a detailed account (the Karnak annals).
Ramesses III annihilates the fleet of the Sea Peoples at the mouths of the Nile: Egypt is the only state to withstand the Bronze Age collapse.

conflictos/imperio-nuevo-egipto.descripc.t: After expelling the Hyksos, Egypt builds its greatest empire: from the Fourth Cataract of the Nile (Kush) to the Euphrates. Thutmose III fights at Megiddo the first documented battle in history; Ramesses II halts the Hittites at Kadesh and signs with them the earliest surviving peace treaty; Ramesses III repels the Sea Peoples.

conflictos/imperio-nuevo-egipto.nombre.t: Expansion of the Egyptian New Kingdom

conflictos/imperio-nuevo-egipto.zonas.ca.t: Campaigns of Thutmose III in Canaan and Syria

conflictos/incidente-manchuria.batallas..t: A staged explosion on the railway that serves as a pretext for the invasion.

conflictos/incidente-manchuria.descripci.t: The Kwantung Army stages the Mukden sabotage and occupies all of Manchuria, creating the puppet state of Manchukuo and precipitating Japan's withdrawal from the League of Nations.

conflictos/independencia-eeuu.batallas.b.t: Battle of Forts Clinton and Montgomery
The victory that convinces France to enter the war.

conflictos/independencia-eeuu.batallas.g.t: Spain and France besiege the Rock for almost four years without success.

conflictos/independencia-eeuu.batallas.r.t: Spain recovers the island lost at Utrecht.

conflictos/independencia-eeuu.batallas.s.t: Surrender of Cornwallis; decisive Franco-American victory.

conflictos/independencia-eeuu.batallas.t.t: Gálvez drives the British out of West Florida.

conflictos/independencia-eeuu.descripcio.t: The American colonies win independence from Great Britain with the help of France and Spain. Control of the territory shifted: the British held Boston (1775–76), New York (1776–83), Philadelphia (1777–78) and the South (1779–82), while the Patriots controlled New England and the interior; after Yorktown (1781) British control was reduced to New York.

conflictos/independencia-escocia.descrip.t: After the Scottish succession crisis arbitrated by Edward I at Norham (1291), Scotland resists English rule: William Wallace wins at Stirling Bridge (1297) and Robert the Bruce at Bannockburn (1314). The Treaty of Edinburgh–Northampton (1328) recognizes Scottish independence.

conflictos/independencia-hispanoamerica..t: Sucre defeats the last royalist army; end of Spanish rule on the mainland.
Bolívar secures the independence of New Granada.
Bolívar secures the independence of Venezuela.
San Martín's Army of the Andes defeats the royalists and opens the road to Santiago.
Victory of the patriot cavalry before Ayacucho.
The American viceroyalties gain independence from Spain after the crisis of 1808.
Río de la Plata and Chile

conflictos/india-britanica.bajas.t: hundreds of thousands dead (plus the Bengal famines)

conflictos/india-britanica.batallas.bata.t: The victory the future Wellington considered his finest battle.
Clive, with 3,000 men and bribes, wins Bengal.

conflictos/india-britanica.batallas.caid.t: Tipu Sultan, the “Tiger of Mysore”, dies.

conflictos/india-britanica.descripcion.t: From Plassey (1757) to the final defeat of the Marathas (1818): the East India Company turns the subcontinent into the heart of the British Empire.

conflictos/invasion-lombarda.batallas.en.t: Alboin crosses the Julian Alps into Friuli.

conflictos/invasion-lombarda.batallas.to.t: The future capital of the Lombard kingdom falls.

conflictos/invasion-lombarda.descripcion.t: Alboin leads the Lombards into Italy on 2 April 568 and within a few years subdues the north of the peninsula, shattering the Byzantine reunification and founding a kingdom with its capital at Pavia.

conflictos/invasion-rusa-ucrania.bajas.t: hundreds of thousands of military casualties and tens of thousands of civilians (ongoing)

conflictos/invasion-rusa-ucrania.batalla.t: Russia takes the Donbas stronghold at enormous cost.
The longest and bloodiest battle of the war; the city falls in May 2023.
The capital holds out; Russia withdraws from the north in April.
First Ukrainian offensive on Russian territory, repelled in 2025.
The only occupied regional capital, retaken by Ukraine in November.
Three months of siege and resistance at the Azovstal steelworks.

conflictos/invasion-rusa-ucrania.descrip.t: On 24 February 2022 Russia launches the largest war in Europe since 1945. After the failed offensive on Kyiv, the front stalls in the east and south; the war is still ongoing in 2026, with peace negotiations deadlocked.

conflictos/invasiones-vikingas.bajas.t: tens of thousands over three centuries (no reliable records)

conflictos/invasiones-vikingas.batallas..t: Hundreds of Viking ships besiege Paris for a year; Count Odo holds out.
Athelstan defeats the alliance of Dublin Vikings and Scots: the idea of a united England is born.
Brian Boru breaks Viking power in Ireland, dying in the hour of victory.
Alfred the Great defeats Guthrum and saves Wessex; the subsequent treaty sets the borders of the Danelaw.
The raid on the monastery of the Holy Island, on 8 June 793, marks the beginning of the Viking Age.
The Great Heathen Army of Ivar and Halfdan captures York, capital of the future Danelaw.

conflictos/invasiones-vikingas.descripci.t: From the sack of Lindisfarne (793) to Stamford Bridge (1066): the Scandinavians raid and then colonize the British Isles, Ireland and the Seine, impose the Danelaw in north-east England and found settlements from Dublin to Normandy.

conflictos/invasiones-vikingas.zonas.el-.t: The Danelaw (Northumbria, East Anglia and the Five Boroughs)

conflictos/invasiones-vikingas.zonas.inc.t: Coastal raids on the British Isles
Raids along the Seine (until the treaty of 911)

conflictos/italo-etiope-adwa.bajas.t: some 12,000 dead (most of them on the Italian side at Adwa)

conflictos/italo-etiope-adwa.descripcion.t: Italy tries to turn Ethiopia into a protectorate, relying on an ambiguous interpretation of the Treaty of Wuchale. Emperor Menelik II mobilizes a large army and on 1 March 1896 crushes the Italian forces at the Battle of Adwa, the greatest defeat suffered by a European colonial power in Africa; Ethiopia preserves its independence.

conflictos/liberacion-tibet.batallas.bat.t: The People's Liberation Army begins the annexation of Tibet.

conflictos/liberacion-tibet.descripcion.t: The People's Liberation Army defeats the Tibetan army at the Battle of Qamdo (Chamdo) in October 1950; in May 1951 the Seventeen Point Agreement incorporates Tibet into the People's Republic of China. Spanish- and English-language historiography speaks of the annexation of Tibet; the PRC officially calls it the “peaceful liberation of Tibet”.

conflictos/liberacion-tibet.nombre.t: Incorporation of Tibet into the People's Republic of China (1950-1951)

conflictos/manzikert.bajas.t: thousands; Emperor Romanos IV is taken prisoner

conflictos/manzikert.descripcion.t: Alp Arslan defeats and captures Romanos IV Diogenes at Manzikert; the Turks spread across Anatolia and Byzantium asks the West for help, a prelude to the Crusades.

conflictos/manzikert.nombre.t: Byzantine–Seljuk war and Battle of Manzikert

conflictos/ming-qing.batallas.batalla-de.t: The surrender of Taiwan completes the Qing conquest.
Wu Sangui opens the Great Wall to the Manchus.

conflictos/ming-qing.batallas.caida-de-p.t: Li Zicheng takes the capital; the last Ming emperor hangs himself.

conflictos/ming-qing.batallas.sitio-de-y.t: massacre of the population over ten days
The Southern Ming resistance is crushed.

conflictos/ming-qing.descripcion.t: From Nurhaci's Seven Grievances (1618) to the fall of Beijing and Shanhaiguan (1644), the resistance of the Southern Ming and the capture of Taiwan (1683): the Manchus found the last imperial dynasty.

conflictos/mitridaticas.batallas.batalla.t: Sulla defeats the Pontic army in Greece.

conflictos/mitridaticas.descripcion.t: Three wars against Mithridates VI of Pontus; Pompey reorganizes the entire Roman East.

conflictos/mongolas.batallas.batalla-de-.t: The Mamluks of Qutuz and Baibars halt the Mongol advance towards Egypt (3 September 1260).
The Mongols defeat the Poles and the Teutonic Knights.
Batu and Subutai annihilate the army of Béla IV of Hungary (11 April 1241).

conflictos/mongolas.batallas.batalla-del.t: Subutai and Jebe defeat the princes of Rus' and the Cumans (31 May 1223).

conflictos/mongolas.batallas.saqueo-de-b.t: Hulagu destroys the Abbasid capital; end of the Baghdad caliphate.

conflictos/mongolas.batallas.sitio-de-xi.t: Key victory of Kublai Khan over the Song.

conflictos/mongolas.descripcion.t: The largest land conquest in history, from Korea to Poland.

conflictos/mongolas.zonas.primera-incurs.t: First raid into the Pontic steppe

conflictos/mongoles-japon.bajas.t: ~100,000 dead, most of them drowned invaders

conflictos/mongoles-japon.batallas.prime.t: The Mongols land at Hakata; a storm wrecks their fleet.

conflictos/mongoles-japon.batallas.segun.t: A typhoon annihilates Kublai's great armada.

conflictos/mongoles-japon.descripcion.t: Kublai Khan launches two invasions of Japan; both fleets are destroyed by typhoons, the “kamikaze” or divine winds.

conflictos/napoleonicas.batallas.batalla.t: The 'Battle of the Three Emperors', Napoleon's masterpiece.
The first defeat of a Napoleonic army in open battle, at the hands of General Castaños.
~70,000 killed and wounded in one day
A bloody battle at the gates of Moscow during the invasion of Russia.
A bloody clash with no clear victor between the French and the Russians in East Prussia.
French victory over Russia that leads to the Peace of Tilsit (14 June 1807).
Napoleon and Davout shatter the Prussian army (14 October 1806).
Wellington defeats Marmont's French army south of Salamanca (22 July 1812).
Nelson destroys the Franco-Spanish fleet; he is killed in action.
Wellington drives out Joseph I; the French booty is left scattered across the field.
Napoleon defeats Austria north-east of Vienna (5–6 July 1809).
Wellington and Blücher defeat Napoleon once and for all.

conflictos/napoleonicas.batallas.levanta.t: Madrid rises up against Murat's troops; Goya painted the executions of 3 May.

conflictos/napoleonicas.batallas.sitios-.t: “War to the knife”: Palafox's resistance astonishes Europe.

conflictos/napoleonicas.descripcion.t: Napoleon dominates Europe until his final defeat at Waterloo. Includes the Peninsular War (Spanish War of Independence, 1808–1814).

conflictos/navas.batallas.batalla-de-las.t: Alfonso VIII, Peter II and Sancho VII defeat al-Nasir.
Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa

conflictos/navas.descripcion.t: Christian coalition against the Almohads; a turning point of the Reconquista.

conflictos/navas.nombre.t: Crusade of Las Navas de Tolosa

conflictos/ochenta-anos.batallas.batalla.t: Louis of Nassau defeats the Spanish troops: this is considered the start of the war (23 May 1568).
The Dutch destroy the last great Spanish armada.
Maurice of Nassau defeats Archduke Albert in the dunes of Flanders (also part of the Anglo-Spanish War).

conflictos/ochenta-anos.batallas.sitio-d.t: Alexander Farnese recovers the great city for Spain.
The surrender that Velázquez painted in “The Lances”.

conflictos/ochenta-anos.descripcion.t: The revolt of the Netherlands against Philip II turns into an eighty-year war that bleeds the Spanish monarchy dry; the Peace of Westphalia recognizes Dutch independence.

conflictos/opio.batallas.saqueo-del-pala.t: Anglo-French troops burn down the imperial marvel.
Sacking of the Old Summer Palace

conflictos/opio.batallas.toma-de-canton..t: British cannons open up southern China.

conflictos/opio.descripcion.t: Britain imposes the opium trade at cannon point: China cedes Hong Kong and opens its ports; in 1860 Anglo-French troops loot the Summer Palace in Beijing.

conflictos/otomano-habsburgo.batallas.ba.t: The Holy League destroys the Ottoman fleet; Cervantes fights in the battle.
Louis II of Hungary dies; the kingdom is split in two.

conflictos/otomano-habsburgo.batallas.pr.t: Suleiman fails before the walls of Vienna.

conflictos/otomano-habsburgo.descripcion.t: Struggle between Suleiman and the Habsburgs for Hungary and the Mediterranean.

conflictos/peregrinacion-gracia.descripc.t: Major popular revolt in the north of England against Henry VIII's break with Rome and the dissolution of the monasteries, led by Robert Aske. It was harshly suppressed after the deception of a royal amnesty.

conflictos/poitiers.batallas.batalla-de-.t: Charles Martel halts the Umayyad advance in Western Europe.

conflictos/poitiers.descripcion.t: Umayyad expeditions north of the Pyrenees, halted by the Franks.

conflictos/primera-guerra-chino-japonesa.t: Surrender of the Chinese fleet; Treaty of Shimonoseki.
Japan defeats the Beiyang Fleet; control of the Yellow Sea.

China (Qing) and Japan clash over control of Korea. The Chinese defeat, sealed in the Yellow Sea and at Weihaiwei, exposes the backwardness of the Qing empire compared with modernized Japan; the Treaty of Shimonoseki (1895) cedes Taiwan and Korea leaves the Chinese orbit.

conflictos/primera-punica.batallas.batal.t: The naval victory that decides the war; Carthage sues for peace.
The first great Roman naval victory, thanks to the corvus.
One of the largest naval battles of Antiquity.

conflictos/primera-punica.descripcion.t: Rome and Carthage fight over Sicily for 23 years; Rome becomes a naval power and gains its first province.
