conflictos/rebelion-bar-kokhba.bajas.t: 580,000 Jews killed according to Cassius Dio

conflictos/rebelion-bar-kokhba.batallas..t: Fall of Bar Kokhba's fortress, 11 km south-west of Jerusalem (coordinates of Battir, where its remains lie).

conflictos/rebelion-bar-kokhba.descripci.t: Jewish uprising against Hadrian over the refoundation of Jerusalem as Aelia Capitolina. Simon bar Kokhba creates a short-lived state; the fall of Betar (135) ends the resistance and Judea is left depopulated.

conflictos/rebelion-boxer.descripcion.t: Anti-foreign movement backed by Cixi; the intervention of eight powers lifts the siege of the Beijing legations and imposes the Boxer Protocol (1901) on China.

conflictos/rebelion-glyndwr.batallas.bat.t: The Welsh defeat and capture Edmund Mortimer near Pilleth (22 June 1402).
Welsh victory on the Monmouthshire border (approximate coordinates, near Grosmont).
John Talbot's English defeat the forces of Rhys Gethin.
Henry IV defeats the rebel Percys, who were expecting Welsh help from Glyndŵr.
Traditional battle of very doubtful existence: there is no contemporary evidence that it was ever fought.

conflictos/rebelion-glyndwr.descripcion.t: Owain Glyndŵr proclaims himself Prince of Wales in 1400 and rises against Henry IV of England; with French support (1405) he controls much of Wales, but loses his castles around 1409 and the resistance fades out around 1415. It is a war distinct from the Hundred Years' War, although France took advantage of it.

conflictos/rebelion-india-1857.bajas.t: hundreds of thousands, mostly Indian civilians (figures disputed)

conflictos/rebelion-india-1857.descripci.t: The sepoys mutiny at Meerut and proclaim the last Mughal emperor; once the revolt is crushed, the British Crown takes over the government of India (1858, British Raj).

conflictos/rebelion-jonia.batallas.batal.t: Battle of Lade / fall of Miletus

conflictos/rebelion-jonia.descripcion.t: Revolt of the Greek poleis of Ionia (Asia Minor) against Persian rule, supported by Athens and Eretria. The burning of Sardis provoked the retaliation of Darius I; the naval defeat at Lade and the fall of Miletus (494) crushed the rebellion and triggered the Persian Wars.

conflictos/rebelion-masakado.batallas.ba.t: Fujiwara no Hidesato and Taira no Sadamori defeat and kill Masakado.

conflictos/rebelion-masakado.descripcion.t: The warlord Taira no Masakado rises in revolt in Kantō and proclaims himself 'new emperor'; he is defeated and killed in 940, an early sign of the military power of the bushi.

conflictos/rebelion-taiping.bajas.t: ~20–30 million dead: the deadliest civil war in history

conflictos/rebelion-taiping.batallas.cai.t: Zeng Guofan's army crushes the kingdom; hundreds of thousands are massacred.

conflictos/rebelion-taiping.batallas.tom.t: The Taiping make Nanjing their “Heavenly Capital” for eleven years.

conflictos/rebelion-taiping.descripcion.t: Hong Xiuquan, self-proclaimed brother of Jesus Christ, founds the “Heavenly Kingdom of Great Peace” and drags the Yangtze valley into a war that bleeds Qing China dry.

conflictos/reconquista.bajas.t: unknown: seven centuries of frontier warfare

conflictos/reconquista.batallas.batalla-.t: ~20,000 Castilian casualties according to the chronicles
The great Almohad victory that precedes Las Navas.
According to tradition, Almanzor's first great defeat shortly before his death (“In Calatañazor Almanzor lost his drum”).
Legendary victory of Ramiro I of Asturias, origin of the myth of Saint James the Moor-slayer (historicity disputed).
The Almoravids crush Alfonso VI and halt the Christian advance.
Ramiro II of León defeats Abd al-Rahman III.
Castilian disaster; the heir Sancho Alfónsez is killed.
Castile and Portugal defeat the last great invading North African army.

conflictos/reconquista.batallas.conquist.t: Afonso I Henriques takes the city with the help of the crusaders of the Second Crusade (1 July – 25 October 1147); Alfonso VI had briefly occupied it in 1093–1094.
Ferdinand III takes the largest city of al-Andalus after a two-year siege.
Rodrigo Díaz de Vivar takes the city, which his widow will lose in 1102.

conflictos/reconquista.batallas.toma-de-.t: Alfonso VI conquers the old Visigothic capital; the frontier jumps to the Tagus.

conflictos/reconquista.descripcion.t: Seven and a half centuries of Christian advance from north to south across the peninsula, from Covadonga (722) to Granada (1492), with long periods of coexistence and frontier in between.

conflictos/reconquista.zonas.frontera-de.t: Frontier from the Tagus to the Guadalquivir

conflictos/reinos-combatientes.batallas..t: ~450,000 Zhao dead according to Sima Qian
Qin annihilates the army of Zhao; most of the prisoners are executed. It was fought northwest of Gaoping (Shanxi): the marker is at Gaoping.
Qi defeats Wei again; death of Pang Juan.

conflictos/reinos-combatientes.descripci.t: After the fragmentation of the Eastern Zhou, seven great states vie for hegemony over China. Qi defeats Wei at Guilin (Guiling) and Maling thanks to the strategies of Sun Bin; finally Qin, strengthened by the Legalist reforms of Shang Yang, absorbs its rivals and unifies China in 221 BC.

conflictos/reinos-combatientes.zonas.est.t: Warring states of the Central Plain of China

conflictos/reunificacion-sui.batallas.co.t: Sui reunifies China after almost four centuries of division.

conflictos/reunificacion-sui.descripcion.t: Emperor Wen (Yang Jian) of Sui launches a great offensive against the last of the Southern states, the Chen dynasty, taking its capital Jiankang (Nanjing) in 589 and reunifying China after almost four centuries of division.

conflictos/reunificacion-sui.zonas.ofens.t: Sui offensive on the lower Yangtze

conflictos/revolucion-abasi.bajas.t: tens of thousands; the Umayyad family is massacred except for Abd al-Rahman I

conflictos/revolucion-abasi.batallas.bat.t: The Abbasids defeat the last Umayyad caliph, Marwan II, by the Great Zab. The exact site is unknown: the marker is at the confluence of the Great Zab and the Tigris.

conflictos/revolucion-abasi.descripcion.t: From Khorasan, the Abbasid movement overthrows the Umayyads at the Battle of the Zab (750); the capital moves to Iraq and a surviving Umayyad founds the Emirate of Córdoba (756).

conflictos/revolucion-francesa.batallas..t: Decisive victory over the coalition; first military use of an observation balloon.
Moreau defeats the Austrians east of Munich (3 December 1800).
Bonaparte defeats the Mamluks near Embabeh (21 July 1798).
Bonaparte's victory over Austria in Piedmont (14 June 1800).
Bonaparte defeats the Austrians in northern Italy (14 January 1797).
The cannonade that saved the Revolution: the republic is proclaimed two days later.
Nelson destroys the French fleet in Aboukir Bay (1–3 August 1798).

conflictos/revolucion-francesa.descripci.t: From the storming of the Bastille to Napoleon's 18 Brumaire: the monarchy falls, the republic survives the Terror and the European coalition, and the modern political world is born.

conflictos/revolucion-francesa.nombre.t: French Revolution and French Revolutionary Wars

conflictos/revolucion-gloriosa.bajas.t: few in England (higher in Ireland and Scotland)

conflictos/revolucion-gloriosa.batallas..t: Landing of William of Orange at Torbay

conflictos/revolucion-gloriosa.descripci.t: William III of Orange lands at Torbay (5 November 1688) at the invitation of the Protestant elite; James II flees with hardly any resistance. Parliament offers the crown to William and Mary II and passes the Bill of Rights (1689), establishing parliamentary monarchy.

conflictos/revolucion-gloriosa.zonas.des.t: Landing at Torbay and march on London

conflictos/revolucion-haitiana.batallas..t: Dessalines' final victory over the Napoleonic army; independence is proclaimed in January 1804.

conflictos/revolucion-haitiana.descripci.t: The largest slave rebellion in history: Toussaint Louverture and Dessalines defeat France and found the world's first Black republic.

conflictos/revolucion-mexicana.bajas.t: between 1 and 2 million dead (combat, famine and epidemics)

conflictos/revolucion-mexicana.descripci.t: Francisco I. Madero's uprising against the long dictatorship of Porfirio Díaz in 1910 unleashes a decade of civil war. The factions of Pancho Villa, Emiliano Zapata ("Land and Liberty"), Venustiano Carranza and Álvaro Obregón fight for power and land reform. The process culminates in the Constitution of 1917, one of the most advanced of its time.

conflictos/revolucion-rusa.batallas.asal.t: The October Revolution takes Petrograd almost without bloodshed.

conflictos/revolucion-rusa.batallas.defe.t: The future Stalingrad, contested between Reds and Whites.

conflictos/revolucion-rusa.descripcion.t: February topples the tsar, October gives power to the Bolsheviks, and the civil war between Reds and Whites ends with the founding of the USSR (1922).

conflictos/revuelta-campesinos-1381.bata.t: Confrontation at Smithfield (death of Wat Tyler)

conflictos/revuelta-campesinos-1381.desc.t: Popular rebellion against the poll tax and serfdom under Richard II, led by Wat Tyler and John Ball. The rebels of Kent and Essex take London before being crushed; Tyler dies at Smithfield.

conflictos/rif.batallas.desastre-de-annu.t: The collapse of the Melilla command shakes Spain.

conflictos/rif.batallas.desembarco-de-al.t: Joint Spanish-French operation that breaks Abd el-Krim.

conflictos/rif.descripcion.t: Abd el-Krim's Riffian resistance inflicts the Disaster of Annual on Spain (1921); the Alhucemas landing (1925), the first modern amphibious operation, decides the war.

conflictos/segunda-guerra-chino-japonesa.t: Three months of urban fighting before the city falls.
Clash that begins total war in northern China.
Capture of the Chinese capital followed by mass killings of civilians and prisoners.
Full-scale Japanese invasion of China from the Marco Polo Bridge Incident (1937): the Battle of Shanghai, the Nanjing Massacre and a war of attrition that merges into the Second World War.

conflictos/segunda-guerra-congo.bajas.t: millions dead, most from hunger and disease (the IRC's figure of 5.4 million is disputed)

conflictos/segunda-guerra-congo.descripc.t: The “African World War”: nine states and dozens of militias fight in the Congo, the deadliest conflict since 1945.

conflictos/segunda-guerra-italo-etiope.b.t: tens of thousands of Ethiopians (figures disputed); Italy uses mustard gas

conflictos/segunda-guerra-italo-etiope.d.t: Mussolini's Italy invades Ethiopia and incorporates it into Italian East Africa; the League of Nations imposes ineffective sanctions. The occupation lasts until 1941.

conflictos/segunda-punica.batallas.batal.t: ~55,000 Romans killed in a single day
Hannibal's greatest victory, a masterpiece of tactical envelopment.
Scipio Africanus defeats Hannibal and decides the war.

conflictos/segunda-punica.descripcion.t: Hannibal crosses the Alps and invades Italy; Rome ultimately prevails and becomes the dominant power of the western Mediterranean.

conflictos/sengoku.bajas.t: hundreds of thousands dead in a century and a half of civil wars

conflictos/sengoku.batallas.batalla-de-n.t: Nobunaga's arquebuses annihilate the Takeda cavalry.

conflictos/sengoku.batallas.batalla-de-o.t: Nobunaga, with 3,000 men, surprises and destroys 25,000.

conflictos/sengoku.batallas.batalla-de-s.t: Ieyasu wins the battle that decides the fate of Japan.

conflictos/sengoku.batallas.sitio-de-osa.t: The last Toyotomi stronghold falls; 250 years of peace begin.

conflictos/sengoku.descripcion.t: Oda Nobunaga, Toyotomi Hideyoshi and Tokugawa Ieyasu unify the Japan of the “Warring States”; after Sekigahara (1600) and Osaka (1615) comes the Tokugawa peace.

conflictos/siete-anos.batallas.batalla-d.t: Frederick II defeats the Austrians in Silesia (5 December 1757).
Clive wins Bengal for the East India Company.
Frederick II defeats the French and Imperial forces in Saxony (5 November 1757).

conflictos/siete-anos.batallas.toma-de-l.t: Great Britain captures the key to the Spanish Caribbean; it will return it in exchange for Florida.

conflictos/siete-anos.batallas.toma-de-m.t: An expedition from India occupies the Philippine capital.

conflictos/siete-anos.batallas.toma-de-q.t: Wolfe defeats Montcalm; France loses Canada.

conflictos/siete-anos.descripcion.t: The first world war in history: fighting takes place in Europe, America, the Caribbean, India and the Philippines. Great Britain emerges as the leading colonial power; France loses Canada and Spain cedes Florida (recovering Havana and Manila).

conflictos/sucesion-austriaca.batallas.b.t: Allied victory; the last time a British king led troops in person.
French victory of Maurice de Saxe (11 May 1745; coordinates of Antoing, the municipality to which Fontenoy belongs).

conflictos/sucesion-austriaca.descripcio.t: Prussia, France, Spain and Bavaria contest the inheritance of Maria Theresa; Prussia keeps Silesia and the Peace of Aachen (1748) confirms Maria Theresa. The War of Jenkins' Ear between Great Britain and Spain merges into it.

conflictos/sucesion-castellana.batallas..t: Indecisive clash on the field but a political victory for the Catholic Monarchs, who secure Isabella on the throne.

conflictos/sucesion-castellana.descripci.t: Isabella the Catholic and Ferdinand of Aragon against Joanna la Beltraneja and Afonso V of Portugal for the throne of Castile; victory consolidates the Catholic Monarchs.

conflictos/sucesion-espanola.batallas.ba.t: Decisive Bourbon victory on Spanish soil.
Marlborough and Eugene of Savoy defeat France.
Very costly victory of Marlborough and Eugene of Savoy over the French (11 September 1709).
After taking Brihuega, Philip V and Vendôme defeat the Allied army (11 December 1710).
Battle of Huerto de las Bombas

conflictos/sucesion-espanola.batallas.si.t: The city falls to Philip V on 11 September 1714.

conflictos/sucesion-espanola.batallas.to.t: An Anglo-Dutch fleet takes the stronghold in the name of Archduke Charles (1–4 August 1704).

conflictos/sucesion-espanola.descripcion.t: Europe fights over the Spanish crown between Bourbons and Habsburgs.

conflictos/talas.batallas.batalla-del-ri.t: The Abbasids win; end of Tang expansion to the west.

conflictos/talas.descripcion.t: The clash between China and Islam over Central Asia; Chinese prisoners spread the secret of paper to the West.

conflictos/tercera-guerra-sagrada.descri.t: War for control of the sanctuary of Delphi: the Phocians occupied the oracle and plundered its treasury to pay for mercenaries. The intervention of Philip II of Macedon on behalf of the Amphictyony gave him a foothold in Greek politics, foreshadowing his hegemony.

conflictos/tercera-guerra-sagrada.zonas..t: Phocis and the sanctuary of Delphi

conflictos/tercera-punica.batallas.destr.t: The city is razed after the final assault.

conflictos/tercera-punica.descripcion.t: “Delenda est Carthago”: after a three-year siege, Scipio Aemilianus razes Carthage and its territory becomes the province of Africa.

conflictos/treintaanos.batallas.batalla-.t: First great Protestant victory, won by Gustavus II Adolphus.
Imperial and Catholic League troops crush the Bohemian rebels near Prague (8 November 1620); approximate coordinates of the hill of Bílá Hora.
Swedish victory in which Gustavus Adolphus is killed (16 November 1632); coordinates of the town.
Spanish and Imperial forces defeat the Swedes (5–6 September 1634).
France defeats the Spanish tercios; the twilight of their legend.

conflictos/treintaanos.descripcion.t: Religious and political war that devastates Central Europe; it ends with the Peace of Westphalia.

conflictos/tres-reinos.bajas.t: ~36,000,000 according to the censuses (war, famine and epidemics)

conflictos/tres-reinos.batallas.batalla-.t: Cao Cao defeats Yuan Shao and dominates the north.
Cao Cao's fleet burns; China remains divided in three.

conflictos/tres-reinos.descripcion.t: From the Yellow Turban Rebellion (184) to the division of China into three kingdoms and its reunification by Jin (280); the era novelized in the “Romance of the Three Kingdoms”.

conflictos/tres-reinos.nombre.t: Fall of the Han and the Three Kingdoms

conflictos/unificacion-italia.batallas.b.t: Rome drives Pyrrhus out of Italy.
Decisive victory over the Samnite-Gallic coalition.

conflictos/unificacion-italia.descripcio.t: Rome subdues central and southern Italy in the three Samnite Wars (343–290 BC) and defeats Pyrrhus of Epirus (280–275 BC), becoming master of the peninsula.

conflictos/unificacion-qin.bajas.t: hundreds of thousands (the wars of the Warring States were among the bloodiest of Antiquity)

conflictos/unificacion-qin.batallas.caid.t: Qin takes the capital of Zhao.

conflictos/unificacion-qin.batallas.conq.t: The last kingdom surrenders; the Chinese empire is born.

conflictos/unificacion-qin.descripcion.t: Ying Zheng conquers the six rival kingdoms in nine years and proclaims himself Qin Shi Huang, first emperor of China (221 BC).

conflictos/wwi.batallas.batalla-de-capor.t: Italian defeat; the front falls back to the Piave.

conflictos/wwi.batallas.batalla-de-jutla.t: The largest naval battle of the war; the German fleet never again challenges the blockade.

conflictos/wwi.batallas.batalla-de-passc.t: Third Battle of Ypres, a symbol of mud and the war of attrition.

conflictos/wwi.batallas.batalla-de-st-qu.t: Battle of the St. Quentin Canal

conflictos/wwi.batallas.batalla-de-tanne.t: Hindenburg and Ludendorff destroy the Russian Second Army in East Prussia.

conflictos/wwi.batallas.batalla-de-verdu.t: The longest battle of the war: ten months of attrition.

conflictos/wwi.batallas.batalla-del-golf.t: Battle of the Gulf of Riga

conflictos/wwi.batallas.batalla-del-somm.t: 57,000 British casualties on the first day alone.

conflictos/wwi.batallas.galipoli.descrip.t: Allied failure at the Dardanelles against the Ottoman Empire.

conflictos/wwi.batallas.marcha-sobre-hie.t: Ice Cruise of the Baltic Fleet

conflictos/wwi.batallas.ofensiva-brusilo.t: The largest Russian offensive of the war, in Galicia and Volhynia.

conflictos/wwi.batallas.primera-batalla-.t: The Allies halt the German advance on Paris.

conflictos/wwi.batallas.segunda-batalla-.t: Second Battle of the Aisne (Nivelle offensive)

conflictos/wwi.descripcion.t: The Great War: trenches, new weapons and the end of four empires.

conflictos/wwii.batallas.asedio-de-varso.t: Surrender of the Polish capital on 28 September.

conflictos/wwii.batallas.batalla-de-berl.t: The Red Army takes the German capital; end of the war in Europe.

conflictos/wwii.batallas.batalla-de-buch.t: Battle of Buchhof and Stein am Kocher

conflictos/wwii.batallas.batalla-de-kurs.t: The largest tank battle in history; the initiative passes to the USSR.

conflictos/wwii.batallas.batalla-de-las-.t: Last major German offensive in the west (Bastogne).

conflictos/wwii.batallas.batalla-de-mosc.t: First defeat of the Wehrmacht; end of the blitzkrieg in the East.

conflictos/wwii.batallas.batalla-de-stal.t: Turning point on the Eastern Front; the German 6th Army surrenders.

conflictos/wwii.batallas.desembarco-de-n.t: The largest amphibious operation in history opens the Western Front.

conflictos/wwii.batallas.evacuacion-de-d.t: Some 338,000 Allied soldiers evacuated to Great Britain.

conflictos/wwii.batallas.operacion-bagra.t: Destruction of Army Group Center in Belarus.

conflictos/wwii.batallas.sitio-de-lening.t: 872 days of siege (1941–1944), around 800,000 civilians dead.

eventos/1000-coronacion-de-san-esteban-i.t: Stephen I is crowned with a crown sent by the pope, founding the Christian kingdom of Hungary.
Coronation of Stephen I of Hungary

eventos/1000-vinlandia-los-vikingos-lleg.t: Leif Erikson lands in Vinland (L'Anse aux Meadows, Newfoundland): Europeans in America 492 years before Columbus.

eventos/1045-imprenta-de-tipos-moviles-b.t: Bi Sheng invents ceramic movable type (pin at the Song capital, Kaifeng).

eventos/105-el-papel.descripcion.t: Cai Lun perfects paper at the Han court (pin at the capital, Luoyang).

eventos/1050ac-alfabeto-fenicio.descripc.t: In Byblos the alphabet from which the Greek and Latin alphabets descend takes shape.

eventos/1054-gran-cisma-de-oriente-y-occ.t: Rupture between the churches of Rome and Constantinople.

eventos/1077-humillacion-de-canossa.desc.t: Emperor Henry IV waits three days outside the castle of Canossa for Pope Gregory VII to lift his excommunication, in the midst of the Investiture Controversy.

eventos/1088-universidad-de-bolonia.desc.t: The first university in Europe is born.

eventos/1090-brujula-de-navegacion.descr.t: Song China applies the magnetized needle to navigation (pin at Kaifeng).

eventos/1150-construccion-de-angkor-wat..t: King Suryavarman II builds at Angkor the largest religious complex in the world, dedicated to the Hindu god Vishnu and later converted into a Buddhist temple. It is the pinnacle of the art of the Khmer Empire and today a symbol of Cambodia.

eventos/1180ac-colapso-de-la-edad-del-br.t: Between 1200 and 1150 BC (approximate date), the Hittite Empire, the Mycenaean kingdoms and Ugarit fall; Egypt survives, weakened. The causes (Sea Peoples, drought, internal crises) are still debated. Marker at Mycenae.

eventos/1200ac-san-lorenzo-primer-centro.t: Between 1200 and 900 BC (approximate dates), the first great Olmec center flourishes at San Lorenzo, on the Gulf of Mexico, famous for its colossal heads.

eventos/1215-carta-magna.descripcion.t: King John agrees to limit royal power at Runnymede.

eventos/1250ac-huesos-oraculares-de-yinx.t: Around the 13th century BC (reign of Wu Ding, c. 1250–1191 BC), at Yin, the last Shang capital (Anyang), divinatory inscriptions are carved on bones and shells; they are the oldest known Chinese writing.

eventos/1259ac-tratado-de-kadesh-el-trat.t: Ramesses II and Hattusili III sign the oldest surviving peace treaty preserved in the versions of both parties, Egyptian and Hittite; the earlier treaty between Ebla and Abarsal might dispute the title. A copy is displayed at UN headquarters.
Treaty of Kadesh, the oldest surviving peace treaty

eventos/1300ac-escritura-lineal-b-miceni.t: Mycenaean civilization uses the Linear B syllabic script, the oldest known record of the Greek language, attested on the tablets of Pylos, Mycenae and Knossos.

eventos/130ac-apertura-de-la-ruta-de-la-.t: The missions of the diplomat Zhang Qian under Emperor Wu open the trade routes connecting China with Central Asia, Persia and the Mediterranean.

eventos/1324-peregrinacion-de-mansa-musa.t: The emperor of Mali crosses Africa with so much gold that he depresses its price in Cairo for years: European maps begin to show Timbuktu.

eventos/1325-fundacion-de-tenochtitlan.d.t: The Mexica found their city on an islet in Lake Texcoco (traditional date); a century later it will be the head of the Triple Alliance.

eventos/1347-peste-negra.descripcion.t: The pandemic enters Europe through Messina (Sicily), aboard Genoese galleys, and kills a third of the population.

eventos/1378-cisma-de-occidente.descripc.t: Rival popes in Rome and Avignon (and from 1409 also in Pisa) divide Latin Christendom until the Council of Constance (1417).

eventos/1397-union-de-kalmar.descripcion.t: Margaret I unites Denmark, Norway and Sweden under a single monarch; the union lasts until the election of Gustav Vasa in 1523.

eventos/1405-viajes-de-zheng-he.descripc.t: The fleets of Admiral Zheng He set sail from Liujiagang; in seven voyages (1405–1433) they reach India, Hormuz and the east coast of Africa.

eventos/1412-compromiso-de-caspe.descrip.t: Nine arbiters from Aragon, Catalonia and Valencia elect Ferdinand of Antequera as king: the Castilian Trastámaras accede to the Aragonese throne.

eventos/1450-imprenta-de-gutenberg.descr.t: Gutenberg prints the 42-line Bible in Mainz.

eventos/1469-boda-de-isabel-y-fernando.d.t: Isabella of Castile and Ferdinand of Aragon marry in Valladolid; the dynastic union of both crowns would follow in 1479.

eventos/1492-expulsion-de-los-judios-de-.t: The Alhambra Decree forces Jews to convert or leave; tens of thousands of Sephardim emigrate to Portugal, North Africa and the Ottoman Empire.
Expulsion of the Jews from Castile and Aragon

eventos/1494-tratado-de-tordesillas.desc.t: Castile and Portugal divide the zones of navigation and conquest between them.

eventos/1498-vasco-da-gama-llega-a-la-in.t: After rounding the Cape of Good Hope, Vasco da Gama's fleet reaches Calicut on 20 May 1498: the first direct sea route between Europe and Asia.

eventos/1517-lutero-publica-las-95-tesis.t: In Wittenberg, Luther criticizes the sale of indulgences; the Protestant Reformation begins.

eventos/1517-selim-i-y-el-califato-del-i.t: Selim I conquers Cairo, ends the Mamluk Sultanate and takes the last Abbasid caliph, al-Mutawakkil III, to Istanbul. That the latter then ceded the caliphate to him is a later tradition with no contemporary evidence (it is first documented in writing in 1790); the sultans would only use the title of caliph systematically from the 18th century, as recognized in the Treaty of Küçük Kaynarca (1774).
Selim I and the caliphate of Islam

eventos/1519-primera-vuelta-al-mundo.des.t: The Magellan–Elcano expedition departs from and returns to Sanlúcar de Barrameda.

eventos/1534-cisma-anglicano-ruptura-de-.t: The Act of Supremacy declares Henry VIII Supreme Head of the Church of England, breaking with the papacy after its refusal to annul his marriage to Catherine of Aragon.
English Reformation: Henry VIII breaks with Rome

eventos/1543-copernico-publica-de-revolu.t: Copernicus's heliocentric model is printed in Nuremberg, the starting point of the Scientific Revolution.

eventos/1543-llegada-de-los-portugueses-.t: Shipwrecked Portuguese sailors introduce firearms to Japan, transforming Sengoku warfare.
Arrival of the Portuguese at Tanegashima

eventos/1545-concilio-de-trento.descripc.t: The council (1545–1563) defines Catholic doctrine in response to the Reformation: it is the core of the Counter-Reformation.

eventos/1555-paz-de-augsburgo.descripcio.t: Each prince of the Empire decides the religion of his territory (cuius regio, eius religio), choosing between Catholicism and Lutheranism.

eventos/1587-edicto-de-expulsion-de-misi.t: Hideyoshi orders the expulsion of the Jesuit missionaries, the beginning of the persecution of Christianity.

eventos/1587-ejecucion-de-maria-reina-de.t: Mary Stuart is beheaded at Fotheringhay Castle on the orders of Elizabeth I, accused of conspiring against the English crown.
Execution of Mary, Queen of Scots

eventos/1588-caza-de-espadas-de-hideyosh.t: Disarmament of peasants and monks that fixes the separation between samurai and non-samurai.

eventos/1598-edicto-de-nantes.descripcio.t: Henry IV grants rights to the Huguenots and ends the Wars of Religion.

eventos/1609-expulsion-de-los-moriscos.d.t: Philip III decrees the expulsion of the Moriscos (1609–1614), beginning with the Kingdom of Valencia.

eventos/1620-padres-peregrinos-el-mayflo.t: A group of Separatist Puritans sails from Plymouth on the Mayflower and founds Plymouth Colony in North America, a milestone in the English colonization of New England.
Pilgrim Fathers: the Mayflower to New England

eventos/1635-sistema-de-asistencia-alter.t: The daimyo are required to reside in Edo in alternating periods, binding the nobility to Tokugawa power.

eventos/1639-cierre-del-pais-sakoku.desc.t: The Tokugawa close Japan to the outside world and eradicate Christianity; only Dejima (Nagasaki) remains open to the Dutch.

eventos/1648-paz-de-westfalia.descripcio.t: End of the Thirty Years' War; the order of sovereign states is born.

eventos/1649-ejecucion-de-carlos-i.descr.t: Charles I is beheaded outside Whitehall after being tried by Parliament; the monarchy is abolished and the Commonwealth of England is proclaimed.

eventos/1659-paz-de-los-pirineos.descrip.t: Signed on Pheasant Island: Spain cedes Roussillon and Cerdagne, and France becomes the hegemonic power.

eventos/1687-newton-publica-los-principi.t: The law of universal gravitation and the laws of motion crown the Scientific Revolution.

eventos/1699-tratado-de-karlowitz.descri.t: First major Ottoman territorial cession: after its defeat in the Great Turkish War, the empire hands Hungary to the Habsburgs and Podolia to Poland. It marks the beginning of the Ottoman retreat in Europe.

eventos/1700ac-palacio-minoico-de-cnosos.t: The palace of Knossos is the center of Minoan civilization, the first palatial culture of Europe and protagonist of the Cretan thalassocracy in the Bronze Age Aegean.

eventos/1703-fundacion-de-san-petersburg.t: Peter I founds the new capital on the Neva, his “window to Europe”.

eventos/1707-acta-de-union-nace-el-reino.t: The parliaments of England and Scotland merge through the Acts of Union of 1707, creating the Kingdom of Great Britain under Queen Anne.
Acts of Union: birth of the Kingdom of Great Britain

eventos/1713-tratado-de-utrecht.descripc.t: End of the War of the Spanish Succession: Spain loses Gibraltar, Minorca, Flanders and Italy; Great Britain obtains the slave asiento and the navío de permiso (permission ship).

eventos/1754ac-codigo-de-hammurabi.descr.t: King Hammurabi has nearly 300 laws engraved on a basalt stele under the principle of retaliation ("an eye for an eye"): one of the first great legal codes in history, now in the Louvre.

eventos/1755-terremoto-de-lisboa.descrip.t: The earthquake and tsunami of 1 November devastate Lisbon; Pombal directs the reconstruction and the disaster fuels Enlightenment debate.

eventos/1769-maquina-de-vapor-de-watt.de.t: James Watt patents his steam engine in Glasgow; the Industrial Revolution takes off.

eventos/1774-tratado-de-kucuk-kaynarca.d.t: It ends the Russo-Turkish War of 1768–1774: Crimea becomes independent (a prelude to its Russian annexation) and Russia obtains rights of protection over the empire's Orthodox Christians.

eventos/1776-declaracion-de-independenci.t: On 4 July, in Philadelphia, the Thirteen Colonies declare their independence.

eventos/1783-hambruna-de-tenmei.descripc.t: Bad harvests and the eruption of Mount Asama cause one of the worst famines of the Edo period.

eventos/1789-declaracion-de-los-derechos.t: The National Assembly, at Versailles, proclaims equality before the law and national sovereignty (26 August).
Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen

eventos/1789-toma-de-la-bastilla.descrip.t: The French Revolution breaks out on 14 July 1789.

eventos/1796-la-vacuna-jenner.descripcio.t: Edward Jenner vaccinates against smallpox in Berkeley (England).

eventos/1800-acta-de-union-con-irlanda.d.t: The Act of Union of 1800 merges Great Britain and Ireland into the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland, in force from 1801.

eventos/1803-compra-de-luisiana.descripc.t: France, which had just received Louisiana from Spain, sells it to the United States; the transfer takes place at the Cabildo in New Orleans.

eventos/1804-coronacion-de-napoleon.desc.t: Napoleon crowns himself Emperor of the French in Notre-Dame (2 December).

eventos/1804-independencia-de-haiti.desc.t: On 1 January, in Gonaïves, Dessalines proclaims the independence of former Saint-Domingue: the first Black republic and the second independent state in the Americas.

eventos/1810-grito-de-dolores.descripcio.t: The priest Hidalgo calls for insurrection on 16 September and the Mexican War of Independence begins.

eventos/1812-constitucion-de-cadiz.descr.t: “La Pepa”, the first Spanish constitution, promulgated on 19 March 1812.

eventos/1814-congreso-de-viena.descripci.t: The powers reorganize Europe after Napoleon.

eventos/1825-el-ferrocarril-de-vapor.des.t: The Stockton–Darlington line inaugurates the public steam railway.

eventos/1826-abolicion-del-cuerpo-de-los.t: Mahmud II forcibly liquidates the Janissaries, the feared elite infantry that had become a brake on reform. The 'Auspicious Incident' paves the way for the modernization of the Ottoman army.

eventos/1830-ley-de-traslado-forzoso-de-.t: The US Congress authorizes the deportation of the Southeastern nations to west of the Mississippi.

eventos/1831-sendero-de-lagrimas.descrip.t: Thousands of Cherokee, Creek, Chickasaw, Choctaw and Seminole die in the forced deportation.

eventos/1833-abolicion-de-la-esclavitud..t: From the British Empire (1833) to the United States (1865) and Brazil (1888, the last in the Americas): half a century to dismantle legal Atlantic slavery.

eventos/1839-edicto-de-gulhane-inicio-de.t: The Edict of Gülhane inaugurates the Tanzimat, a period of reforms that seeks to modernize the administration, guarantee rights to all subjects and westernize the empire's institutions.
Edict of Gülhane: start of the Tanzimat

eventos/1844-el-telegrafo-morse.descripc.t: “What hath God wrought”: the first Washington–Baltimore message.

eventos/1848-fiebre-del-oro-de-californi.t: Gold at Sutter's Mill accelerates the settlement of the West and the dispossession of Native lands.

eventos/1848-manifiesto-comunista.descri.t: Marx and Engels publish in London the programme of the Communist League.

eventos/1848-revoluciones-de-1848-primav.t: A liberal and nationalist revolutionary wave that begins in Paris in February and spreads to Vienna, Berlin, Milan and Budapest; Metternich falls.

eventos/1853-llegada-del-comodoro-perry-.t: Matthew Perry's American fleet forces the opening of Japan to foreign trade.
Arrival of Commodore Perry (the Black Ships)

eventos/1861-proclamacion-del-reino-de-i.t: The Parliament in Turin proclaims Victor Emmanuel II King of Italy (17 March).
Proclamation of the Kingdom of Italy

eventos/1865-abolicion-de-la-esclavitud-.t: Ratified in December 1865, at the end of the Civil War.
Abolition of slavery in the U.S. (Thirteenth Amendment)

eventos/1868-juramento-de-la-carta.descr.t: The new Meiji government proclaims the reformist principles that will guide modernization.

eventos/1868-restauracion-meiji.descripc.t: Japan dismantles the shogunate and industrializes within a generation: from closed country to world power.

eventos/1868-revolucion-de-1868-la-glori.t: A military pronunciamiento launched in Cádiz that dethrones Isabella II and opens the Democratic Sexennium.

eventos/1869-apertura-del-canal-de-suez..t: It links the Mediterranean and the Red Sea and shortens the route to India.

eventos/1871-comuna-de-paris.descripcion.t: Revolutionary government from March to May, crushed in the “Bloody Week”.

eventos/1871-mision-iwakura.descripcion.t: Grand embassy of Meiji leaders to the US and Europe to study their institutions and technology.

eventos/1871-proclamacion-del-imperio-al.t: William I is proclaimed emperor in the Hall of Mirrors (18 January).
Proclamation of the German Empire at Versailles

eventos/1873-proclamacion-de-la-primera-.t: After the abdication of Amadeo I, the Cortes proclaim the First Republic; it lasted less than two years.
Proclamation of the First Spanish Republic

eventos/1876-el-telefono-bell.descripcio.t: Bell patents the telephone in Boston.

eventos/1876-primera-constitucion-otoman.t: Under Abdul Hamid II the first constitution (Kanun-i Esasi) is promulgated and a short-lived parliament opens, soon suspended by the sultan. It is the first attempt at an Ottoman constitutional monarchy.

eventos/1876-tratado-de-ganghwa.descripc.t: Japan imposes an unequal treaty on Korea, the first step in its continental expansion.

eventos/1876-victoria-proclamada-emperat.t: The Royal Titles Act grants Queen Victoria the title of Empress of India, a symbol of the height of British imperial power.

eventos/1878-congreso-de-berlin.descripc.t: The powers reorganize the Balkans after the Russo-Turkish War of 1877–1878: Serbia, Romania and Montenegro become independent, Bulgaria becomes autonomous and the empire loses influence in southeastern Europe.

eventos/1879-la-bombilla-edison.descripc.t: At Menlo Park, Edison achieves a long-lasting incandescent lamp.

eventos/1884-conferencia-de-berlin-el-re.t: The European powers carve up Africa with ruler and set square, without a single African at the table.
Berlin Conference: the Scramble for Africa

eventos/1886-el-automovil-benz.descripci.t: Karl Benz patents the first gasoline-powered automobile in Mannheim.

eventos/1889-constitucion-meiji.descripc.t: Japan's first modern constitution is promulgated, establishing an empire with a parliamentary Diet.

eventos/1899-ley-de-proteccion-de-antigu.t: Policy of forced assimilation of the Ainu people under the Meiji state.

eventos/1903-el-avion-hermanos-wright.de.t: First controlled powered flight, at Kitty Hawk.

eventos/1908-revolucion-de-los-jovenes-t.t: The Young Turk movement forces Abdul Hamid II to restore the 1876 constitution and the parliament. It opens a period of Turkish nationalism and growing militarization of the regime.

eventos/1912-proclamacion-de-la-republic.t: The Xinhai Revolution overthrows the Qing dynasty and ends more than two millennia of empire; the Republic of China is born.
Proclamation of the Republic of China

eventos/1914-asesinato-de-francisco-fern.t: On 28 June, the trigger of the First World War.
Assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo

eventos/1915-las-veintiuna-demandas-a-ch.t: Japan demands broad economic and political concessions from China, straining relations in Asia.

eventos/1916-acuerdo-sykes-picot.descrip.t: The United Kingdom and France secretly divide the Arab provinces of the Ottoman Empire into zones of influence, laying the foundations of the map of the Middle East after the First World War.

eventos/1919-tratado-de-versalles.descri.t: Peace with Germany: war guilt, reparations, loss of Alsace-Lorraine and of the colonies; it creates the League of Nations.

eventos/1920-tratado-de-sevres.descripci.t: The treaty imposes the dismemberment of the Ottoman Empire: French and British mandates over the Arab provinces, cessions to Greece and Italy and a reduced Turkey. Turkish nationalist rejection would render it a dead letter.

eventos/1921-fundacion-del-partido-comun.t: The 1st Congress of the Communist Party of China is held in Shanghai, with Mao Zedong among its founding delegates.
Founding of the Chinese Communist Party

eventos/1922-abolicion-del-sultanato.des.t: The Grand National Assembly led by Mustafa Kemal abolishes the sultanate; the last sultan, Mehmed VI, flees Istanbul. Thus ends a dynasty that had reigned for more than six centuries.

eventos/1922-marcha-sobre-roma.descripci.t: Victor Emmanuel III entrusts the government to Mussolini.

eventos/1923-golpe-de-estado-de-primo-de.t: A military pronunciamiento that establishes the dictatorship of the Military Directory and suspends the parliamentary system.

eventos/1923-gran-terremoto-de-kanto.des.t: A devastating earthquake destroys Tokyo and Yokohama, causing more than 100,000 deaths.

eventos/1923-proclamacion-de-la-republic.t: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk proclaims the Republic of Turkey with its capital in Ankara, definitively closing the Ottoman imperial era and founding the modern Turkish state.
Proclamation of the Republic of Turkey

eventos/1928-la-penicilina-fleming.descr.t: Fleming discovers penicillin in his London laboratory.

eventos/1929-crac-del-29.descripcion.t: Collapse of the New York Stock Exchange (24–29 October), the beginning of the Great Depression.

eventos/1931-constitucion-republicana-de.t: A constitution that establishes women's suffrage, a secular state and broad freedoms.

eventos/1931-proclamacion-de-la-segunda-.t: On 14 April 1931, after the municipal elections, the Second Republic is proclaimed and Alfonso XIII leaves the country.
Proclamation of the Second Spanish Republic

eventos/1932-creacion-de-manchukuo.descr.t: Japan sets up a puppet state in Manchuria with the last Qing emperor, Puyi, as its nominal figurehead.

eventos/1933-hitler-canciller-de-alemani.t: Hindenburg appoints Hitler chancellor on 30 January; within months the Weimar Republic is dismantled.

eventos/1941-ataque-a-pearl-harbor.descr.t: The Japanese attack on the naval base in Hawaii drags the United States into the Second World War.

eventos/1941-holocausto.descripcion.t: Systematic extermination of some six million European Jews by Nazi Germany; the marker is at Auschwitz-Birkenau.

eventos/1945-bombardeo-atomico-de-hirosh.t: The first atomic bomb used in war destroys Hiroshima on 6 August 1945.

eventos/1945-bombardeo-atomico-de-nagasa.t: The second atomic bomb destroys Nagasaki on 9 August 1945, hastening the surrender.

eventos/1945-conferencia-de-yalta.descri.t: Roosevelt, Churchill and Stalin agree on the post-war order (February).

eventos/1945-fundacion-de-la-onu.descrip.t: The Charter is signed in San Francisco on 26 June.

eventos/1945-rendicion-de-japon.descripc.t: Japan capitulates (15 Aug / signed 2 Sep 1945), ending the Second World War.

eventos/1947-el-transistor.descripcion.t: Bell Labs creates the transistor, the basis of all modern electronics.

eventos/1947-ocupacion-aliada-y-constitu.t: Under US occupation, Japan adopts a pacifist constitution whose Article 9 renounces war.

eventos/1947-particion-de-la-india.descr.t: Independence and partition into India and Pakistan: ~15 million displaced and up to a million dead in the largest forced migration in history.

eventos/1948-declaracion-universal-de-lo.t: Adopted by the UN General Assembly in Paris (10 December).

eventos/1949-fundacion-de-la-otan.descri.t: North Atlantic Treaty, signed in Washington on 4 April.

eventos/1949-proclamacion-de-la-republic.t: On 1 October 1949 Mao Zedong proclaims the People's Republic of China from Tiananmen Gate, after the communist victory in the civil war.
Proclamation of the People's Republic of China

eventos/1951-acuerdo-de-los-17-puntos.de.t: Signed in Beijing on 23 May 1951 by delegates of the Lhasa government after the Tibetan defeat at Qamdo, it incorporates Tibet into the People's Republic of China, which presents it as the “peaceful liberation of Tibet”.

eventos/1956-crisis-de-suez.descripcion.t: Nasser nationalizes the canal; the Anglo-French expedition fails under pressure from the US and the USSR: the symbolic end of the European empires.

eventos/1956-enfermedad-de-minamata.desc.t: Mass mercury poisoning from waste dumped into Minamata Bay, a milestone in environmental awareness.

eventos/1957-tratados-de-roma-cee.descri.t: Six countries found the European Economic Community and Euratom.

eventos/1958-gran-salto-adelante.descrip.t: A campaign of collectivization and accelerated industrialization driven by Mao (1958–1960) that caused a mass famine.

eventos/1959-plan-de-estabilizacion-de-1.t: The Franco regime's economic turn towards liberalism, which opens the 'developmentalism' of the 1960s.

eventos/1959-revolucion-cubana.descripci.t: Batista flees on 1 January; Fidel Castro takes power.

eventos/1960-ano-de-africa.descripcion.t: Seventeen African countries become independent in a single year.

eventos/1961-construccion-del-muro-de-be.t: The GDR builds the wall on 13 August 1961; it falls on 9 November 1989.

eventos/1962-crisis-de-los-misiles-de-cu.t: Thirteen days on the brink of nuclear war: the Soviet missiles are withdrawn in exchange for the American ones in Turkey.

eventos/1964-primera-bomba-atomica-china.t: On 16 October 1964 China detonates its first atomic bomb at Lop Nur, becoming the fifth nuclear power.

eventos/1966-revolucion-cultural-china.d.t: Mao unleashes the Red Guards against the “Four Olds”: a decade of purges and chaos with between half a million and two million dead.

eventos/1967-primera-bomba-de-hidrogeno-.t: On 17 June 1967 China successfully tests its first thermonuclear bomb at Lop Nur.

eventos/1968-mayo-del-68.descripcion.t: Student revolt and general strike in France.

eventos/1969-llegada-del-hombre-a-la-lun.t: Apollo 11 lifts off from Cape Canaveral; Armstrong sets foot on the Moon on 20 July.

eventos/1970-primer-satelite-artificial-.t: On 24 April 1970 China launches its first satellite, Dong Fang Hong 1, from Jiuquan, entering the space race.
First Chinese artificial satellite (Dong Fang Hong 1)

eventos/1974-revolucion-de-los-claveles..t: The Estado Novo dictatorship falls (25 April) and Portuguese decolonization begins.

eventos/1975-muerte-de-franco.descripcio.t: On 20 November 1975 Francisco Franco dies, giving way to the democratic Transition.

eventos/1976-muerte-de-mao-y-caida-de-la.t: The death of Mao Zedong and the arrest of the Gang of Four end the Cultural Revolution and open the way to Reform and Opening Up.
Death of Mao and fall of the Gang of Four

eventos/1977-pactos-de-la-moncloa.descri.t: Agreements between the Government, the opposition and the social partners to tackle the economic crisis and consolidate democracy.

eventos/1978-constitucion-espanola-de-19.t: It establishes the parliamentary monarchy and the State of Autonomies, the basis of the current democratic regime.

eventos/1978-inicio-de-la-reforma-y-aper.t: The Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee, led by Deng Xiaoping, launches the Reform and Opening Up policy that transforms the Chinese economy.
Start of Reform and Opening Up (Third Plenum of the CCP)

eventos/1980-zonas-economicas-especiales.t: China creates the first Special Economic Zones (Shenzhen, Zhuhai, Shantou and Xiamen), engines of the opening to foreign capital.

eventos/1981-golpe-de-estado-del-23-f.de.t: Coup attempt by Lieutenant Colonel Tejero in the Congress of Deputies, thwarted within a few hours.

eventos/1986-adhesion-de-espana-a-la-cee.t: On 1 January 1986 Spain joins the European Economic Community (today the European Union) together with Portugal.
Accession of Spain to the EEC

eventos/1989-caida-del-muro-de-berlin.de.t: On 9 November 1989 the Wall falls; the symbolic end of the Cold War.

eventos/1989-la-world-wide-web.descripci.t: Tim Berners-Lee proposes the web at CERN (Geneva).

eventos/1990-reunificacion-alemana.descr.t: The GDR joins the FRG on 3 October.

eventos/1991-disolucion-de-la-union-sovi.t: Gorbachev resigns on 25 December and the USSR dissolves; fifteen independent republics are born.

eventos/1994-fin-del-apartheid.descripci.t: Nelson Mandela, imprisoned for 27 years, wins South Africa's first free elections and buries apartheid.

eventos/1997-retorno-de-hong-kong-a-chin.t: On 1 July 1997 the United Kingdom returns Hong Kong to China, where it becomes a Special Administrative Region under the principle of 'one country, two systems'.
Handover of Hong Kong to China

eventos/1999-retorno-de-macao-a-china.de.t: On 20 December 1999 Portugal returns Macau to China, where it becomes a Special Administrative Region.

eventos/2001-adhesion-de-china-a-la-omc..t: On 11 December 2001 China joins the World Trade Organization, accelerating its integration into the global economy.
Accession of China to the WTO

eventos/2001-atentados-del-11-de-septiem.t: Al-Qaeda crashes two planes into the Twin Towers and one into the Pentagon, and another comes down in Pennsylvania; nearly 3,000 dead.

eventos/2008-crisis-financiera-de-2008.d.t: The bankruptcy of Lehman Brothers (15 September) triggers the Great Recession.

eventos/2008-juegos-olimpicos-de-beijing.t: Beijing hosts the 2008 Summer Olympic Games, a showcase of China's rise as a global power.

eventos/2010-exposicion-universal-de-sha.t: Shanghai hosts the 2010 World Expo, one of the largest in history by number of visitors.

eventos/2010-primavera-arabe.descripcion.t: The self-immolation of Mohamed Bouazizi in Tunisia sparks a wave of revolts that topples regimes in Tunisia, Egypt and Libya.

eventos/2011-accidente-nuclear-de-fukush.t: An earthquake and tsunami (~19,000 dead) cause the worst nuclear accident since Chernobyl.

eventos/2011-terremoto-y-tsunami-de-toho.t: A megathrust earthquake and tsunami devastate northeastern Japan and trigger the Fukushima disaster.

eventos/2012-descubrimiento-del-boson-de.t: CERN's LHC confirms the particle that gives mass to the others, half a century after it was predicted.

eventos/2013-iniciativa-de-la-franja-y-l.t: Xi Jinping launches the Belt and Road Initiative, a vast programme of infrastructure and connectivity on a Eurasian and global scale.

eventos/2014-abdicacion-de-juan-carlos-i.t: After 39 years on the throne, he abdicates in favour of his son, proclaimed Felipe VI on 19 June.

eventos/2015-acuerdo-de-paris-sobre-el-c.t: 195 countries agree to limit global warming to “well below” 2 °C.

eventos/2015-primera-deteccion-de-ondas-.t: LIGO detects the merger of two black holes, a hundred years after Einstein predicted gravitational waves.

eventos/2016-brexit.descripcion.t: The United Kingdom votes to leave the European Union (2016) and leaves it on 31 January 2020.

eventos/2019-primera-imagen-de-un-agujer.t: The Event Horizon Telescope photographs the black hole in the galaxy M87 (unveiled in Brussels, Munich and other venues).
First image of a black hole

eventos/2020-pandemia-de-covid-19.descri.t: Detected in Wuhan at the end of 2019, SARS-CoV-2 causes ~7 million confirmed deaths (and an estimated ~20+ million) and brings the planet to a standstill; the WHO ends the emergency in May 2023.

eventos/2021-erupcion-del-volcan-de-la-p.t: 85 days of eruption at Cumbre Vieja: ~3,000 buildings buried by lava.

eventos/2021-lanzamiento-del-telescopio-.t: The largest space telescope in history lifts off from Kourou on 25 December.
Launch of the James Webb Space Telescope

eventos/2022-ia-generativa-chatgpt.descr.t: The launch of ChatGPT popularizes generative artificial intelligence: 100 million users in two months.

eventos/2022-muerte-de-isabel-ii.descrip.t: She dies after a 70-year reign, the longest in British history; she is succeeded by Charles III.

eventos/2024-dana-de-valencia.descripcio.t: The floods of 29 October cause ~230 deaths, the worst natural disaster in Spain in decades.

eventos/210ac-ejercito-de-terracota-de-q.t: Thousands of life-size terracotta warriors guard the mausoleum of the First Emperor near Xi'an; they were discovered in 1974.
Terracotta Army of Qin Shi Huang

eventos/212-constitutio-antoniniana.desc.t: Caracalla's edict (212) grants Roman citizenship to almost all free men of the Empire, unifying their legal status.

eventos/213ac-quema-de-libros-y-entierro.t: Chancellor Li Si promotes the destruction of texts and the persecution of scholars to impose the Legalist orthodoxy of the Qin Empire.
Burning of books and burying of scholars (Qin)

eventos/214ac-gran-muralla-china-bajo-qi.t: After unifying China, the first emperor Qin Shi Huang orders the northern frontier walls to be linked and extended to hold back the steppe peoples. Successive dynasties would rebuild it; most of the stonework visible today dates from the Ming period. (The marker is on a Ming-era section: the exact course of the Qin walls is unknown.)
Great Wall of China (under Qin Shi Huang)

eventos/238-ano-de-los-seis-emperadores..t: In the year 238 six emperors follow one another (Maximinus, Gordian I and II, Pupienus, Balbinus and Gordian III), a symptom of the military anarchy that ushers in the Crisis of the Third Century.

eventos/2560ac-gran-piramide-de-guiza.de.t: The tomb of Khufu, the only wonder of the ancient world still standing, was the tallest structure on Earth for 3,800 years.

eventos/2650ac-piramide-escalonada-de-sa.t: Imhotep raises for Djoser the world's first great building of cut stone.

eventos/280ac-faro-de-alejandria.descrip.t: The Ptolemies raise on the island of Pharos the tower that gave its name to all lighthouses: another wonder of the ancient world.

eventos/283ac-biblioteca-y-museion-de-al.t: The first Ptolemies found in Alexandria the Mouseion and its Library, the greatest center of learning in the Hellenistic world, which aspired to gather all known books and where scholars such as Euclid, Eratosthenes and Aristarchus worked.

eventos/293-tetrarquia-de-diocleciano.de.t: Diocletian divides the government of the Empire between two Augusti (himself in Nicomedia and Maximian in Milan) and two Caesars (Galerius in Sirmium and Constantius in Trier) to better defend its frontiers.

eventos/3000ac-el-arado.descripcion.t: The ox-drawn plow revolutionizes Mesopotamian agriculture (pin at Ur).

eventos/3000ac-unificacion-de-egipto.des.t: Around 3150–3100 BC (on the timeline, in 3000 BC), Narmer (Menes) unites Upper and Lower Egypt and founds Memphis.

eventos/301-armenia-adopta-el-cristianis.t: King Tiridates III, converted by Gregory the Illuminator, makes Christianity the religion of the kingdom of Armenia, the first state to adopt it officially (the traditional date is 301; some authors propose 314). Marker at Etchmiadzin.

eventos/313-edicto-de-milan.descripcion.t: Constantine and Licinius grant freedom of worship to Christians.

eventos/320-chandragupta-i-funda-el-impe.t: Chandragupta I is crowned at Pataliputra with the title of maharajadhiraja; with his son Samudragupta the Gupta Empire is born, the “golden age” of classical India.
Chandragupta I founds the Gupta Empire

eventos/3200ac-escritura-cuneiforme.desc.t: The first known writing is born in Uruk, on clay tablets.

eventos/323ac-muerte-de-alejandro-magno..t: Alexander dies in Babylon, in the palace of Nebuchadnezzar II, at the age of 32. His generals (the Diadochi) divide the empire among themselves.

eventos/330-inauguracion-de-constantinop.t: On 11 May Constantine inaugurates the new capital on the site of ancient Byzantium, with forty days of festivities in the Hippodrome. It will be the capital of the Eastern Roman Empire for more than a thousand years.

eventos/331ac-fundacion-de-alejandria.de.t: Alexander the Great lays out, on the coast of the Nile Delta, the city that will bear his name and become the capital of the Ptolemies and a great cultural center of the Hellenistic world.

eventos/3500ac-la-rueda.descripcion.t: The first potter's wheels and cart wheels appear in Mesopotamia (pin at Uruk).

eventos/380-edicto-de-tesalonica.descrip.t: On 27 February, Theodosius, Gratian and Valentinian II proclaim Nicene Christianity the official religion of the Roman Empire.

eventos/395-division-definitiva-del-impe.t: On the death of Theodosius I, the empire is divided between Honorius (West) and Arcadius (East).
Final division of the Roman Empire

eventos/447ac-construccion-del-partenon..t: On the Acropolis of Athens the Parthenon is built, a Doric temple dedicated to Athena Parthenos, symbol of the city's political and artistic zenith in the time of Pericles.

eventos/44ac-asesinato-de-julio-cesar.de.t: On the Ides of March, a group of senators led by Brutus and Cassius stab Caesar in the curia of the Theater of Pompey. His death, far from saving the Republic, opens the civil war that will bring Augustus to power.

eventos/4ac-nacimiento-de-jesus-de-nazar.t: Birth of Jesus of Nazareth in the kingdom of Judea, a client of Rome. Approximate and disputed date: historians place it between 7 and 4 BC; the marker is at Bethlehem, the place given by tradition. He died in Jerusalem around AD 30–33.

eventos/500ac-confucio-y-las-cien-escuel.t: Confucius (551–479 BC) teaches, in the China of the Spring and Autumn period, an ethic of duty, respect and social harmony. Around him flourish the great currents of Chinese thought (Confucianism, Taoism, Mohism and Legalism), the basis for more than two millennia of politics, family and administration in East Asia.
Confucius and the Hundred Schools of Thought

eventos/508ac-democracia-ateniense-de-cl.t: Cleisthenes reorganizes the citizens into ten territorial tribes, establishes isonomy and ostracism, and consolidates government by the assembly. It is considered the birth of Athenian democracy.

eventos/528ac-nacimiento-del-budismo.des.t: According to tradition, Siddhartha Gautama attains enlightenment under the Bodhi tree at Bodh Gaya and becomes the Buddha. His teaching on suffering and how to overcome it will give rise to one of the world's great religions. (Traditional date; many scholars place the Buddha's life around 480–400 BC.)

eventos/529-regla-de-san-benito-y-fundac.t: Saint Benedict founds Monte Cassino and writes his Rule, the foundation of Western monasticism.
Rule of Saint Benedict and founding of Monte Cassino

eventos/537-consagracion-de-santa-sofia..t: Justinian inaugurates the new basilica of Hagia Sophia in Constantinople, built in less than six years after the Nika riots; its dome on pendentives will be a model for centuries.

eventos/587ac-cautiverio-de-babilonia.de.t: Nebuchadnezzar II destroys Jerusalem and its Temple and deports a large part of the Jewish people to Babylon. The exile, which lasts until the Persian conquest of 539 BC, deeply shapes Jewish religion and identity.

eventos/589-iii-concilio-de-toledo.descr.t: Reccared renounces Arianism and converts the Visigoths to Catholicism, unifying Hispania religiously.

eventos/594ac-reformas-de-solon.descripc.t: Solon, appointed archon of Athens, abolished debt slavery (seisachtheia), organized society into property classes (timocracy) and created the Boule, laying the institutional foundations that would lead to democracy.

eventos/600ac-la-moneda-acunada.descripc.t: Lydia mints the first electrum coins (pin at its capital, Sardis).

eventos/604-constitucion-de-los-diecisie.t: Prince Shōtoku promulgates moral and bureaucratic principles of government of Confucian and Buddhist inspiration.

eventos/609-gran-canal-de-china-dinastia.t: The Sui dynasty builds the largest canal of the ancient world, linking northern and southern China and forming the backbone of its economy for centuries.

eventos/622-hegira.descripcion.t: Muhammad emigrates from Mecca to Medina; beginning of the Muslim calendar.

eventos/64-gran-incendio-de-roma.descrip.t: On the night of 18–19 July 64 a fire destroys much of Rome during the reign of Nero; afterwards the city is rebuilt and the Christians are persecuted.

eventos/664-sinodo-de-whitby.descripcion.t: The kingdom of Northumbria adopts the Roman rite over the Celtic one in calculating Easter, aligning the English Church with Rome.

eventos/680-batalla-de-kerbala.descripci.t: The troops of Caliph Yazid kill Husayn, grandson of Muhammad, and his small retinue; Husayn's martyrdom turns the party of Ali into the Shia religious current.

eventos/720-compilacion-del-kojiki-y-el-.t: The first official chronicles are compiled, setting down the mythology and legendary history of Japan.
Compilation of the Kojiki and the Nihon Shoki

eventos/752-gran-buda-del-templo-todaiji.t: The colossal bronze statue of the Buddha is consecrated in Nara, a symbol of state Buddhism.

eventos/753ac-fundacion-de-roma-leyenda..t: Legendary date of the founding of Rome by Romulus.

eventos/762-fundacion-de-bagdad.descripc.t: Caliph al-Mansur founds the round city of Baghdad (Madinat al-Salam), the new Abbasid capital and a great center of Islamic learning.

eventos/770ac-los-zhou-se-trasladan-a-lu.t: After the sack of Fenghao in 771 BC, King Ping moves the court east to Luoyi (c. 770 BC); royal power passes to the feudal states.
The Zhou move to Luoyi: Spring and Autumn period

eventos/776ac-primeros-juegos-olimpicos..t: The first recorded Olympic Games are held at the sanctuary of Zeus at Olympia. Their four-year cycle (the Olympiad) became the Panhellenic system of reckoning time.

eventos/79-erupcion-del-vesubio-pompeya-.t: Vesuvius erupts and buries the Roman cities of Pompeii, Herculaneum and Stabiae under ash and pyroclastic flows. Their exceptional preservation would make them, centuries later, a unique window onto Roman daily life.

eventos/800-coronacion-de-carlomagno.des.t: Leo III crowns Charlemagne emperor in Rome on Christmas Day 800.

eventos/814ac-fundacion-de-cartago-tradi.t: According to tradition, settlers from Tyre found Carthage in 814 BC; it is a traditional date: the oldest urban remains found date from the 7th century BC.

eventos/825-templos-de-borobudur.descrip.t: The Sailendra dynasty erects in central Java the world's largest Buddhist monument: a colossal terraced stone mandala crowned with stupas, testimony to the spread of Buddhism and Indian culture across Southeast Asia.

eventos/843-reparto-de-verdun.descripcio.t: The Carolingian Empire is divided among Charlemagne's three grandsons, the seed of France and Germany.

eventos/850-la-polvora.descripcion.t: Chinese alchemists of the Tang era describe gunpowder (pin at the capital, Chang'an).

eventos/862-rurik-y-el-origen-de-la-rus..t: The Varangian chieftain Rurik settles in Novgorod: his dynasty will rule the Rus —and Russia— for seven centuries.
Rurik and the origins of the Rus'

eventos/864-bautismo-de-boris-i-de-bulga.t: Khan Boris I accepts Christianity and baptizes the Bulgarians, bringing them into the Byzantine orbit.
Baptism of Boris I of Bulgaria

eventos/874-colonizacion-de-islandia.des.t: Ingólfur Arnarson founds Reykjavík; in 930 the settlers create the Althing, the oldest parliament still in operation.

eventos/910-fundacion-de-la-abadia-de-cl.t: Cluny is founded, driving force of the great monastic reform that would renew the Western Church.

eventos/911-fundacion-de-normandia.descr.t: By the Treaty of Saint-Clair-sur-Epte, the Frankish king cedes to the Viking Rollo the land of the “Northmen”: Normandy, cradle of the conquerors of 1066.

eventos/962-coronacion-imperial-de-oton-.t: Otto I is crowned emperor in Rome, renewing the Empire in the West and giving rise to the Holy Roman Empire.

eventos/985-erik-el-rojo-coloniza-groenl.t: Exiled from Iceland, Erik founds the Norse settlements of Greenland, inhabited for almost five centuries.

mapa:Nahua ( Morelos, Puebla, Tlaxcala,.t: Nahua (Morelos, Puebla, Tlaxcala, Veracruz, Hidalgo, San Luis Potosí)

mapa:North American Pacifi foraging, hun.t: North American Pacific foraging, hunting and fishing peoples

paises/abasi.resena.t: The Abbasid Caliphate (750–1258) was a caliphal dynasty founded in 750 by Abu al-Abbas, a descendant of al-Abbas, uncle of Muhammad, who seized power after eliminating the Umayyad dynasty and moved the capital from Damascus to Baghdad.

paises/acad.resena.t: The first empire in history (c. 2334–2154 BC, middle chronology), founded by Sargon of Akkad, who united the Akkadian- and Sumerian-speaking peoples under a single king and extended his rule from the Mediterranean to Iran. The location of its capital, Akkad, is unknown.

paises/afganistan.resena.t: Afghanistan, officially the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan but still internationally recognized as the Islamic Republic of Afghanistan, is a mountainous landlocked country located in South Asia. It is a theocratic Islamic state based on the religious principles of Sunni Islam.

paises/aglabi.resena.t: The Aghlabids, or Banu al-Aghlab, were a dynasty of Sunni Muslim Arab emirs of North Africa whose power was centered in Ifriqiya (Tunisia), where the founder Ibrahim I ibn al-Aghlab established in 800 an emirate nominally dependent on the Abbasid Caliphate, which became a military power in the central Mediterranean, extending north to Ar…

paises/alanos.resena.t: An Iranian nomadic people related to the Sarmatians. They lived on the steppes east of the Don and north of the Caucasus. The Huns subjugated many of them in 375: some joined the Vandals and Suebi in their move to the West, while others took refuge in the Caucasus, where they are at the origin of the Ossetians.

paises/albania.resena.t: Albania, officially the Republic of Albania, is a country in Southeast Europe. It lies on the Adriatic and Ionian Seas within the Mediterranean Sea and shares land borders with Montenegro to the northwest, Kosovo to the northeast, North Macedonia to the east and Greece to the south; and a maritime border with Greece, Montenegro and Italy to the west.

paises/alemania.resena.t: Germany, officially the Federal Republic of Germany, is a country in Central Europe and the member state of the European Union with the largest population and GDP. Constituted as a social and democratic state under the rule of law, its form of government is a federal parliamentary republic.

paises/almoravide.resena.t: A Sanhaja Berber religious and military movement that emerged around 1050 in the western Sahara. It founded Marrakesh around 1070, united the western Maghreb and al-Andalus after its victory at Sagrajas (1086), and fell to the Almohads in 1147.

paises/andorra.resena.t: Andorra, officially the Principality of Andorra, is a sovereign landlocked microstate located in southwestern Europe, between the autonomous community of Catalonia (Spain) and the region of Occitania (France), on the edge of the Iberian Peninsula.

paises/angola.resena.t: Angola, officially the Republic of Angola, is a country in southern Africa bordered by Namibia to the south, Zambia to the southeast, the Democratic Republic of the Congo to the north and northeast and the Republic of the Congo to the northwest, while to the west it has a coastline on the Atlantic Ocean.

paises/anguila.resena.t: The term anguila may refer to: eels (Anguillidae), a family of teleost fish of the order Anguilliformes; the American eel; the European eel; the electric eel, a fish of the family Gymnotidae; Anguilla, a British overseas territory (archipelago) located in the Caribbean Sea; Anguilla, an island of that archipelago; Anguilla, a town i…

paises/antigua-y-barbuda.resena.t: Antigua and Barbuda is one of the thirteen countries that make up Insular America, the Antilles or Caribbean islands, and one of the thirty-five on the American continent. It is located in the north of the Lesser Antilles, bordered by Guadeloupe to the south, Montserrat to the southwest, Saint Kitts and Nevis to the west and Saint Martin to the northwest.

paises/antillas-neerlandesas.resena.t: The Netherlands Antilles were, until 10 October 2010, an autonomous territory made up of five islands in the Caribbean Sea, belonging to the Kingdom of the Netherlands alongside the European Netherlands itself.

paises/aquemenida.resena.t: The first great Persian empire, founded by Cyrus the Great around 550 BC after subjugating the Medes, Lydians and Babylonians. Under Darius I it reached its greatest extent, from the Aegean and Egypt to the Indus Valley, organized into satrapies, linked by royal roads and a postal system, and with capitals at Susa, Persepolis, Pasargadae and Ecbatana. It failed in its attempt to subdue the Greeks (Greco-Persian Wars) and fell to Alexander the Great in 330 BC.

paises/arabia-saudita.resena.t: Saudi Arabia, officially the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, is a country in Western Asia, located on the Arabian Peninsula —in the Near East—, whose form of government is an absolute monarchy. Its capital and most populous city is Riyadh.

paises/aragon.resena.t: The Crown of Aragon, also known by other alternative names, was a political entity made up of a group of territories that, through conquests and marriages, were under the jurisdiction of the King of Aragon and Count of Barcelona between 1137 and 1707–1716.

paises/argelia.resena.t: Algeria, officially the People's Democratic Republic of Algeria, is one of the fifty-four countries that make up the African continent. It is constitutionally defined as an Arab, Amazigh and Muslim country. Its capital and most populous city is Algiers.

paises/argentina.nombres_periodo.1810.no.t: United Provinces of the Río de la Plata

paises/argentina.resena.t: Argentina, officially the Argentine Republic, is a sovereign country located in the far south and southeast of South America. Its form of government is democratic, federal, representative and republican.

paises/armenia.resena.t: Armenia, officially the Republic of Armenia, is a landlocked country located on the Armenian Highlands in Eurasia. Culturally, historically and politically, Armenia is considered part of Eastern Europe.

paises/asiria.resena.t: Assyria refers to an ancient region of Upper Mesopotamia that takes its name from the city of Aššur —the same name as Ashur, its tutelary deity—, and is also the name of the state —and later empire— that it formed between the 3rd and 1st millennia BC.

paises/asturias.resena.t: The Kingdom of Asturias, or of the Astures, was the first Christian political entity established in the Iberian Peninsula after the collapse of the Visigothic Kingdom of Toledo following the disappearance of King Roderic at the Battle of Guadalete and the subsequent Muslim conquest of the Iberian Peninsula.

paises/australia.resena.t: Australia, officially the Commonwealth of Australia, is a sovereign country comprising mainland Australia, the island of Tasmania and numerous smaller islands. With an area of 7,741,220 km², Australia is the largest country in Oceania and the sixth largest in the world.

paises/austria.resena.t: Austria, officially the Republic of Austria, is a country in Central Europe and a member state of the European Union. It borders the Czech Republic and Germany to the north, Slovakia and Hungary to the east, Slovenia and Italy to the south, and Switzerland and Liechtenstein to the west.

paises/ayubi.resena.t: A Kurdish dynasty founded by Saladin, who abolished the Fatimid Caliphate in 1171. It ruled Egypt, Syria, Yemen and Upper Mesopotamia, recaptured Jerusalem in 1187 and fell to the Mamluks (1250 in Egypt, 1260 in Syria).

paises/azerbaiyan.resena.t: Azerbaijan, officially the Republic of Azerbaijan, is a sovereign country in the Caucasus region, located between Western Asia and Eastern Europe. With no access to any ocean, it is bordered by the Caspian Sea to the east, Russia to the north, Georgia to the northwest, Armenia to the west and Iran to the south.

paises/azteca.resena.t: The Mexica Empire or Triple Alliance, also called the Aztec Empire and —more precisely— the Tenochca Empire, was an empire organized as a complex, multiethnic and flexible confederation of city-states with diverse political situations, which existed in central Mesoamerica during the Late Postclassic period until the Spanish conquest.

paises/babilonia.resena.t: Babylonia was an ancient state located in south-central Mesopotamia, centered on the city of the same name, which came to extend over Akkad and Sumer, wresting hegemony from the Amorite dynasties of Isin and Larsa of the so-called Sumerian Renaissance.

paises/bahamas.resena.t: The Bahamas, officially the Commonwealth of The Bahamas, is an island country and one of the 13 countries that make up Insular America or the Caribbean islands, one of the 35 on the American continent. Its capital and most populous city is Nassau, located on the island of New Providence.

paises/balticos.resena.t: Speakers of Baltic languages settled between the lower Vistula, the Daugava and the upper Dnieper. Tacitus calls them the Aestii; this group includes the Galindians, Sudovians and, later, the Prussians, Lithuanians and Latvians.

paises/banglades.resena.t: Bangladesh, officially the People's Republic of Bangladesh, is a sovereign country located in South Asia. Its territory is almost completely surrounded by India, except for a small strip in the southeast where it borders Burma.

paises/barbados.resena.t: Barbados is an island country in the Antilles whose form of government is a parliamentary republic made up of eleven parishes. It is located in the Lesser Antilles, northeast of mainland Venezuela, just east of Saint Lucia and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines.

paises/belgica.resena.t: Belgium, officially the Kingdom of Belgium, is one of the twenty-seven sovereign states that make up the European Union, located in northwestern Europe. The country covers an area of 30,528 km² and in 2023 had a population of 11,754,004 inhabitants.

paises/belice.resena.t: Belize is a sovereign country in the Americas located at the northeastern tip of Central America and in the Caribbean region. It is bordered by Mexico to the north and Guatemala to the south and west.

paises/benin.resena.t: Benin, until 1975 Dahomey, officially the Republic of Benin, is a country located in West Africa. It is bordered by Togo to the west, Nigeria to the east, and Burkina Faso and Niger to the north.

paises/bernicia.resena.t: An Anglian kingdom centered on Bamburgh, between the Tees and the Forth. Æthelfrith united it with Deira around 604, and Oswiu formed Northumbria from both.

paises/bielorrusia.resena.t: Belarus, officially the Republic of Belarus, is a sovereign landlocked country located in Eastern Europe that was part of the Soviet Union until 1991. It is bordered by Lithuania and Latvia to the north, Russia to the east, Ukraine to the south and Poland to the west.

paises/birmania.resena.t: Burma or Myanmar, officially the Republic of the Union of Myanmar, is a sovereign state in Southeast Asia. It borders India and Bangladesh to the west, Thailand and Laos to the east, China to the north and northeast, and the Bay of Bengal and the Andaman Sea to the south.

paises/bizancio.resena.t: The continuation of the Roman Empire in the East, with its capital at Constantinople. Justinian (527–565) recovered Italy and North Africa; it lost Syria and Egypt to Islam in the 7th century and Anatolia to the Turks after Manzikert (1071). It fell to the Ottomans in 1453.

paises/bolivia.resena.t: Bolivia, officially the Plurinational State of Bolivia, is a sovereign country located in western South America, a member of the Andean Community, politically constituted as a social, plurinational, unitary and decentralized state with autonomies. The country is organized into nine departments and one hundred and twelve provinces.

paises/bosnia-y-herzegovina.resena.t: Bosnia and Herzegovina, commonly called Bosnia-Herzegovina or simply Bosnia, is a sovereign European country with its capital at Sarajevo, located at the crossroads of Central and Southeast Europe, bordered by Croatia to the north, west and south; Serbia to the east; Montenegro to the east and south; and the Adriatic Sea to the southwest along 21.2…

paises/botsuana.resena.t: Botswana, officially the Republic of Botswana, is a sovereign landlocked country in southern Africa whose form of government is a unitary presidential republic. Its territory is divided into fifteen districts, nine rural and six urban.

paises/brasil.nombres_periodo.1815.nombr.t: United Kingdom of Portugal, Brazil and the Algarves

paises/brasil.nombres_periodo.1889.nombr.t: Republic of the United States of Brazil

paises/brasil.resena.t: Brazil, officially the Federative Republic of Brazil, is a sovereign country in South America comprising the eastern half of the subcontinent and some groups of small islands in the Atlantic Ocean. Its capital is Brasília and its most populous city is São Paulo.

paises/britanos.resena.t: Celtic peoples native to Great Britain. After the end of Roman rule they formed kingdoms in Wales, in the southwest (Dumnonia) and in the north (the Hen Ogledd: Rheged, Gododdin, Alt Clut, Elmet), which gradually gave way to the Anglo-Saxons.

paises/brunei.resena.t: Brunei is one of the countries that make up the Asian continent. Its capital and most populous city is Bandar Seri Begawan.

paises/bulgaria-primer.resena.t: A state founded in 681 by Khan Asparuh south of the Danube, after defeating Byzantium. Under Krum and Simeon I (893–927) it was a major Balkan power; Boris I Christianized it in 864. Basil II annexed it to Byzantium in 1018.

paises/burkina-faso.resena.t: Burkina Faso is a landlocked country in West Africa bordered by Mali to the northwest, Niger to the east, Benin to the southeast, and Côte d'Ivoire, Ghana and Togo to the south. In 2025 the UN estimated its population at 24,074,580 inhabitants.

paises/burundi.resena.t: Burundi, officially the Republic of Burundi, is a landlocked sovereign state located in the Great Lakes region of East Africa. It is bordered by Rwanda to the north, Tanzania to the south and east, and the Democratic Republic of the Congo to the west.

paises/butan.resena.t: Bhutan, officially the Kingdom of Bhutan, is a landlocked country in South Asia located in the Himalayas. It is bordered by the People's Republic of China to the north and northwest and by India to the south and southeast.

paises/buyi.resena.t: The Buyids, also known as Buwayhids or, in English, Buwaihids or Buyyids, were a Shia Iranian dynasty originating from Daylam. They founded a confederation that controlled most of present-day Iran and Iraq in the 10th and 11th centuries.

paises/camboya.resena.t: Cambodia, officially the Kingdom of Cambodia, is a sovereign state located in the south of the Indochinese Peninsula, in Southeast Asia. Its capital and most populous city is Phnom Penh.

paises/camerun.resena.t: Cameroon, officially the Republic of Cameroon, is a unitary state organized as a republic in Central Africa. It is bordered to the south by Equatorial Guinea, then by Gabon (298 km), and by the Republic of the Congo (523 km).

paises/canada.resena.t: Canada is a sovereign country located in North America whose form of government is a federal parliamentary monarchy. Its territory is organized into ten provinces and three territories.

paises/carpos.resena.t: A free Dacian people of Moldavia, between the Siret and the Prut, east of the Carpathians. From 238 they repeatedly attacked the Danubian provinces. Aurelian defeated them in 272, Diocletian and Galerius between 296 and 303, and Constantine in 317–318. Rome resettled many of the Carpi in its provinces, and after 318 the sources no longer mention them.

paises/cartago.resena.t: Carthage was an ancient city in North Africa, capital of the Punic state, in present-day Tunisia, founded by Phoenician emigrants from Tyre at the end of the 9th century BC, according to the most widely accepted modern dating.

paises/castilla.resena.t: The Crown of Castile, as a historical entity, is usually considered to begin with the last and definitive dynastic union of the kingdoms of Castile and León, with their respective territories, in 1230, or else with the joint meeting of their Cortes a few decades later.

paises/catar.resena.t: Qatar, officially the State of Qatar, is a sovereign Arab state located in Western Asia that occupies the small peninsula of the same name in the east of the Arabian Peninsula. It has a single land border, with Saudi Arabia to the south, while the rest of its territory is bathed by the waters of the Persian Gulf.

paises/ceredigion.resena.t: A small Welsh kingdom between the Dyfi and the Teifi, which emerged in the mid-5th century and was independent until around 872.

paises/chad.resena.t: Chad, officially the Republic of Chad, is a landlocked country located in Central Africa. It is bordered by Libya to the north, Sudan to the east, the Central African Republic to the south, Cameroon and Nigeria to the southwest and Niger to the west.

paises/checoslovaquia.nombres_periodo.19.t: Protectorate of Bohemia and Moravia / Slovak Republic

paises/chile.resena.t: Chile, officially the Republic of Chile, is a sovereign state located in the far southwest of South America. Its form of government is republican, democratic, presidential and unitary.

paises/chipre.resena.t: Cyprus, officially the Republic of Cyprus, is an island country in the eastern Mediterranean and the only Asian member of the twenty-seven sovereign states that make up the European Union. It is located on the island of the same name and its form of government is a presidential republic.

paises/civilizacion-del-indo.resena.t: A Bronze Age urban civilization on the Indus and its tributaries (Pakistan and northwestern India). Its mature phase (c. 2600–1900 BC) had planned cities such as Harappa and Mohenjo-Daro, with sewerage and standardized weights; its script remains undeciphered. It declined between 1900 and 1300 BC.
