paises/colombia.resena.t: Colombia, officially the Republic of Colombia, is a sovereign country located in the northwestern region of South America. It is constituted as a unitary, democratic and social state under the rule of law, organized into 32 departments and the Capital District of Bogotá.

paises/connacht.resena.t: A province in the west of Ireland, west of the Shannon, divided in the Early Middle Ages among the Uí Briúin, the Uí Fiachrach and the Uí Maine. In the 7th century it lost present-day Clare to Munster.

paises/cordoba.resena.t: A Muslim state of al-Andalus founded in 756 by Abd al-Rahman I, an Umayyad who escaped the Abbasid massacre. An emirate independent of Baghdad, it was proclaimed a caliphate by Abd al-Rahman III in 929; under Almanzor it reached the height of its power, and it broke up into taifa kingdoms after the fitna (1009–1031).

paises/corea-del-norte.resena.t: The Democratic People's Republic of Korea, commonly North Korea, is a sovereign country in East Asia, located in the northern part of the Korean Peninsula. It is bordered by China to the north, Russia to the northeast and South Korea to the south, with which it formed a single country until 1945.

paises/corea-del-sur.resena.t: The Republic of Korea, commonly South Korea, is a sovereign country in East Asia, located in the southern part of the Korean Peninsula. It is bordered to the north by North Korea, with which it formed a single country until 1945.

paises/costa-marfil.resena.t: Côte d'Ivoire, officially the Republic of Côte d'Ivoire, is a country located in West Africa. It is bordered by Liberia and Guinea to the west, Mali to the northwest, Burkina Faso to the northeast and Ghana to the east, and has a coastline on the Gulf of Guinea to the south.

paises/costa-rica.resena.t: Costa Rica, officially the Republic of Costa Rica, is a sovereign state organized as a unitary presidential republic made up of 7 provinces. Located in Central America, it has a territory with a total area of 51,179 km².

paises/croacia.resena.t: Croatia, officially the Republic of Croatia, is one of the twenty-seven sovereign states that make up the European Union, located between Central Europe, Southern Europe and the Adriatic Sea; it is bordered by Hungary to the northeast, Serbia to the east, Bosnia-Herzegovina and Montenegro to the southeast, Slovenia to the northwest and the Adriatic Sea to the southwest, where it sh…

paises/cuba.resena.t: Cuba, officially the Republic of Cuba, is a sovereign island state located in the Antilles of the Caribbean Sea in the North American region. Its territory is organized into fifteen provinces and one special municipality, with Havana as its capital and most populous city.

paises/cultura-de-kiev.resena.t: An archaeological culture of the 3rd to 5th centuries in the middle and upper basin of the Dnieper, the Desna and the Pripyat. It is considered the first identifiable Slavic culture, although its ethnic attribution is disputed.

paises/cultura-de-zarubintsy.resena.t: An archaeological culture from the 3rd century BC to the 1st century AD, with late phases in the 2nd, on the upper and middle Dnieper and the Pripyat, as far as the Southern Bug. It partly succeeded the Milograd culture and is associated with the early Slavs, although its ethnic attribution is disputed. Its central groups gave way to the Kiev culture.

paises/dal-riata.resena.t: A Gaelic kingdom on both sides of the North Channel: Argyll (Kintyre, Islay, Lorne, Cowal) and northern Antrim, with its capital at Dunadd and the monastery of Iona. It declined after Mag Rath (637), fell under the Picts in the 730s and merged with them into Alba.

paises/deira.resena.t: An Anglian kingdom between the Humber and the Tees, from the sea to the western edge of the Vale of York. It shared a king with Bernicia from 604 and merged with it into Northumbria after the death of Oswine (651).

paises/delhi.resena.t: A Muslim state of northern India (1206–1526) ruled by five successive dynasties (Mamluk, Khalji, Tughlaq, Sayyid and Lodi). It reached its greatest extent in the early 14th century; Timur devastated it in 1398 and Babur put an end to it at Panipat (1526).

paises/dominica.resena.t: Dominica, officially the Commonwealth of Dominica, is an island and republic in the Americas considered a microstate, part of the Lesser Antilles in the Caribbean Sea. It is located, specifically, between the French overseas territories of Guadeloupe to the north and Martinique to the south, and east of Aves Island (Venezuela).

paises/dumnonia.resena.t: A Brittonic kingdom of the southwest (Devon, Cornwall and parts of Somerset and Dorset). Wessex whittled it down from the east: to the Parrett after Peonnum (658) and more land after Geraint's defeat by Ine (710). Cornwall remained Brittonic until the 9th century.

paises/dyfed.resena.t: A Welsh kingdom of the southwest (Pembrokeshire), founded by Irish settlers in the 5th century; in the early 10th century it joined its neighbors in Deheubarth.

paises/ecuador.resena.t: Ecuador, officially the Republic of Ecuador, is a sovereign country located in the northwestern region of South America. It is constituted as a social, democratic, plurinational state under the rule of law, whose form of government is a presidential, unitary and decentralized republic.

paises/eeuu.resena.t: The United States, officially the United States of America, is a federation constituted as a constitutional republic made up of fifty states and a federal district. Its capital is Washington D.

paises/egipto.resena.t: Egypt, officially the Arab Republic of Egypt, is a transcontinental sovereign country. It is located mostly in the far northeast of Africa, while the Sinai Peninsula lies in Asia.

paises/el-salvador.resena.t: El Salvador, officially the Republic of El Salvador, is a sovereign country in Central America with coasts on the Pacific Ocean. According to the current constitution, it is a unitary, representative and fully presidential republic together with the Legislative Assembly.

paises/elam.resena.t: A civilization of southwestern Iran (Khuzestan and Fars) with its capital at Susa, active from c. 3200 BC. A rival and partner of Mesopotamia for three millennia, it was devastated by Ashurbanipal around 647 BC and absorbed by the Persians around 540 BC.

paises/elmet.resena.t: A Brittonic kingdom in present-day West Yorkshire (between Leeds and Selby), one of the last in the south of the Hen Ogledd. Edwin of Northumbria conquered it in 616–617.

paises/emiratos-arabes-unidos.resena.t: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) is a sovereign country constituted as a federal monarchy in the Near East, located on the Arabian Peninsula. It is made up of seven emirates: Abu Dhabi, Ajman, Dubai, Fujairah, Ras al-Khaimah, Sharjah and Umm al-Quwain.

paises/eritrea.resena.t: Eritrea, officially the State of Eritrea, is a country located in northeastern Africa. It is bordered by Sudan to the north and west and by Ethiopia and Djibouti to the south, and to the east it is bathed by the Red Sea.

paises/escitas.resena.t: An Iranian nomadic people of horsemen who dominated the Pontic steppe from the 8th–7th centuries BC; between c. 626 and 616 BC their raids reached as far as Palestine, and from c. 600 BC their center of power was the steppe north of the Black Sea.

paises/eslavos.resena.t: Slavic-speaking peoples cited by Byzantine sources from the early 6th century as Sclaveni and Antes. Jordanes places them between the Vistula, the Dnieper and the area north of the lower Danube. By the end of that century they already extended as far as the Elbe and the Saale and were penetrating the Balkans.

paises/eslovaquia.resena.t: Slovakia, officially the Slovak Republic, is one of the twenty-seven sovereign states that make up the European Union. Located in Central Europe, it is a landlocked state.

paises/eslovenia.resena.t: Slovenia, officially the Republic of Slovenia, is a country located in Central Europe and one of the twenty-seven sovereign states that make up the European Union. It is bordered by Italy to the west; the Adriatic Sea to the southwest; Croatia to the south and east; Hungary to the northeast; and Austria to the north.

paises/espana.resena.t: Spain, formally the Kingdom of Spain, is a transcontinental sovereign country located mainly in southwestern Europe and, to a lesser extent, in North Africa. Constituted as a social state under the rule of law, its form of government is a parliamentary monarchy.

paises/essex.resena.t: The kingdom of the East Saxons (527–825), with Essex, Middlesex, much of Hertfordshire and two former Roman capitals, Colchester and London, which it lost to Mercia in the 8th century. It passed to Wessex in 825.

paises/estados-pontificios.resena.t: Territories of central Italy ruled by the pope as temporal sovereign from the Donation of Pepin the Short (756) until Italian unification (1870).

paises/estanglia.resena.t: The kingdom of the East Angles, in Norfolk and Suffolk, from the 6th century until its incorporation into England in 918. Rædwald (d. c. 624), probably buried at Sutton Hoo, was the most powerful king of his time.

paises/estonia.resena.t: Estonia, officially the Republic of Estonia, is one of the twenty-seven sovereign states that make up the European Union, and the smallest of the three Baltic countries. It is bordered by Latvia to the south, Russia to the east, the Gulf of Finland to the north and the Baltic Sea to the west.

paises/esuatini.resena.t: Swaziland or Eswatini, officially the Kingdom of Eswatini and formerly the Kingdom of Swaziland, is a small landlocked sovereign state located in Southern Africa, on the eastern foothills of the Drakensberg Mountains, between South Africa and Mozambique. Its territory is organized into four districts.

paises/etiopia.resena.t: Ethiopia, officially the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia, formerly known as Abyssinia, is a landlocked country located in the Horn of Africa. Population estimates for 2021 place it as the second most populous country in Africa, behind only Nigeria, and the twelfth in the world, as well as the most populous landlocked country in the world.

paises/etruscos.resena.t: A people of central Italy organized in a federation of city-states from c. 900 BC. Around 500 BC they dominated Tuscany, Umbria and part of Latium, with influence in the Po Valley and Campania. They greatly influenced early Rome, which gradually absorbed them from the 4th century BC.

paises/fatimi.resena.t: The Fatimid Caliphate was the fourth Islamic caliphate, existing between the 10th and 12th centuries under the rule of the Fatimids. It was thus the only Shia caliphate in all of history —Ismaili, specifically—.

paises/fenicia.resena.t: A group of Canaanite city-states on the coast of present-day Lebanon (Tyre, Sidon, Byblos, Arwad), at their height between c. 1200 and 332 BC. Great seafarers and traders, they founded colonies throughout the Mediterranean, including Carthage, and spread the alphabet.

paises/filipinas.resena.t: The Philippines —officially the Republic of the Philippines— is an island country located in Southeast Asia, in the Pacific Ocean. Its capital is Manila and its most populous city is Quezon City.

paises/finlandia.resena.t: Finland, officially the Republic of Finland, is one of the twenty-seven sovereign states that make up the European Union. It is located in northeastern Europe.

paises/fiyi.resena.t: Fiji, officially the Republic of Fiji, is a sovereign island country in Oceania, located in the Pacific Ocean. It is constituted as a parliamentary republic.

paises/francia.nombres_periodo.1944.nomb.t: Provisional Government of the French Republic

paises/francia.resena.t: France, officially the French Republic, is a transcontinental sovereign country spanning Western Europe and overseas regions and territories in the Americas and the Atlantic, Pacific and Indian Oceans. It is one of the twenty-seven sovereign states that make up the European Union.

paises/francos.resena.t: The Kingdom of the Franks, also known in Latin as Francia, or simply the Frankish kingdom, are the historiographical names for the kingdom of the Franks established in the late 5th century, taking advantage of the decline of Roman imperial authority in Gaul during the period of the so-called "barbarian invasions".

paises/frigia.resena.t: Kingdom of central Anatolia with its capital at Gordion. It reached its peak in the late 8th century BC under King Midas and was destroyed by the Cimmerians around 675 BC.

paises/frisios.resena.t: Germanic people of the North Sea coast, in Frisia. The Frisian kingdom (c. 600–734) extended, according to some authors, from the Zwin, near Bruges, to the Weser. The Franks subjugated it after the Battle of the Boarn (734).

paises/gabon.resena.t: Gabon, officially the Gabonese Republic, is a country on the west coast of Central Africa. It borders Equatorial Guinea and Cameroon to the north, the Republic of the Congo to the east and south, and the Atlantic Ocean to the west.

paises/gambia.resena.t: The Gambia, officially the Republic of The Gambia, is a West African nation. It is entirely surrounded by Senegal, except at the mouth of the Gambia River on the Atlantic Ocean.

paises/gaznavi.resena.t: The Ghaznavids were a Muslim dynasty of Turkic origin, founded by the Samanid commander Sebük Tegin, which reigned from the late 10th century to the late 12th century over an empire made up of the regions of Khorasan, Afghanistan and Punjab, with its capital at Ghazni and later, near the end of the regime, at Lahore.

paises/georgia.resena.t: Georgia is a sovereign country located in the Caucasus region, on the eastern coast of the Black Sea, on the boundary between Eastern Europe and Western Asia.

paises/gepidos.resena.t: East Germanic people from the lower Vistula. After defeating the Huns at the Nedao (454) it dominated the Tisza plain and Transylvania, with its capital at Sirmium. The Lombards defeated it in 552 and the Avars destroyed it in 567.

paises/ghana.resena.t: Ghana, officially the Republic of Ghana, is a West African country constituted as a presidential republic. It borders Burkina Faso to the north, Togo to the east, Ivory Coast to the west and the Gulf of Guinea to the south.

paises/glywysing.resena.t: Welsh kingdom of the southeast (the future Glamorgan). On the map it includes its neighbours Gwent, Brycheiniog and Ergyng. United with Gwent it formed Morgannwg, which fell to the Normans.

paises/gododdin.resena.t: Brittonic kingdom of Lothian and the Borders, with Din Eidyn (Edinburgh) and Traprain Law. After the disaster of Catraeth (c. 600), celebrated in the poem Y Gododdin, Edinburgh fell to the Angles in 638.

paises/granada-2.resena.t: Granada is a Spanish municipality and city, capital of the province of the same name, in the autonomous community of Andalusia. It is located in the central part of the Vega de Granada comarca, at an altitude of 680 m above sea level.

paises/granada.resena.t: The Nasrid Kingdom of Granada, also known as the Emirate of Granada or the Sultanate of Granada, was a Muslim state in the south of the Iberian Peninsula, with its capital in the city of Granada, that existed during the Middle Ages.

paises/granbretana.resena.t: The United Kingdom, officially the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, is a sovereign island country located off the northwest of continental Europe. Geographically, its territory consists of the island of Great Britain, the northeast of the island of Ireland and small adjacent islands.

paises/grecia.resena.t: Greece, officially the Hellenic Republic, is one of the twenty-seven sovereign states that make up the European Union. The country has around ten million inhabitants, forming a very homogeneous society in which Greek is mainly spoken and Orthodox Christianity is practised.

paises/groenlandia.resena.t: Greenland is an island in the Northern Hemisphere, between the Atlantic and Arctic Oceans, which is politically a constituent country of the Kingdom of Denmark. With a total area of 2,166,086 km², it is considered the largest island in the world, taking Australia to be a continental landmass.

paises/guatemala.resena.t: Guatemala, officially the Republic of Guatemala, is a sovereign country located at the northwestern end of Central America. According to its constitution, its form of government is a democratic, secular and representative republic, administered through 22 departments and 340 municipalities, which are organised into 8 administrative regions.

paises/guayana-francesa.resena.t: French Guiana, or simply the Department of Guiana, is an overseas region and department of France, which is part of the European Union as an outermost region. As a single territorial collectivity, it has only one assembly, which combines the powers of the regional and departmental councils.

paises/guinea-bisau.resena.t: Guinea-Bissau, officially the Republic of Guinea-Bissau, is a West African country covering 36,125 km² with an estimated population of 1,644,000 (2022). It borders Senegal to the north, Guinea to the south and east, and the Atlantic Ocean to the west.

paises/guinea-ecuatorial.resena.t: Equatorial Guinea, officially the Republic of Equatorial Guinea, is an African country on the Gulf of Guinea, which its constitution defines as an independent, republican, unitary, social and democratic state, with a presidential republic as its form of government. Its territory is made up of eight provinces.

paises/guinea.resena.t: Guinea, officially the Republic of Guinea, often called Guinea-Conakry to distinguish it from two other African countries, its neighbour Guinea-Bissau and Equatorial Guinea, is a West African country formerly known as French Guinea.

paises/gupta.resena.t: Empire of northern India founded by Chandragupta I, crowned at Pataliputra around 320. Samudragupta and Chandragupta II extended it across the Ganges plain and defeated the Western Sakas. Its era is considered the golden age of classical India, with advances in mathematics and astronomy, Sanskrit literature and the founding of the university of Nalanda. The Hephthalite invasions from the mid-5th century accelerated its decline, and it disappeared around 550.

paises/gurida.resena.t: Empire of Afghan origin (1175–1215) that replaced the Ghaznavids, defeated the Rajputs at Tarain (1192) and conquered northern India. The Delhi Sultanate arose from its slave generals.

paises/guyana.resena.t: Guyana, officially the Co-operative Republic of Guyana, is a country on the northern coast of South America and the Caribbean, a member of UNASUR and CELAC and an associate member of Mercosur. Georgetown is the capital of Guyana and also the country's largest city.

paises/gwynedd.resena.t: Welsh kingdom of the northwest (Anglesey and Snowdonia), founded according to tradition by Cunedda around 500. Its kings were often called kings of the Britons; Edward I conquered it in 1282–1283.

paises/hafsi.resena.t: Berber dynasty that ruled Ifriqiya (Tunisia and eastern Algeria) from its separation from the Almohad empire in 1229 until the Ottoman conquest of 1574.

paises/haiti.resena.t: Haiti, officially the Republic of Haiti, is a country in the Americas located on Hispaniola; it is one of the thirteen states that make up Insular America, the Antilles or islands of the Caribbean Sea. Its capital and most populous city is Port-au-Prince.

paises/hitita.resena.t: The Hittites were an Anatolian Indo-European people who formed one of the first major civilisations of Western Asia during the Bronze Age. Possibly originating from beyond the Black Sea, they settled in present-day Turkey in the early 2nd millennium BC.

paises/honduras.resena.t: Honduras, officially the Republic of Honduras, is a country in Central America with coastlines on the Atlantic Ocean and the Pacific Ocean. It is constituted as a unitary, free, sovereign and independent state.

paises/hong-kong.resena.t: Hong Kong, officially the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China, is one of the two special administrative regions of the People's Republic of China, together with Macau.

paises/hordadeoro.resena.t: The Golden Horde —in Tatar: Алтын Урда, Altın Urda — was a Mongol state that covered part of present-day Russia, Ukraine and Kazakhstan.

paises/hungria-oriental.resena.t: Name given by historians to the kingdom of John Zápolya, elected King of Hungary after the Battle of Mohács (1526) in opposition to Ferdinand of Habsburg, and of his son John Sigismund. Zápolya swore allegiance to Sultan Suleiman in 1529; after the Ottoman capture of Buda (1541) the kingdom was reduced to Transylvania, the Partium and, until 1552, the Banat. In 1570, by the Treaty of Speyer, John Sigismund renounced the royal title and the kingdom became the Principality of Transylvania.

paises/hungria.resena.t: The Kingdom of Hungary was a kingdom that existed in Central Europe from the year 1000 until 1919, with a five-month interruption between that year and 1920 during which the Hungarian Soviet Republic existed. After the overthrow of the communist regime the kingdom was restored.

paises/hunos.resena.t: The Hunnic Empire was founded by the Huns, an Asian people of great importance in the 4th century. They made deep incursions into Europe and Asia.

paises/iljanato.resena.t: Mongol khanate of Persia founded by Hulagu after the capture of Baghdad (1258). It covered Iran, Iraq, the Caucasus and much of Anatolia; it disintegrated on the death of Abu Said in 1335.

paises/imperio-galo.resena.t: State that arose in 260, during the Crisis of the Third Century, when the general Postumus proclaimed himself emperor in Gaul after the capture of Valerian. It came to rule Gaul, Germania, Britannia and Hispania with its own Roman institutions (consuls, senate, guard) and mints at Trier and Cologne. Hispania returned to the Empire around 269, and Aurelian reincorporated it after defeating Tetricus at Châlons (274).

paises/imperio-ghana.resena.t: Soninke kingdom of the western Sahel, in the southeast of present-day Mauritania and western Mali, with its capital at Koumbi Saleh. It controlled the trans-Saharan gold trade until its decline in the 12th century and became a vassal of Mali in the mid-13th century. It has no territorial connection with present-day Ghana, which took its name in 1957.

paises/india.resena.t: India, officially the Republic of India, is a sovereign country in South Asia. With an estimated population of more than 1,476 million, it has been the most populous country in the world since 2023.

paises/indonesia.nombres_periodo.1602.no.t: East Indies of the Dutch East India Company (VOC)

paises/indonesia.resena.t: Indonesia, officially the Republic of Indonesia, is a country in Southeast Asia and northern Oceania, between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. It consists of more than 17,000 islands, including Sumatra, Java, Sulawesi and parts of Borneo and New Guinea.

paises/inglaterra.resena.t: England is one of the four constituent countries of the United Kingdom. Its territory consists of the southern and central part of Great Britain, an island it shares with Scotland and Wales, and about a hundred smaller islands such as the Isles of Scilly and the Isle of Wight.

paises/irak.resena.t: Iraq, officially the Republic of Iraq, historically also known in the West as Mesopotamia, is an Asian country of the Near East that covers most of the northwest of the Zagros mountain range, the eastern part of the Syrian Desert and the northern part of the Arabian Desert.

paises/iran.resena.t: Iran, officially the Islamic Republic of Iran, historically also known in the West as Persia, is a sovereign country of the Near East and Western Asia. It is a theocratic Islamic republic based on the religious principles of Shia Islam.

paises/irlanda-gaelica.resena.t: Collection of Gaelic lordships (O'Neill, O'Donnell, O'Brien, MacCarthy and others) and Gaelicised Anglo-Irish lordships (the Earls of Kildare, Ormond and Desmond) which at the end of the 15th century dominated Ireland outside the Pale and recognised only nominally the sovereignty of the King of England as Lord of Ireland. It was not a unified state: the map groups them because their borders are not precisely known. The Tudor conquest and the proclamation of the Kingdom of Ireland (1542) ended their de facto independence over the course of the 16th century.

paises/irlanda.resena.t: Ireland, also known as the Republic of Ireland, is a sovereign island country that occupies most of the island of Ireland. It is one of the twenty-seven member states of the European Union.

paises/isla-de-pascua.resena.t: Easter Island, or Rapa Nui, is a Chilean island belonging to the province of Isla de Pascua, in the Valparaíso Region. It lies in the heart of Polynesia, Oceania, in the middle of the Pacific Ocean, about 3,700 kilometres from Caldera, in mainland Chilean territory, which is the nearest inhabited point within Chile.

paises/islandia.resena.t: Iceland is a European island country whose territory comprises the island of the same name and some small adjacent islands and islets in the Atlantic Ocean. Its capital is Reykjavík.

paises/islas-turcas-y-caicos.resena.t: The Turks and Caicos Islands are a British Overseas Territory dependent on the United Kingdom. They were administered by Jamaica until 1962, after which administration of the islands passed to the Bahamas until 1973.

paises/israel-antiguo.resena.t: According to the Bible, Saul, David and Solomon reigned over a united state (c. 1047–931 BC) that split into the kingdoms of Israel and Judah around 930 BC; the existence and extent of this united monarchy are debated among historians and archaeologists. Israel fell to Assyria in 722 BC and Judah to Babylon in 586 BC.

paises/israel.resena.t: Israel, officially the State of Israel, is a sovereign state in Western Asia located in the Near East region, in the Mediterranean Levant.

paises/italia.resena.t: Italy, officially the Italian Republic, is a sovereign country in Southern Europe and one of the twenty-seven member states of the European Union. It is constituted as a parliamentary republic made up of twenty regions, which in turn comprise one hundred and ten provinces.

paises/jamaica.resena.t: Jamaica is one of the thirteen countries that make up Insular America, the Antilles or islands of the Caribbean Sea. It is one of the thirty-five countries of the American continent.

paises/japon.resena.t: Japan is an island country in East Asia located in the northwest Pacific Ocean. It is bordered by the Sea of Japan to the west and extends from the Sea of Okhotsk in the north to the East China Sea and Taiwan in the south.

paises/jemer.resena.t: The Khmer Empire was an empire of Southeast Asia, centred on hydraulic cities in what is now northern Cambodia. Known as Kambuja to its inhabitants, it grew out of the earlier civilisation of Chenla and lasted from 802 to 1431.

paises/jin-jurchen.resena.t: The Jin dynasty, also known as the Jurchen dynasty, was founded by the Wanyan, a clan of the Jurchens, the ancestors of the Manchus who founded the Qing dynasty five hundred years later. The name is sometimes written as Jinn[citation needed] to distinguish it from the earlier Jin dynasty, whose name is transliterated the same way.

paises/jin.resena.t: Dynasty founded by Sima Yan, who in 266 deposed the last emperor of Wei. In 280 it conquered the kingdom of Wu and reunified China for the first time since the fall of the Han. The civil wars of the Eight Princes and the revolts of northern peoples cost it Luoyang (311) and Chang'an (316); the court took refuge in Jiankang (Nanjing), where the Eastern Jin held out until 420 and halted the Former Qin at the Battle of the Fei River (383).

paises/jordania.resena.t: Jordan, officially the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan, called Transjordan until 1950, is a country in Asia located in the Near East region. It borders Syria to the north, Iraq to the northeast, the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to the east and south, the Red Sea to the southwest, and the Dead Sea, Israel and Palestine to the west.

paises/kazajistan.resena.t: Kazakhstan, officially the Republic of Kazakhstan, is a transcontinental country, with most of its territory in Central Asia and a smaller part, west of the Ural River, in Eastern Europe. With an area of 2,724,900 km², it is the ninth-largest country in the world, as well as the world's largest landlocked state.

paises/kenia.resena.t: Kenya, officially the Republic of Kenya, is an East African country bordering Ethiopia to the north, Somalia to the east, Tanzania to the south, Uganda to the west and South Sudan to the northwest, with the Indian Ocean washing its southeastern coast.

paises/kent.resena.t: Anglo-Saxon kingdom of southeastern England, founded by the Jutes in the 5th century. Under Æthelberht (c. 589–616) it was the first to receive the mission of Augustine (597) and the see of Canterbury. It passed to Wessex in 825.

paises/kirguistan.resena.t: Kyrgyzstan, officially the Kyrgyz Republic, is a mountainous, landlocked country in Central Asia. It shares borders with Kazakhstan to the north, China to the east, Tajikistan to the south and Uzbekistan to the west.

paises/kongo.resena.t: Bantu kingdom of the lower Congo River basin, with its capital at Mbanza Kongo (São Salvador, today in northern Angola). It formed around 1390 and from the late 15th century maintained relations with Portugal; its kings adopted Catholicism. The defeat at Mbwila (1665) by the Portuguese opened a long period of internal wars, and in the 19th century the kingdom ended up as a vassal of Portugal until the titular monarchy was abolished in 1914. It has no connection with the present-day Republic of the Congo.

paises/kush.resena.t: Nubian kingdom of the middle Nile, heir to the Kerma culture. After centuries of Egyptian rule it regained independence around 1070 BC with its capital at Napata; its kings ruled Egypt as the 25th Dynasty (747–656 BC) and, around 591 BC, moved the capital to Meroë, a centre of iron-working and of trade with the Red Sea. It dissolved around AD 350.

paises/kushan.resena.t: Empire founded around the year 30 by Kujula Kadphises, chief of one of the Yuezhi clans settled in Bactria. At its height, under Kanishka (2nd century), it stretched from the Amu Darya to the Ganges valley, with capitals at Purushapura (Peshawar) and Mathura. It controlled the central stretch of the Silk Road between Rome, Parthia and Han China, and under its patronage the Greco-Buddhist art of Gandhara flourished. After Vasudeva I (c. 225) it fragmented under pressure from the Sasanians and, later, the Kidarites.

paises/kuwait.resena.t: Kuwait, officially the State of Kuwait, is an Arab country in Western Asia, at the northeastern tip of the Arabian Peninsula and the northern end of the Persian Gulf, where it shares borders with Iraq to the north and Saudi Arabia to the south. Its name is an Arabic diminutive of the word كوت (kūt), meaning "fortress".

paises/laos.resena.t: Laos, officially the Lao People's Democratic Republic, is a sovereign state located on the Indochinese Peninsula. It borders Myanmar and China to the northwest, Vietnam to the east, Cambodia to the southeast, and Thailand to the west and southwest, and it is the only landlocked country in Southeast Asia.

paises/leinster.resena.t: Kingdom of eastern Ireland (Laigin). It lost the Midlands to the southern Uí Néill, who formed Mide, and Osraige to Munster; in the 7th and 8th centuries it was dominated by the Uí Dúnlainge.

paises/leon-castilla.resena.t: Personal union of the kingdoms of León and Castile (with Galicia) under a single king in the 11th and 12th centuries. Ferdinand I, Count of Castile, won the Leonese throne at Tamarón (1037) and on his death (1065) divided his kingdoms among his sons. Alfonso VI reunited them in 1072, conquered Toledo in 1085 and styled himself Emperor of all Hispania; he was succeeded by his daughter Urraca and his grandson Alfonso VII, who took Coria, Calatrava and Almería. On the death of Alfonso VII (1157), Castile passed to Sancho III and León to Ferdinand II. Each kingdom kept its own institutions, and the definitive union did not come until Ferdinand III, in 1230.

paises/leon.resena.t: The Kingdom of León was an independent medieval kingdom located in the northwest of the Iberian Peninsula. It was founded in 910, when the Christian princes of the Kingdom of Asturias, on the northern coast of the peninsula, moved their capital from Oviedo to the city of León.

paises/lesoto.resena.t: Lesotho, officially the Kingdom of Lesotho, is a landlocked country in southern Africa, geographically and politically enclaved within South Africa.

paises/letonia.resena.t: Latvia, officially the Republic of Latvia, is a sovereign country in Northern Europe, constituted as a social and democratic state under the rule of law, whose form of government is a parliamentary republic. It is one of the twenty-seven sovereign states that make up the European Union.

paises/liao.resena.t: The Liao dynasty (907–1125), also known as the Khitan Empire, was a Chinese dynasty of foreign origin that ruled much of the northeast of present-day China. The Khitans, one of the Tungusic ethnic groups that centuries ago inhabited present-day Manchuria, founded in 907 a state initially called the Khitan State.

paises/libano.resena.t: Lebanon, officially the Lebanese Republic, is an Arab country in Western Asia, located in the Mediterranean Levant. It borders Israel to the south, Syria to the north and east, and the Mediterranean Sea to the west.

paises/liberia.nombres_periodo.1822.nomb.t: Colony of the American Colonization Society (Commonwealth of Liberia)

paises/liberia.resena.t: Liberia, officially the Republic of Liberia, is a country on the west coast of Africa bordering Sierra Leone to the northwest, Ivory Coast to the east and Guinea to the north. To the south and west it borders the Gulf of Guinea, part of the Atlantic Ocean, at the point of the African continent closest to South America, from which it is about 2,840 km away.

paises/libia.nombres_periodo.1977.nombre.t: Great Socialist People's Libyan Arab Jamahiriya

paises/libia.resena.t: Libya, officially the State of Libya, is a sovereign republican country in North Africa. Its capital is Tripoli.

paises/lidia.resena.t: Kingdom of western Anatolia with its capital at Sardis, ruled by the Mermnad dynasty from c. 680 BC. Under Alyattes and Croesus it dominated everything west of the Halys River, and it is famous for the first coins ever minted. Cyrus II conquered it in 546 BC.

paises/liechtenstein.resena.t: Liechtenstein, officially the Principality of Liechtenstein, is a landlocked Central European microstate whose form of government is a constitutional monarchy, located between Switzerland and Austria on the eastern bank of the Rhine. The official language is German, but in everyday life mainly the Alemannic dialect is spoken, with distinctly local variations.

paises/lindsey.resena.t: Small Anglian kingdom or sub-kingdom in present-day Lincolnshire, between the Humber, the Trent and the Witham. Contested by Northumbria and Mercia, it passed to the latter after the Battle of the Trent (679).

paises/lituania.resena.t: Lithuania, officially the Republic of Lithuania, is one of the twenty-seven sovereign states that make up the European Union, constituted as a social and democratic state under the rule of law, whose form of government is a unitary semi-presidential republic. Its territory is organised into ten counties.

paises/lombardos.resena.t: The Lombard Kingdom, or Kingdom of the Lombards, later the Kingdom of (all) Italy, was an early medieval state established by the Lombards on the Italian Peninsula between 568–569 and 774.

paises/lugios.resena.t: Large confederation of peoples between the Oder and the Vistula, north of the Sudetes and the Carpathians, mentioned by Strabo, Tacitus and Ptolemy between the 1st and 2nd centuries. It is identified with the Przeworsk archaeological culture and has been linked to the Vandals; its name disappears from the sources in the 3rd century.

paises/luxemburgo.resena.t: Luxembourg, officially the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, is one of the twenty-seven sovereign states that make up the European Union. It is a landlocked state surrounded by Germany, Belgium and France.

paises/macedonia-del-norte.resena.t: North Macedonia, officially the Republic of North Macedonia, is a landlocked country in southeastern Europe, on the Balkan Peninsula. It borders Serbia and Kosovo to the north, Bulgaria to the east, Greece to the south and Albania to the west.

paises/madagascar.resena.t: Madagascar, officially the Republic of Madagascar, is an island country in the Indian Ocean, off the southeast coast of the African continent, east of Mozambique. The nation comprises the island of the same name, the largest in Africa and the fourth-largest in the world, and numerous small peripheral islands.

paises/magadha.resena.t: One of the sixteen great kingdoms (mahajanapadas) of the Ganges valley, in present-day Bihar, with its capital first at Rajagriha and later at Pataliputra. The Buddha preached there. It was the base of the Nanda and Maurya empires. The chronology of its first kings (Bimbisara) is disputed.

paises/majapahit.resena.t: Hindu-Buddhist empire of eastern Java founded in 1293 by Raden Wijaya, with its capital at Trowulan. It dominated much of the archipelago in the 14th century, put an end to the last successor state of Srivijaya (Palembang, 1377) and disappeared before the Sultanate of Demak around 1527.

paises/malasia.resena.t: Malaysia is one of the forty-nine countries that make up the Asian continent. Kuala Lumpur is the official and legislative capital as well as the most populous city, while Putrajaya is the administrative and judicial capital.

paises/malaui.resena.t: Malawi, officially the Republic of Malawi, is a landlocked country in southeastern Africa, formerly known as Nyasaland, whose capital is the city of Lilongwe. It borders Zambia to the northwest, Tanzania to the northeast and Mozambique to the southeast, south and southwest.

paises/mali.resena.t: The Mali Empire was a medieval state of the Mandinka (1235–1546), a people whose heartland was the Manden region, between the present-day cities of Bamako (Mali) and Siguiri (Guinea), in West Africa. The empire was founded by Sundiata Keïta.

paises/malta.resena.t: Malta, officially the Republic of Malta, is one of the twenty-seven sovereign states that make up the European Union. It is one of the most densely populated states, consisting of an archipelago located in the centre of the Mediterranean Sea, south of Italy, east of Tunisia and north of Libya.

paises/mamelucos.resena.t: The Mamluk Sultanate of Egypt, also known as Mamluk Egypt or the Mamluk Empire, was a medieval realm spanning Egypt, the Mediterranean Levant and the Hejaz. It lasted from the fall of the Ayyubid dynasty in 1250 until the Ottoman conquest of Egypt in 1517.

paises/manchukuo.resena.t: Manchuria, a region of northeastern China. After the Mukden Incident (1931), Japan occupied it and in 1932 created the State of Manchukuo, formally independent but under Japanese control, with Puyi as Chief Executive and, from 1934, emperor. It disappeared with the Soviet invasion of 1945.

paises/marruecos.nombres_periodo.1912.no.t: French and Spanish protectorates in Morocco

paises/marruecos.resena.t: Morocco, officially the Kingdom of Morocco, formerly called the Sharifian Empire, is a sovereign country located in the Maghreb.

paises/martinica.resena.t: Martinique is an island with the status of an overseas region and department of France, forming an integral part of the French Republic and of the European Union as an outermost region. As a single territorial collectivity, it has only one assembly, which combines the powers of the regional and departmental councils.

paises/mauritania.resena.t: Mauritania, officially the Islamic Republic of Mauritania, is a country in northwest Africa. It borders the Atlantic Ocean to the west, Senegal to the southwest, Mali to the east and southeast, Algeria to the northeast and the territory of Western Sahara to the north.

paises/mayas.resena.t: The Maya culture was a Mesoamerican civilization that developed mainly in what are now the territories of Guatemala and Mexico, as well as in Belize and the western part of Honduras and El Salvador, covering more than 300,000 km².

paises/media.resena.t: Kingdom of the Medes, in the western Iranian Plateau, with its capital at Ecbatana. Under Cyaxares (624–585 BC) it allied with Babylon to destroy Assyria and reached the Halys River, although the actual extent of its rule is disputed. Cyrus II conquered it in 550 BC.

paises/mercia.resena.t: Anglian kingdom of the Midlands, with its core in the Trent valley. Penda won the Hwicce after Cirencester (628) and Æthelred secured Lindsey at the Battle of the Trent (679). Under Offa (757–796), who built the dyke that bears his name facing Wales, it dominated southern England.

paises/mexico.resena.t: Mexico, officially the United Mexican States, is a sovereign country in the southern part of North America; its capital and most populous city is Mexico City. Under the current constitution, its form of government is a representative, democratic, secular and federal republic, made up of 32 federal entities.

paises/minoicos.resena.t: Bronze Age civilization on Crete (c. 3100–1100 BC). It built palaces such as Knossos, Phaistos and Malia from c. 2100 BC and dominated Aegean trade; around 1450 BC it passed into the hands of a Mycenaean elite.

paises/mitani.resena.t: Hurrian kingdom of Upper Mesopotamia and northern Syria (c. 1550–1260 BC) with its capital at Washukanni, on the upper Khabur. It contested Syria with Egypt and the Hittites, who devastated it around 1345 BC; its eastern remnant, Hanigalbat, fell to Assyria under Shalmaneser I, who annexed it around the mid-13th century BC.

paises/moldavia.resena.t: Moldova, officially the Republic of Moldova, is a country in Eastern Europe, located between Romania and Ukraine. It has an area of 33,851 km² and its capital is Chișinău, located in the center of the country.

paises/mongol.resena.t: The Mongol Empire was the second-largest empire in history and the largest empire made up of contiguous territories. It was founded by Genghis Khan in 1206 and reached its peak when it covered approximately 23,000,000 km².

paises/mongolia.resena.t: Mongolia is a landlocked sovereign state in East Asia. It borders Russia to the north and China to the south.

paises/montenegro.resena.t: Montenegro is a country in southeastern Europe on the Balkan Peninsula, with almost 300 km of coastline on the Adriatic Sea. It borders Bosnia and Herzegovina and Serbia to the north; Albania to the south; Croatia to the west; and Kosovo to the east.

paises/montserrat.resena.t: The island of Montserrat is a British Overseas Territory located southeast of the island of Puerto Rico and northwest of Venezuela, in the waters of the Caribbean Sea.

paises/moscu.resena.t: Russian principality that emerged around 1263 under Daniel, son of Alexander Nevsky. A tributary of the Golden Horde, it gradually gained territory until it united northeastern Russia. Ivan III annexed Novgorod in 1478 and stopped paying tribute after the “Great Stand on the Ugra” (1480).

paises/mozambique.resena.t: Mozambique, officially the Republic of Mozambique, is a country in southeastern Africa, on the shores of the Indian Ocean.

paises/munster.resena.t: Kingdom of southern Ireland (Mumu), dominated from the 7th century by the Eóganachta of Cashel. Faílbe Flann crossed the Shannon and won the future Thomond (Clare) from Connacht.

paises/namibia.resena.t: Namibia, officially the Republic of Namibia, is a country in southwestern Africa. It shares land borders with Angola to the north, Zambia to the northeast, Botswana to the east and South Africa to the southeast and south, and borders the Atlantic Ocean to the west.

paises/navarra.resena.t: The Kingdom of Navarre was the institutional continuation of the Kingdom of Pamplona, one of the medieval kingdoms of Europe, located on both sides of the western Pyrenees but with most of its territory south of the range, in the north of the Iberian Peninsula, from 1162.

paises/nepal.resena.t: Nepal, officially the Federal Democratic Republic of Nepal, is a landlocked country in South Asia. Geographically it lies in the Himalayas, bordered to the north by the People's Republic of China and to the south by India.

paises/nicaragua.resena.t: Nicaragua, officially the Republic of Nicaragua, is a country in Central America. Its capital and most populous city is Managua, although previously they were León and Granada.

paises/niger.resena.t: Niger, officially the Republic of the Niger or Republic of Niger, is a landlocked country in West Africa. It borders Nigeria and Benin to the south, Burkina Faso and Mali to the west, Algeria and Libya to the north, and Chad to the east.

paises/nigeria.resena.t: Nigeria, officially the Federal Republic of Nigeria, is a country in West Africa, bordered by Niger to the north, Chad to the northeast, Cameroon to the east and Benin to the west. Its southern coast lies on the Gulf of Guinea in the Atlantic Ocean.

paises/niue.resena.t: Niue is an island territory in the South Pacific Ocean, known as the Rock of Polynesia. Although self-governing, it maintains a status of free association with New Zealand.

paises/northumbria.resena.t: Anglian kingdom (654–1066) born of the union of Deira and Bernicia. Around 700 it stretched from the Humber and the Mersey to the Forth, including Elmet, Lothian and Rheged. It was the cultural center of Lindisfarne, Jarrow and Bede; the Vikings took York from it in 866–867.

paises/nueva-zelanda.resena.t: New Zealand is a sovereign island country in Oceania, located in the southwestern Pacific Ocean near Australia, and constituted as a parliamentary monarchy. It consists of two large islands, the North Island and the South Island, along with a large number of smaller islands, most notably Stewart Island and the Chatham Islands.

paises/olmecas.resena.t: The first great civilization of Mesoamerica, on the coast of the Gulf of Mexico (c. 1600/1200–400 BC). Its centers were San Lorenzo (c. 1200–900 BC) and La Venta (c. 900–400 BC), known for their colossal heads.

paises/oman.resena.t: Oman, officially the Sultanate of Oman, is a country in western Asia, on the eastern coast of the Arabian Peninsula. It borders the United Arab Emirates (UAE) to the northwest, Saudi Arabia to the west and Yemen to the southwest.

paises/omeya.resena.t: The Umayyad Caliphate, or caliphate of the Umayyads, was the second of the four major caliphates established after the death of Muhammad. The caliphate was ruled by the Umayyad dynasty, an Arab lineage that held the power of caliph, first in the East, with its capital at Damascus, and later in al-Andalus, with its capital at Córdoba.

paises/orden-teutonica.resena.t: State of the German military order in Prussia and Livonia, formed from 1230 at the expense of the pagan Prussians. Its defeat by Poland-Lithuania at Grunwald (1410) began its decline.

paises/ostrogodos.resena.t: The Ostrogothic Kingdom of Italy was a political entity, a barbarian kingdom nominally part of the Roman Empire, founded by the Germanic Ostrogoths, which controlled the territories of the praetorian prefecture of Italy between 493 and 553. Its approximate borders stretched from Provence to Illyria.

paises/otomano.resena.t: The Ottoman Empire, officially the Sublime Ottoman State, was a multiethnic state ruled by the Ottoman dynasty. It was known as the Turkish Empire by its contemporaries, although the Ottoman rulers never used that name to refer to their state.

paises/pagan.resena.t: The first state to unify the Irrawaddy valley (Burma). Anawrahta (1044) turned it into an empire and took Thaton in 1057. After the Mongol invasions it collapsed between 1287 and 1297.

paises/paisesbajos.resena.t: The Netherlands is one of the four constituent countries of the Kingdom of the Netherlands and a member state of the European Union. Its official capital and most populous city is Amsterdam; however, the seat of the government, parliament, monarchy and judiciary is The Hague.

paises/pakistan.resena.t: Pakistan, officially the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, is a sovereign state in Asia located in the Middle East and the Indian subcontinent, bordering Afghanistan to the north and northwest, Iran to the west, India to the east and China to the northeast, while to the south it has some 1,046 km of coastline on the Arabian Sea and the Gulf…

paises/palestina.resena.t: Palestine, officially the State of Palestine, is a country in Asia located in the Near East region, more specifically in the Mediterranean Levant, consisting of the West Bank and the Gaza Strip, with East Jerusalem as its capital.

paises/palmira.resena.t: State of the caravan city of Palmyra, in Syria. Odaenathus defended the Roman East against the Sasanians and recovered Mesopotamia (262–263) as an ally of Gallienus. After his death, his widow Zenobia, regent for her son Vaballathus, occupied Egypt, Arabia and much of Anatolia as far as Ancyra (270–271), and both took the title of Augustus. Aurelian defeated her in 272 and razed Palmyra after a new revolt (273).

paises/panama.resena.t: Panama, officially the Republic of Panama, is a country in Central America. It is divided into ten provinces and six indigenous comarcas.

paises/papua-nueva-guinea.resena.t: Papua New Guinea, officially the Independent State of Papua New Guinea, is a sovereign country in Oceania that occupies the eastern half of the island of New Guinea and numerous surrounding islands. The other half of the island belongs to Indonesia and consists of the region known as Western New Guinea.

paises/paraguay.resena.t: Paraguay, officially the Republic of Paraguay, is a sovereign country in central South America with large expanses of forests, waterfalls and wetlands. It is organized as a unitary state, made up of a capital and seventeen departments. Its capital is Asunción, one of the oldest cities in the Americas.

paises/parto.resena.t: The Parthian Empire, also known as the Arsacid Empire, was one of the major Iranian political and cultural powers of ancient Iran.

paises/pechenegos.resena.t: Confederation of Turkic-speaking nomadic tribes of the Pontic–Caspian steppe. Pushed westward by the Khazars and other steppe peoples at the end of the 9th century, they attacked the Magyars around 895 and occupied Etelköz, between the Dnieper and the Siret. From there they dominated the steppe north of the Black Sea during the 10th century, alternating alliances and wars with Byzantium, Kievan Rus' and Bulgaria; their khan Kurya killed Sviatoslav I of Kiev in 972. The Byzantines and Cumans annihilated them at the Battle of Levounion (1091).

paises/pergamo.resena.t: The Kingdom of Pergamon was an ancient state (241 BC–133 BC.

paises/persia.resena.t: Iran, officially the Islamic Republic of Iran, also known historically in the West as Persia, is a sovereign country in the Near East and Western Asia. It is a theocratic Islamic republic based on the religious principles of Shia Islam.

paises/peru.resena.t: Peru, officially the Republic of Peru, is a sovereign state in western South America. It borders Ecuador and Colombia to the north; Brazil and Bolivia to the east; Chile to the south; and the Pacific Ocean to the west, which borders its 2,250 km of coastline.

paises/pictos.resena.t: Celtic people of Scotland north of the Forth and the Clyde. From the 7th century the kingdom of Fortriu imposed its hegemony; at Dun Nechtain (685) it halted Northumbria. Around the mid-9th century it united with Dál Riata in the kingdom of Alba.

paises/polis-griegas.resena.t: The Greek world of Antiquity. In the Bronze Age, Mycenaean kingdoms with palaces at Mycenae, Pylos or Tiryns (c. 1750–1050 BC); after their collapse, from the 8th century BC, independent city-states (poleis) such as Athens or Sparta, which colonized the Mediterranean and the Black Sea. From Chaeronea (338 BC) they came under the hegemony of Macedon.

paises/polonia.resena.t: Poland, officially the Republic of Poland, is a country in Central Europe, one of the twenty-seven sovereign states that make up the European Union, constituted as a democratic state governed by the rule of law, whose form of government is a parliamentary republic. It is a unitary state with 16 administrative subdivisions or regions called voivodeships.

paises/portugal.resena.t: Portugal, officially the Portuguese Republic, is a sovereign country in southwestern Europe, located on the Iberian Peninsula. It is one of the twenty-seven member states of the European Union.

paises/powys.resena.t: Welsh kingdom of central and eastern Wales, including the plains of the Severn and the Dee. It lost Chester to Æthelfrith of Northumbria (613–616) and its lowlands to Mercia; Offa's Dyke later fixed the border.

paises/prusia.resena.t: Prussia was a Baltic state, located on the North European Plain between Pomerania, Poland and Lithuania, which existed from the end of the Middle Ages, beginning with the secularization in 1525 of the Prussian part of the State of the Teutonic Order.

paises/ptolemaico.resena.t: The Ptolemaic dynasty was founded by Ptolemy I Soter, a general of Alexander the Great. This dynasty ruled Ancient Egypt during the Hellenistic period from 323 BC.

paises/pueblo-godo.resena.t: East Germanic people who, from the lower Vistula, reached the Pontic steppe in the 3rd century. There, together with other peoples, they formed the Chernyakhov culture. The Greuthungi (between the Dniester and the Don) and the Tervingi (west of the Dniester) dispersed with the arrival of the Huns, around 375, and gave rise to the Ostrogoths and Visigoths.

paises/pueblos-germanicos.resena.t: Germanic-speaking peoples without a common state who occupied Germania Magna, between the Rhine, the Danube and the Vistula, and southern Scandinavia: Saxons, Thuringians, Lombards, Burgundians, Vandals or Geats, among others. On the map they are grouped under this label where there is no more precise attribution; borders are approximate.

paises/puerto-rico.resena.t: Puerto Rico, officially the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, is one of the fourteen unincorporated territories and one of the two self-governing commonwealths of the United States of America. With approximately 3.

paises/qin.resena.t: The Qin dynasty was the first imperial dynasty of China, from 221 BC.

paises/rashidun.resena.t: The first caliphate after the death of Muhammad (632–661), ruled by the four caliphs whom Sunni tradition calls “rightly guided”: Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman and Ali. From Medina, and later from Kufa, it unified Arabia in the Ridda wars and in less than twenty years took Syria, Palestine, Egypt and Cyrenaica from Byzantium and put an end to the Sasanian Empire. The civil war that followed the assassination of Uthman ended in 661 with the rise to power of the Umayyads.

paises/rd-congo.resena.t: The Democratic Republic of the Congo is a country in Central Africa, one of the fifty-four countries that make up the African continent. It is the second-largest country in Africa, after Algeria, and the eleventh-largest in the world.

paises/reino-benin.resena.t: Kingdom of the Edo in the south of present-day Nigeria, with its capital at Edo (now Benin City). The obas ruled it from the 12th century; under Ewuare, in the mid-15th century, it went from a city-state to a regional power. It remained independent until a British expedition took the capital in 1897 and looted the palace (the Benin Bronzes). The oba still exists as a traditional monarchy within Nigeria. It has no historical connection with the Republic of Benin, formerly Dahomey.

paises/reino-del-bosforo.resena.t: Greco-Scythian kingdom of the Kerch Strait, with its capital at Panticapaeum, founded in 438 BC and a client of Rome from the 1st century BC. Traditional historiography considers it to have disappeared around 375–376, with the arrival of the Huns, but an inscription from around 483 indicates that it survived until the Byzantine conquest of 527.

paises/reino-jerusalen.resena.t: The principal Crusader state, founded after the capture of Jerusalem in 1099. It lost the city after Hattin (1187), was re-established on the coast with its capital at Acre (1191) and disappeared with the fall of Acre in 1291.

paises/reino-odoacro.resena.t: Rule over Italy of the Herulian chieftain Odoacer, who deposed Romulus Augustulus on 4 September 476 and sent the imperial insignia to Constantinople, recognizing the Eastern emperor. He obtained Sicily from the Vandals (476) and Dalmatia after the death of Julius Nepos (480). Theodoric and the Ostrogoths defeated and killed him in Ravenna (493).

paises/rep-congo.resena.t: The Congo, officially the Republic of the Congo, also known as Congo-Brazzaville or simply West Congo, is a country in Central Africa.

paises/republica-centroafricana.resena.t: The Central African Republic, or simply Central Africa, is a landlocked country in Central Africa. It borders Chad to the north, Sudan to the northeast, South Sudan to the east, the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the Republic of the Congo to the south and Cameroon to the west.

paises/republica-checa.resena.t: The Czech Republic, also known as Czechia, is a landlocked sovereign country in Central Europe. It borders Germany to the west, Austria to the south, Slovakia to the east and Poland to the north.

paises/republica-dominicana.resena.t: The Dominican Republic is a country in the Americas located in the Caribbean, in the central area of the Antilles; it occupies the central and eastern part of the island of Hispaniola. Its capital and most populous city is Santo Domingo.

paises/republica-turca-del-norte-de-chip.t: Northern Cyprus, officially the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus, is a state with limited recognition that controls the northern third of the island of Cyprus, in the eastern Mediterranean. Its capital is North Nicosia (Lefkoşa).

paises/rheged.resena.t: Brittonic kingdom of the Hen Ogledd, in Cumbria and Dumfries and Galloway, perhaps with lands in Lancashire and Yorkshire. Associated with King Urien, it passed to Northumbria before 730, perhaps through the marriage of Oswiu to Princess Rieinmelth.

paises/roma.resena.t: State of Antiquity born in the city of Rome which, as a republic and from 27 BC as an empire, came to dominate the entire Mediterranean. On the 1 BC map it includes Germania between the Rhine and the Elbe, the province that Augustus tried to organize (7 BC–AD 9) and that was abandoned after the defeat at Teutoburg; from the AD 14 map the border returns to the Rhine.

paises/romaoccidente.resena.t: The Western Roman Empire was a political entity of Antiquity that existed between 286 and 476. It covered the western area of Europe—west of the Rhine and Drina rivers—, much of Great Britain and the Mediterranean strip of Africa, north of the Sahara Desert as far as Libya.

paises/rpchina.resena.t: The People's Republic of China, commonly known as China, is a sovereign country in East Asia with its capital at Beijing. It is the second most populous country in the world.

paises/ruanda.resena.t: Rwanda, officially the Republic of Rwanda, is a landlocked country in East Africa, Central Africa or east-central Africa. It borders Uganda to the north, Tanzania to the east, Burundi to the south and the Democratic Republic of the Congo to the west.

paises/rum.resena.t: Seljuk sultanate of Anatolia (1077–1308), with its capital at Konya from 1097. After the defeat at Köse Dağ (1243) it became a vassal of the Mongols and dissolved into beyliks, among them the Ottoman one.

paises/rumania.resena.t: Romania is one of the twenty-seven sovereign states that make up the European Union. It is located at the intersection of Eastern and Southeastern Europe and has a coastline on the Black Sea to the southeast.

paises/rus.resena.t: Kievan Rus' was a federation of East Slavic tribes from the late 9th century to the mid-13th century, ruled by the Rurik dynasty.

paises/rusia.resena.t: Russia, formally known as the Russian Federation, is a Eurasian country spanning Eastern Europe and Northern Asia. It is the largest country in the world, with an area of 17,125,191 km², equivalent to slightly more than one-ninth of the planet's land area, and has a great variety of landforms and ecosystems.

paises/sacroimperio.resena.t: The Holy Roman Empire, sometimes called the Old Empire to distinguish it from the German Empire of 1871–1918, was a political grouping located in Western and Central Europe, whose power rested with the Holy Roman Emperor from the Middle Ages until the beginning of the Late Modern period.

paises/safavida.resena.t: The Safavid Empire, or Safawi Empire, is considered the greatest Iranian empire since the Muslim conquest of Persia. The Safavids originated in Ardabil, a city in Iranian Azerbaijan, in northern Iran.

paises/sahara-occidental.nombres_periodo.t: Moroccan administration (de facto, most of the territory)

paises/sahara-occidental.resena.t: Western Sahara is a region of North Africa located at the western end of the Sahara Desert, on the shores of the Atlantic Ocean. It is one of the seventeen non-self-governing territories under the supervision of the United Nations Special Committee on Decolonization, with the aim of ending colonialism.

paises/sajones.resena.t: Confederation of West Germanic tribes of the North Sea coast. In Old Saxony (Westphalia, Angria, Eastphalia and Nordalbingia, between the Rhine and the Elbe) they resisted the Franks until Charlemagne's Saxon Wars (772–804). Some of them moved to Britain in the 5th and 6th centuries.

paises/samoa-americana.resena.t: American Samoa is one of the fourteen unincorporated territories of the United States. It is one of the 17 non-self-governing territories under the supervision of the United Nations Special Committee on Decolonization.

paises/samoa.resena.t: Samoa, officially the Independent State of Samoa, is a sovereign island country in Oceania, part of Polynesia. Its capital and most populous city is Apia, on the island of Upolu.

paises/san-cristobal-y-nieves.resena.t: Saint Kitts and Nevis, officially the Federation of Saint Christopher and Nevis, is an island country in the northern Antilles, specifically in the Leeward Islands, taking its name precisely from this pair of islands.

paises/san-martin.resena.t: Saint Martin may refer to several articles:

paises/san-vicente-y-las-granadinas.rese.t: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines is an island country in the Americas, located in the Lesser Antilles chain in the eastern Caribbean Sea, bordered to the north by Saint Lucia, to the east by Barbados, to the south and west by Venezuela and to the south by Grenada.

paises/santa-lucia.resena.t: Saint Lucia is an island country in the Americas, located in the Caribbean Sea, north of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines and south of the island of Martinique. It covers a land area of 617 km² with an estimated population of 183,629 in 2020.

paises/sarmatas.resena.t: Iranian-speaking nomadic peoples related to the Scythians, who dominated the Pontic steppe until the Goths conquered it around the year 200. One branch, the Iazyges, lived between the Danube and the Tisza until the 5th century.

paises/sasanida.resena.t: The Sasanian Empire, or Empire of the Iranians, also known as the Second Persian Empire or Neo-Persian Empire, was the second Persian empire and the fourth and last Iranian state before the Muslim conquest of the 7th and 8th centuries.

paises/segundo-bulgaro.resena.t: Bulgarian state restored in 1185 by the revolt of the brothers Asen and Peter against Byzantium, with its capital at Tarnovo. It dominated the Balkans under Ivan Asen II and fell to the Ottomans (Tarnovo 1393, Vidin 1396).

paises/seleucida.resena.t: The Seleucid Empire (312–63 BC), also called the Hellenistic Empire of Asia and, in its final decades, by the Romans the Seleucid Kingdom of Syria, was a Hellenistic empire in western Asia.

paises/selyucida.resena.t: Sunni Turkish empire founded by Tughril Beg in 1037. It took Baghdad in 1055, defeated Byzantium at Manzikert (1071) and by around 1080 ruled from Anatolia to the Hindu Kush. It fragmented in the 12th century and its last sultan fell to Khwarazm in 1194.

paises/senegal.resena.t: Senegal, officially the Republic of Senegal, is a sovereign state in West Africa whose form of government is a semi-presidential republic. Its territory is organized into fourteen regions.

paises/senorio-irlanda.resena.t: Dominion of the kings of England in Ireland from the Norman invasion (1169–1171) and the granting of the title of Lord of Ireland to John Lackland (1177) until Henry VIII proclaimed himself King of Ireland in 1542. It claimed the whole island, but after the Gaelic resurgence following 1350, effective royal power had shrunk by the end of the 15th century to the Pale: the “four obedient shires” of Dublin, Meath, Louth and Kildare, defended by a ditch from 1494–1495, plus some towns such as Cork, Limerick, Waterford and Wexford. The map marks only the Pale; the rest of the island appears as Gaelic Ireland.

paises/serbia.resena.t: Serbia, officially the Republic of Serbia (), is a sovereign country, constituted as a social and democratic state governed by the rule of law, whose form of government is a parliamentary republic.

paises/shang.resena.t: Dynasty that ruled the central plain of the Yellow River between c. 1600 and 1046 BC. It is the first in the Chinese tradition confirmed by archaeology: its last capital, Yinxu (Anyang), has yielded the oracle bones, the oldest known Chinese writing, and large ritual bronzes. It fell to the Zhou at the Battle of Muye.

paises/sicilia.resena.t: Norman kingdom founded by Roger II in 1130 over Sicily and southern Italy. After the Sicilian Vespers (1282) the island passed to the House of Barcelona and the mainland formed the Kingdom of Naples.

paises/sierra-leona.resena.t: Sierra Leone, officially the Republic of Sierra Leone, is a country in West Africa. It borders Guinea to the north, Liberia to the southeast and the Atlantic Ocean to the southwest, which separates it from Brazil by some 2,840 km.

paises/siria.resena.t: Syria, officially the Syrian Arab Republic, is a sovereign country in the Near East, washed by the Levantine Mediterranean coast. It shares borders with Turkey to the north, Iraq to the east, Israel and Jordan to the south, and Lebanon and the Mediterranean Sea to the west; from its coast the island of Cyprus can be seen in the distance.

paises/soissons.resena.t: Gallo-Roman territory in northern Gaul, around Soissons, that remained in the hands of Roman commanders after imperial power in the West broke down: Aegidius, magister militum of Majorian, and his son Syagrius, whom Gregory of Tours calls “King of the Romans”. Clovis defeated him at the Battle of Soissons (486) and annexed it to the Frankish kingdom.

paises/somalia.resena.t: Somalia, officially the Federal Republic of Somalia, is a country in the Horn of Africa, in the east of the African continent. It borders Ethiopia and Djibouti to the west and northwest, Kenya to the south, the Gulf of Aden to the north and the Indian Ocean to the east.

paises/songhai.resena.t: The Songhai Empire, also known as the Songhay Empire, was a state located in West Africa. From the beginning of the 15th century until the end of the 16th century, Songhai was one of the largest Islamic empires in history.

paises/sri-lanka.resena.t: Sri Lanka, officially the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka, is a sovereign island country in South Asia whose form of government is a semi-presidential republic. Its territory is organised into nine provinces and twenty-four districts.

paises/srivijaya.resena.t: Buddhist thalassocracy centred on Palembang (Sumatra) that dominated the Strait of Malacca and the Sunda Strait between the 7th and 13th centuries. Its last successor state fell to Majapahit in 1377.

paises/strathclyde.resena.t: Brittonic kingdom of the Clyde valley, ruled from Dumbarton Rock (Alt Clut), stretching from north of Loch Lomond to the coast of Ayr. The last kingdom of the Hen Ogledd, it remained independent until the 11th century.

paises/sudafrica.nombres_periodo.1806.no.t: Cape Colony / British colonies and Boer republics

paises/sudafrica.resena.t: South Africa, officially the Republic of South Africa, is a sovereign country located in Southern Africa whose form of government is a parliamentary republic. Its territory is organised into nine provinces.

paises/sudan-del-sur.resena.t: South Sudan is a landlocked country in East Africa. It became independent from Sudan on 9 July 2011, following the referendum held in January of that year, and is the world's youngest recognised state.

paises/sudan.resena.t: Sudan, officially the Republic of the Sudan, is one of the fifty-five countries that make up the African continent. Its capital is Khartoum and its most populous city is Omdurman.

paises/suecia.resena.t: Sweden, officially the Kingdom of Sweden, is a Scandinavian country in Northern Europe, constituted as a social and democratic state with a parliamentary monarchy as its system of government. It is one of the twenty-seven sovereign states that make up the European Union.

paises/sui.resena.t: The Sui dynasty followed the Northern and Southern Dynasties and preceded the Tang dynasty in China. It lasted 37 years and ended nearly four centuries of rule divided among self-proclaimed dynasties in both the north and the south.

paises/suiza.resena.t: Switzerland, officially the Swiss Confederation, is a landlocked country located in Central Europe with a population of 9,048,905 (2024). Switzerland is a federal state with 26 cantons and four official languages: German, French, Italian and Romansh.

paises/surinam.resena.t: Suriname, officially the Republic of Suriname, formerly known as Dutch Guiana, is a country located in northern South America and the Caribbean, bordered by the Atlantic Ocean to the north, the French overseas department of French Guiana to the east, Guyana to the west and Brazil to the south.

paises/sussex.resena.t: Kingdom of the South Saxons, on the coast between the Weald and the English Channel. Of little political weight, it fell into the orbit of Mercia and later of Wessex, which absorbed it in the 9th century.

paises/taifalos.resena.t: People allied with the Tervingi from 291, settled in Oltenia, west of the Olt. Their cavalry fought against Constantine II in 332. They crossed the Danube in 377 and were defeated that same year. Rome settled the vanquished as colonists in northern Italy and in Aquitaine, where the Poitou region came to be called Thifalia.

paises/tailandia.resena.t: Thailand, officially the Kingdom of Thailand, is a country located in Southeast Asia. Its capital and most populous city is Bangkok, the centre of political, commercial and industrial activity.

paises/taiwan.resena.t: The Republic of China is a sovereign country located in East Asia. Its official name has been tied to limited recognition since 1949, as it is located mainly on the archipelago of Taiwan, the name by which it is popularly known.

paises/tanzania.resena.t: Tanzania, officially the United Republic of Tanzania, is a country located on the eastern coast of Central Africa.

paises/tayikistan.resena.t: Tajikistan, officially the Republic of Tajikistan, is a sovereign landlocked country located in Central Asia. It has an estimated population of 10 million and an area of 144,100 km².

paises/teotihuacan.resena.t: Teotihuacan or Teotihuacán, which according to new research may also have been known as Teohuacan, is the name given to the great archaeological complex that was one of the largest in Mesoamerica during the Classic period.

paises/tervingios.resena.t: Branch of the Goths that occupied the plains north of the lower Danube and west of the Dniester, in the former Dacia abandoned by Rome, from the late 3rd century. It is first mentioned around 291. It signed a treaty with Constantine in 332 and fought against Valens in 367–369. In 376, pushed by the Huns, it crossed the Danube under Fritigern and gave rise to the Visigoths.

paises/tibet-imperial.resena.t: Empire of the Tibetan Plateau unified around 618 (Songtsen Gampo). It contested the Tarim Basin and Gansu with the Tang in the 7th–9th centuries. It collapsed after the assassination of Langdarma in 842, beginning the so-called Era of Fragmentation.

paises/tibet.resena.t: Between 1913 and 1950 the Dalai Lama's government in Lhasa acted independently, without recognition from the Republic of China, which considered it part of its territory; in 1950–1951 it was incorporated into the People's Republic of China.

paises/timurida.resena.t: The Timurid Empire, self-designated as the Gurkani State (گورکانیان) or Turan Empire, was an empire founded by Timur (Tamerlane), a warlord and conqueror of Turco-Mongol lineage, who established it between 1370 and his death in 1405.

paises/togo.resena.t: Togo is a country in West Africa. It borders Ghana to the west, Benin to the east and Burkina Faso to the north.

paises/tonga.resena.t: Tonga, officially the Kingdom of Tonga, is a sovereign island country located in Oceania, part of Polynesia, and constituted as a parliamentary monarchy.

paises/transilvania.resena.t: State born in 1570, when John Sigismund Zápolya renounced the title of King of Hungary in the Treaty of Speyer and remained Prince of Transylvania and of the Partium. Its princes were elected by its Diet and it was a vassal and tributary of the Ottoman sultan, although it also negotiated with the Habsburgs. It enjoyed its golden age under Gabriel Bethlen and the Rákóczis; after losing Várad in 1660 it went into decline, and from the Peace of Karlowitz (1699) it came under the Habsburgs, who abolished the principality in 1711.

paises/trinidad-y-tobago.resena.t: Trinidad and Tobago, officially the Republic of Trinidad and Tobago, is a sovereign island country located in the Caribbean Sea, in the northern region of South America.

paises/tunez.resena.t: Tunisia, officially the Republic of Tunisia or Tunisian Republic, is a sovereign country located in North Africa, more specifically on the Mediterranean coast. Its territory is organised into 24 governorates or wilayat.

paises/turkmenistan.resena.t: Turkmenistan, officially the Republic of Turkmenistan, is a country located in Central Asia bordering Kazakhstan to the northwest, Uzbekistan to the north and northeast, Iran to the southwest, Afghanistan to the southeast and the Caspian Sea to the west, although it is considered a landlocked state.

paises/turquia.resena.t: Turkey, formally the Republic of Türkiye, is a transcontinental country, with most of its territory located in Western Asia and a smaller part in Eastern Europe, extending across the whole Anatolian peninsula, the centre of the Armenian Highlands and, in East Thrace, the Balkans.

paises/ucrania.resena.t: Ukraine is a sovereign state located in Eastern Europe. Its form of state is a republic governed by a semi-presidential system, with separation of the executive, legislative and judicial powers.

paises/uganda.resena.t: Uganda, officially the Republic of Uganda, is a sovereign landlocked country located in East Africa. The country borders Kenya to the east, South Sudan to the north, the Democratic Republic of the Congo to the west, Rwanda to the south and Tanzania to the southwest.

paises/ui-neill.resena.t: Lineages descended from Niall of the Nine Hostages that dominated northern and central Ireland: the northern branches (Cenél Conaill, Cenél nEógain) and the southern ones (Mide, Brega), with the Airgíalla as tributaries. They monopolised the title of High King of Tara.

paises/ulaid.resena.t: Kingdom of northeastern Ireland which in historical times was reduced to the lands east of the Bann (Antrim and Down). Its throne was contested between the Dál Fiatach of Downpatrick and the Dál nAraidi.

paises/urartu.resena.t: Kingdom of the Armenian Highlands around Lake Van, formed around 860 BC (Arame). A rival of Assyria in the 9th–7th centuries BC, it fell to the Medes around 590 BC (according to other authors, in the mid-6th century).

paises/uruguay.resena.t: Uruguay, officially the Oriental Republic of Uruguay, is a sovereign country in South America, located in the eastern part of the Southern Cone. Its capital and most populous city is Montevideo.

paises/uzbekistan.resena.t: Uzbekistan, officially the Republic of Uzbekistan, is a landlocked country located in Central Asia. It borders Kazakhstan to the northwest and north, Afghanistan to the south, Kyrgyzstan to the northeast, Tajikistan to the southeast and Turkmenistan to the southwest.

paises/valaquia.resena.t: Romanian principality between the Southern Carpathians and the Danube, with its capital at Târgoviște and later at Bucharest. From 1417 it paid tribute to the sultan and was a vassal of the Ottoman Empire, but it kept its own voivodes, nobility and laws; only a few Danube strongholds (Turnu, Giurgiu and, from the mid-16th century, Brăila) were Ottoman. Michael the Brave united it for a few months in 1600 with Transylvania and Moldavia. In 1859 it united with Moldavia in the United Principalities, the origin of Romania.

paises/vandalos.nombres_periodo.439.nomb.t: Kingdom of the Vandals and Alans

paises/vandalos.resena.t: Kingdom founded by Genseric, who in 429 crossed with the Vandals and Alans from Hispania to Africa, took Carthage in 439 and obtained imperial recognition in 442. With its fleet it dominated the western Mediterranean (the Balearic Islands, Corsica, Sardinia, Sicily) and sacked Rome in 455. Justinian conquered it in 533–534, through Belisarius, after defeating Gelimer.

paises/venecia.resena.t: The Republic of Venice, officially the Most Serene Republic of Venice and popularly known as La Serenissima, was a city-state located in northern Italy, on the shores of the Adriatic Sea, which later brought under its rule all the Venetians of the Triveneto, Istria and Dalmatia. Its capital was the city of Venice.

paises/venezuela.resena.t: Venezuela, officially the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela, is a sovereign country in the Americas, located at the northern end of South America and in the Caribbean region. It consists of a continental territory and numerous islands, islets, cays and archipelagos in the Caribbean Sea.

paises/vietnam.resena.t: Vietnam, officially the Socialist Republic of Vietnam, is a sovereign country in Southeast Asia and the easternmost on the Indochinese Peninsula. With an estimated population of just over one hundred million, it is the sixteenth most populous country in the world, the eighth in Asia and the most populous of the five countries that make up Indochina.

paises/vijayanagara.resena.t: Hindu empire of southern India founded in 1336 by the brothers Harihara and Bukka, with its capital at Vijayanagara (Hampi). A rival of the Deccan sultanates, it was defeated at Talikota in 1565.
