paises/vikingos.resena.t: The Viking Age is the name given to the historical period in Scandinavia and its sphere of influence in Europe, following the Germanic Iron Age, between 793 and 1066, during which the Vikings—Scandinavian warriors and traders—raided and explored most of Europe, southwestern Asia, Africa and northeastern North America.

paises/visigodos.resena.t: The Visigothic Kingdom was a polity established by the Visigothic people after their settlement in part of present-day France and the Iberian Peninsula, during the era of the Germanic invasions, which lasted for much of the Early Middle Ages, occupying territories in Gaul and Hispania in its various stages.

paises/wallis-y-futuna.resena.t: Wallis and Futuna is a group of three tropical islands of volcanic origin located in the South Pacific Ocean, between Fiji and Samoa, constituted as a French overseas collectivity. Between 1961 and 2003 it had the status of an overseas territory.

paises/wessex.resena.t: Kingdom of the West Saxons, in southern England (c. 519–927). It expanded westward at the expense of Dumnonia (Cirencester, Gloucester and Bath in 577; the Parrett in 658; the defeat of Geraint in 710). Ine issued the first law code, and its kings, from Egbert to Alfred and Æthelstan, unified England.

paises/xia-occidental.resena.t: The Tangut Empire, also known by the Chinese name of Western Xia Empire or Xi Xia Empire, was a state that existed between 982 and 1227 in the northwest of the present-day territory of the People's Republic of China.

paises/xia.resena.t: First dynasty of traditional Chinese historiography (c. 2070–1600 BC according to the official chronology). Its historical existence is debated: there are no contemporary texts, and many archaeologists identify it with the Erlitou culture, an identification others do not accept.

paises/xiongnu.resena.t: Confederation of nomadic peoples of the Mongolian steppe, united by the chanyu Modu in 209 BC. It was the great rival of Han China: it imposed tribute on it after the siege of Pingcheng (200 BC), until the campaigns of Emperor Wu forced it back. In AD 48 it split into the Northern and Southern Xiongnu; the Northern Xiongnu dispersed after their defeats of 89–91 and the Southern Xiongnu settled within China's borders.

paises/yemen.resena.t: Yemen, officially the Republic of Yemen, is a bicontinental country located in the Asian Near East, sharing borders with Oman and Saudi Arabia.

paises/yibuti.nombres_periodo.1967.nombr.t: French Territory of the Afars and the Issas

paises/yibuti.resena.t: Djibouti, officially the Republic of Djibouti, is a country located in the Horn of Africa. It covers 23,200 km² and borders Eritrea to the north, Ethiopia to the west and south, and Somalia to the southeast.

paises/yuan.resena.t: Mongol dynasty proclaimed by Kublai Khan in 1271, with its capital at Khanbaliq (Beijing). After defeating the Southern Song at Yamen (1279) it ruled all of China, Mongolia and Korea as a vassal. The Red Turban Rebellion brought it to an end in 1368.

paises/yugoslavia.nombres_periodo.1918.n.t: Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes

paises/zagwe.resena.t: Dynasty that ruled the Ethiopian highlands between c. 1137 (according to other authors, c. 930) and 1270. Its king Lalibela had the rock-hewn monolithic churches that bear his name carved out.

paises/zambia.resena.t: Zambia, officially the Republic of Zambia, is a landlocked country located in south-central Africa. It borders the Democratic Republic of the Congo to the north, Tanzania to the northeast, Malawi and Mozambique to the east, Zimbabwe and Botswana to the south, Namibia to the southwest and Angola to the west.

paises/zhou.resena.t: The Zhou dynasty was a Chinese dynasty that ruled between 1046 and 256 BC.

paises/zimbabue-pais.resena.t: Zimbabwe, officially the Republic of Zimbabwe, is a landlocked country located in southeastern Africa, between the Zambezi River, Victoria Falls and the Limpopo River. It borders Botswana to the west, Zambia to the north, South Africa to the south and Mozambique to the east.

paises/zimbabue.resena.t: Great Zimbabwe is the name given to the remains of an ancient city of the Kingdom of Zimbabwe located on the plateau overlooking the upper course of the Sabi River, in present-day Zimbabwe. It consisted of a city on the upper part and a vast stone enclosure on the lower part.

territorios/atenas.descripcion.t: A polis of Attica and the cradle of democracy: the reforms of Cleisthenes (508 BC), the Age of Pericles (461–429 BC) and the Delian League. Sparta's rival in the Peloponnesian War.

territorios/azores.descripcion.t: Uninhabited until their Portuguese settlement, begun in 1439 (discovered around 1427). Portuguese ever since, today an autonomous region.

territorios/bermudas.descripcion.t: Colonized by England after the wreck of the Sea Venture (1609); St. George's, settled in 1612, was its first capital. Today a British Overseas Territory.

territorios/ceuta-portuguesa.descripcion.t: Conquered by John I of Portugal in 1415, it was the first European stronghold in Africa.

territorios/ceuta.descripcion.t: Under Spanish sovereignty since the union of crowns of 1580. In 1640 the city chose to remain with Philip IV rather than join the Portuguese Restoration, and the Treaty of Lisbon (1668) recognized it as Spanish.

territorios/cisjordania-2.descripcion.t: After the 1948 war, the west bank of the Jordan, including East Jerusalem, came under Jordanian control; Jordan formally annexed it in 1950. The base maps show it as part of Israel: this polygon marks its approximate extent according to the 1949 armistice lines.

territorios/cisjordania-2.estatus.t: Occupied by Transjordan in 1948 and annexed by Jordan in 1950 (an annexation recognized by very few countries)

territorios/cisjordania-3.descripcion.t: Israel occupied the West Bank in the Six-Day War (1967). Since then Israeli settlements have been established, considered illegal by most of the international community. In 1988 the PLO proclaimed the State of Palestine. Approximate extent according to the 1949 lines.

territorios/cisjordania-3.estatus.t: Israeli military occupation since 1967; for the United Nations, Occupied Palestinian Territory. East Jerusalem, de facto annexed by Israel (1967; 1980 law), without international recognition

territorios/cisjordania-4.descripcion.t: The Oslo Accords divided the West Bank into Areas A (Palestinian administration), B (Palestinian civil control, Israeli security control) and C (Israeli control, ~60% of the territory). The UN admitted the State of Palestine as a non-member observer state in 2012. Approximate extent according to the 1949 lines; the areas and settlements are not drawn.

territorios/cisjordania-4.estatus.t: Palestinian National Authority in Areas A and B (Oslo Accords, 1993–1995); Israel retains control of Area C and of security; State of Palestine, UN observer since 2012

territorios/cisjordania.descripcion.t: Until the British withdrawal and the proclamation of Israel (May 1948), the whole territory was the British Mandate of Palestine; the 1945 base map already labels it “Israel”. This polygon marks the approximate extent of the West Bank according to the 1949 armistice lines, to provide continuity with the following periods.

territorios/corinto.descripcion.t: A wealthy commercial polis on the isthmus, a colonial and naval power. A leading member of the Peloponnesian League; razed by Rome in 146 BC.

territorios/dinastia-shang.descripcion.t: The first documented Chinese dynasty; final capital at Yin (Anyang). Founded by Cheng Tang; its ritual bronzes and oracle bones are the earliest examples of Chinese writing. The last king, Di Xin, falls to the Zhou at Muye (1046 BC).

territorios/dinastia-xin.descripcion.t: A brief dynasty of the usurper Wang Mang, which interrupts the Han dynasty between the Western and the Eastern Han with an ambitious reform programme.

territorios/esparta.descripcion.t: A military polis of Laconia, governed by the constitution of Lycurgus. Leonidas falls at Thermopylae (480 BC); after defeating Athens (404 BC) it holds hegemony over Greece until its defeat at Leuctra (371 BC).

territorios/franja-de-gaza-2.descripcion.t: After the 1948 Arab–Israeli War and the 1949 armistices, the Gaza Strip came under Egyptian military administration, without being annexed. It took in a large part of the displaced Palestinian population. The base maps do not distinguish the Strip from Israel: this polygon marks its approximate extent.

territorios/franja-de-gaza-3.descripcion.t: Israel occupied the Strip in June 1967 and administered it militarily. In 1988 the PLO proclaimed the State of Palestine over Gaza and the West Bank. The base maps do not distinguish the Strip from Israel: this polygon marks its approximate extent.

territorios/franja-de-gaza-3.estatus.t: Israeli military occupation since the Six-Day War (1967); for the United Nations, Occupied Palestinian Territory

territorios/franja-de-gaza-4.descripcion.t: The Gaza–Jericho Agreement (1994) transferred civil administration to the Palestinian National Authority. Israel withdrew settlers and troops in 2005 but retains control of the borders, airspace and waters; Hamas has governed since 2007. Scene of successive wars (2008–09, 2012, 2014, since 2023). The base maps do not distinguish the Strip from Israel: this polygon marks its approximate extent.

territorios/franja-de-gaza-4.estatus.t: Palestinian National Authority (Oslo Accords, 1994); Israeli withdrawal in 2005; Hamas government since 2007; State of Palestine, UN observer since 2012

territorios/franja-de-gaza.descripcion.t: Until the British withdrawal and the proclamation of Israel (May 1948), the whole territory was the British Mandate of Palestine; the 1945 base map already labels it “Israel”. This polygon marks the approximate extent of the Strip according to the 1949 armistice lines, to provide continuity with the following periods.

territorios/gibraltar-castellano.descrip.t: Reconquered in 1462 by the troops of the Duke of Medina Sidonia; Castilian and Spanish for 242 years.

territorios/gibraltar.descripcion.t: Taken by the Anglo-Dutch fleet in 1704, during the War of the Spanish Succession, and ceded to Great Britain by the Treaty of Utrecht (1713). Spain claims its return.

territorios/hong-kong-britanico.descripc.t: Occupied in 1841 and ceded by the Treaty of Nanking (1842); the New Territories were leased for 99 years in 1898. In 1997 the entire colony was handed back to China.

territorios/imperio-acadio.descripcion.t: The first empire in history: Sargon of Akkad (c. 2340 BC) unifies Mesopotamia from his capital Agade, near Kish. His grandson Naram-Sin (2260–2223 BC) brings it to its greatest extent and proclaims himself a god.

territorios/isla-de-man.descripcion.t: Norwegian until the Treaty of Perth (1266) and under English feudal lordship from 1399; the British Crown bought the lordship in 1765 (Revestment Act). It is a Crown dependency, not part of the United Kingdom.

territorios/islas-baleares.descripcion.t: James I of Aragon conquered Majorca in 1229–1231; Ibiza (1235) and Minorca (1287) completed their incorporation into the Crown of Aragon and, with it, into Spain.

territorios/islas-canarias.descripcion.t: Conquered for the Crown of Castile between 1402 (Jean de Béthencourt's landing on Lanzarote) and 1496 (surrender of Tenerife). Since then, part of Castile and of Spain.

territorios/islas-chafarinas.descripcion.t: Occupied on 6 January 1848 by General Serrano's expedition, forestalling France.

territorios/islas-del-canal.descripcion.t: Remnants of the Duchy of Normandy: when the English Crown lost continental Normandy (1204), they remained as Crown dependencies, never integrated into the kingdom.

territorios/islas-malvinas-falkland.desc.t: Administered by the United Kingdom since January 1833. Argentina claims them as heir to Spanish sovereignty and briefly occupied them in 1982.

territorios/madeira.descripcion.t: Rediscovered by Portuguese navigators in 1418–1419 and colonized from 1425 on the initiative of John I and Prince Henry the Navigator.

territorios/malta-britanica.descripcion.t: Held by the Order of St John from 1530 (a grant by Charles I of Spain) and occupied by Napoleon in 1798, it passed to British control in 1800; the Treaty of Paris (1814) made it a colony. Independent since 1964.

territorios/melilla.descripcion.t: Taken in 1497 by Pedro de Estopiñán, on an expedition of the Duke of Medina Sidonia, and incorporated into the Crown of Castile.

territorios/menorca-britanica.descripcio.t: Taken by the British in 1708 and ceded at Utrecht (1713). France occupied it in 1756–1763 and Spain in 1782–1798; the Treaty of Amiens (1802) returned it definitively to Spain.

territorios/penon-de-alhucemas.descripci.t: Occupied by Spain in 1673, during the reign of Charles II. One of the plazas de soberanía (places of sovereignty) in North Africa.

territorios/penon-de-velez-de-la-gomera..t: Conquered by Pedro Navarro in 1508, lost in 1522 and definitively recovered by García Álvarez de Toledo in 1564. Spanish without interruption ever since.
Peñón de Vélez de la Gomera

territorios/sumeria.descripcion.t: The first urban civilization, in Lower Mesopotamia. A dozen city-states (Uruk, Ur, Lagash, Kish); the cradle of cuneiform writing and the wheel. Kings: Enmebaragesi of Kish (the earliest documented), Ur-Nammu (Third Dynasty of Ur, c. 2111 BC), Gudea of Lagash.

territorios/tebas.descripcion.t: Capital of Boeotia. Under Epaminondas it breaks Spartan hegemony at Leuctra (371 BC) and holds power in Greece until Mantinea (362 BC).
